articles.title: 3zPz
articles.summary: Leader of the guild Historical [UEZ]. He took it out of Concordia into Ordo Malleus, posted the thread that declared Concordia disbanded in November 2015, and a month later founded Vesta from what remained.

articles.title: 99loulou999
articles.summary: Member of The Dark Phoenix [TNI] who wrote the earliest surviving use of the alliance name Goose, on 19 January 2021, and gave the fullest first-hand account of the Rays desert war a month later.

infobox.label: Known for
infobox.value: First written use of the name [[goose|Goose]] (19 Jan 2021)

articles.body:
On 19 January 2021, 99loulou999 asked [[the-forum-megalist|the megalist]] for an update: "TNR (TNI and TNA) are part of Goose, idk if we already have an editor tho"{{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #71, 19 Jan 2021}}. It is the earliest recorded use of the name [[goose|Goose]] anywhere in the written record — the anti-[[artemis|Artemis]] coalition had been described a month earlier as "a currently unnamed group"{{cite:thread-279337|post #1, 18 Dec 2020}}. Lev98bug of Eden added his guild the same morning{{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #72, 19 Jan 2021}}, and Sg_Voltage answered both: "Just want to drop in and say that I'm a huge fan of the name."{{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #73, 19 Jan 2021}}

A month later, on 20 February 2021, he wrote the longest surviving account of the multi-guild raid on Rays' desert holdings, in the thread "The Issue With 1.20 Guild Wars"{{cite:thread-286375|post #2, 20 Feb 2021}}. Against the claim that attack prices were broken, he replied that the poster was "overshadowing the fact that every guild in artemis except probably 4 were warring the whole desert/savanah/rymek area currently held by Rays, so its normal that after 5h of constant warring the 'pity price'... rose up"{{cite:thread-286375|post #2, 20 Feb 2021}}. On the defenders' position: "Rays HQ kept getting taken because they couldn't war againts 10+ guilds"{{cite:thread-286375|post #2, 20 Feb 2021}}. On his own guild's logistics: "Speaking from experience in TNI during the Rays raid: our smallest attack timer without counting the 10 minutes cooldown was 8 minutes" — the best in the alliance, since no other headquarters sat closer to the desert{{cite:thread-286375|post #2, 20 Feb 2021}}. He classed "TNI and CXZ" as "two guilds I would consider medium sized"{{cite:thread-286375|post #2, 20 Feb 2021}}.

articles.title: Adonis
articles.summary: Adonis was a community alliance founded around May 2022 by the leaders of Titans Valor and Empire of Sindria as Hestia declined — 'a space for those of us who are still active to hang together.' Joined by Avicia within weeks, it outlived the war alliances around it, still hosting community events in early 2024.
articles.body:
## History
Adonis was founded in May 2022 as the successor to the declining Hestia{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol1|vol. 1, 8 May 2022}}; [[Avicia]] had joined by 12 June 2022{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol3|vol. 3, 12 Jun 2022}}. The alliance ran community events through the era of [[Cucumber Company]], [[smtn elf]] and the [[Avocado Aquarium]] — its member guilds passing through those war blocs while Adonis held the social layer, exactly as Hestia had spanned the war blocs before it.

Adonis was still running community events in February 2024{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol12|vol. 12, 20 Feb 2024}}, and in March 2024 ran a joint Discord server with the guild The Farplane, whose membership in Adonis was never recorded{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol13|vol. 13, 22 Mar 2024}}. Nothing later is on record; no dissolution was ever recorded.

## Membership
The end date marks the alliance's last recorded activity, not a dissolution.

{{alliance:Adonis}}

## Legacy
Adonis carried the community-alliance tradition of [[Hestia]] and [[Niflheim]] into the mid-2020s. While the war alliances of 2022–2023 collapsed or faded within a season or two, Adonis was still hosting events nearly two years after its founding{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol13|vol. 13, 22 Mar 2024}} — the last community alliance on record.

articles.title: Aequitas
articles.summary: Wynncraft guild founded in late 2019 and led by FrozenGalaxy; a Goose guild, co-founder of Khaos, and member of Cucumber Company and smtn elf. Defender in the Long Raid of 2024, belligerent in the largest recorded war (against Avicia, 2025), and driven to zero territories in the ongoing 2026 war with Sequoia.
articles.leadImageCaption: Aequitas's guild emblem: a pair of golden scales lit from behind on a dark ground, the guild name beneath.

articles.title: Aequitas-Avicia war
articles.summary: The largest Wynncraft guild war ever recorded: Aequitas against Avicia, 3 November to 21 December 2025, with 15,710 territory exchanges and a weekly peak of 4,736. It was over by Christmas.

infobox.label: Scale
infobox.value: 15,710 territory exchanges; weekly peak 4,736 — the largest war on record

articles.body:
{{map:2025-11-03|The map when the war began}}

{{war-chart:Aequitas|Avicia|2025-10-19|2026-01-03}}

## Background

Like every war of [[private-diplomacy-era|the private-diplomacy era]], it has no written record: no declaration, no named cause, no published sides beyond the two principals{{cite:territory-exchanges|no written declaration, cause or sides survive for this war}}. By late 2025 even the forum's guild-politics venue was gone — the official Discord's #guild-politics channel had been renamed #guild-community that October, and a guild founder writing that October recalled a time when alliances "were formed, enemies were negotiated with, all behind closed doors"{{cite:thread-322643|post #1, IceResistance, 2 Oct 2025}}.

## Course of the war

The war between [[Aequitas]] and [[Avicia]] ran from 3 November to 21 December 2025{{cite:chronicle-records|Aequitas-Avicia war}}. Its seven weeks produced 15,710 territory exchanges, with a weekly peak of 4,736 — more than any other recorded conflict, surpassing the multi-year bloc wars of 2021–22 in raw volume{{cite:territory-exchanges|exchange totals and weekly peak, 3 Nov – 21 Dec 2025}}. Which side prevailed is not recorded; the war was over by Christmas.

## Aftermath

No settlement is recorded. Within a year Aequitas was at war again — [[aequitas-sequoia-war|against Sequoia]], the conflict still running as of September 2026{{cite:territory-exchanges|Aequitas-Sequoia exchanges from the week of 24 Aug 2026}}.

articles.title: Aequitas-Sequoia war
articles.summary: The current war of the Wynncraft territory map: after a one-week clash in August 2025 and spring 2026 skirmishes, full war between Aequitas and Sequoia erupted in the week of 24 August 2026, with 7,488 territory exchanges in its first week. Ongoing as of September 2026.
articles.body:
{{map:2026-08-24|The map when full war erupted}}

{{war-chart:Aequitas|Sequoia|2026-08-09|2026-09-16}}

## Background

The two guilds had clashed before: a one-week fight in August 2025, then renewed skirmishes through spring 2026{{cite:territory-exchanges|Aequitas-Sequoia clashes, Aug 2025 and spring 2026}}. Sequoia entered the war as the dominant guild of the era, winner of seven consecutive [[guild-seasons|guild seasons]] from mid-2024{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|Seasons 19–25, 24 Jun 2024 – 20 Jul 2025}} and survivor of [[avicia-sequoia-war|its 2023 war with Avicia]]; Aequitas came off [[aequitas-avicia-war|the largest war in the territory record]] the previous winter, and before that [[the-long-raid|the Long Raid siege]] of 2024.

As with every conflict of [[private-diplomacy-era|the private-diplomacy era]], no cause or declaration was ever published{{cite:chronicle-records|Aequitas-Sequoia war}}.

## Course of the war

The opening week was among the most violent ever recorded: 7,488 territory exchanges{{cite:territory-exchanges|weekly capture volumes, week of 24 Aug 2026}}. On 3 September 2026 Aequitas held 21 territories{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-aequitas|territory count, captured 3 Sep 2026}}; how far the guild fell during the opening week is not recorded.

## Aftermath

The war has no aftermath yet. As with every conflict of the era, the alliances behind it are undocumented.

articles.title: Aesir Pact
articles.summary: The Aesir Pact was a 2018 pact of sister guilds inside the Federation, "especially dedicated to Gavel, and the birth place of Aesir, the canyon." Created on 25 March 2018 by Fantasy, Sins of Seedia and IceBlue Team, it reached five guilds in October 2018; the three that left the Federation on 10 November carried on alone, conceded part of the Canyon on 31 December, abandoned the region on 18 January 2019, elected a new leader on 23 February and was still being rejoined on 27 March 2019.

articles.title: Alliance Alliance
articles.summary: Alliance Alliance ("Double AA") was the breakaway war alliance of February 2018: five guilds that split from the Coalition over a proposed division of the province of Wynn, joined by Fantasy and Necronomicon. It held most of the map in the days after the split, lost it to the newly formed Federation on 21 February, retook it for three days in early March, and was reduced to a single territory on 19–20 March 2018.

articles.title: Alliance Channel Security, February 2018
articles.summary: Both alliances of February 2018 worked on the assumption that anything written in a channel could be read from the other side, and each of the month's three responses was about access rather than content. Six days after it was founded the Federation shut the general channel anyone could walk into and replaced it with one only members could see.

infobox.label: Times
infobox.value: Alliance clock, eight hours behind UTC

articles.body:
Times here are the alliances' own clock, which ran eight hours behind UTC that winter.

## A service removed for what it could read

On 11 February 2018, asked why a command people found useful had stopped working, a member of the [[coalition|Coalition]]'s moderation explained in the war channel that the service behind it had been taken out of the alliance's server.{{cite:alliance-channel-security-february-2018-discord-private|11 Feb 2018, the question}} Her reasons were that it could read every message in any channel it sat in{{cite:alliance-channel-security-february-2018-discord-private|11 Feb 2018, what it could read}}, that it had been present in the leadership and covert channels as well as the ordinary ones{{cite:alliance-channel-security-february-2018-discord-private|11 Feb 2018, which channels}}, and that it belonged to a member of [[titans-valor|Titans Valor]], a guild then attacking the alliance.{{cite:alliance-channel-security-february-2018-discord-private|11 Feb 2018, the ownership}} A member disputed the technical claim and she maintained it; the service stayed out.{{cite:alliance-channel-security-february-2018-discord-private|11 Feb 2018, the dispute}} Whether the guild ever read anything was never established, and the decision rests on what the alliance thought possible rather than on anything it found.

## A role obtained by impersonation

Two days later members set out an older version of the same problem. On 13 February a member of [[hall-of-fame|Hall of Fame]] described in the Coalition's war channel how a person had created a second account and presented himself on it as a new member of the guild Kasai in order to be given an alliance member role.{{cite:alliance-channel-security-february-2018-discord-private|13 Feb 2018, the second account}} He held a conversation between his two accounts to sustain it.{{cite:alliance-channel-security-february-2018-discord-private|13 Feb 2018, the staged conversation}} Several members confirmed it and one said it had been entertaining at the time.{{cite:alliance-channel-security-february-2018-discord-private|13 Feb 2018, the confirmations}} The telling carries no date for the incident itself, and what office the person held was never established. The wider practice is at [[espionage-and-infiltration|espionage and infiltration]].

## The general channel closed, six days in

The third episode is dated to the minute and cost the alliance something. At 05:45 on 22 February 2018 [[the-federation|the Federation]]'s founder told the guild leaders' channel that the general channel had been closed because its invite link had been posted somewhere public.{{cite:alliance-channel-security-february-2018-discord-private|22 Feb 2018, 05:45, the closure}} The effect he gave was that anyone joining the server at random could no longer see alliance discussion.{{cite:alliance-channel-security-february-2018-discord-private|22 Feb 2018, the effect stated}} He attributed the leak to a member guild's own server, and it went no further than his saying so.{{cite:alliance-channel-security-february-2018-discord-private|22 Feb 2018, the attribution}} A replacement general channel that only members could see had been made by then, and another member had announced it in the same channel two minutes earlier.{{cite:alliance-channel-security-february-2018-discord-private|22 Feb 2018, 05:43}}

The alliance was six days old. Its permanent channel structure had been built on 17 February as a near-copy of the Coalition's, and this is the first change made to that structure — a restriction.{{cite:federation-founding-night-2018-discord-private|channel creations computed from Discord ids, 17 Feb 2018}} What the alliance had written in that channel in its first six days, and whether any of it went into the replacement, was never set out. The Coalition had lost its own first server five weeks earlier — see [[the-coalition-discord-deletion|the Coalition Discord deletion]].{{cite:coalition-discord-deleted-january-2018-discord-private|12 Jan 2018, 04:19-04:20 UTC}}

articles.title: Alliance governance
articles.summary: How Wynncraft alliances of 2016–2019 governed themselves: votes cast through a Discord bot at one vote per guild leader, territory allocated by committee and map, membership held on written conditions, and rulebooks assembled incident by incident. Almost every rule in them can be traced to the thing that had just gone wrong.

articles.title: Defending an ally's territory
articles.summary: A Federation guild that recaptured a territory for an ally chose the defence it left behind, and a defence heavy enough to keep the enemy out could be too heavy for the owner to retake. The guild leaders voted a limit on it in March 2018 and had forgotten it by July; the alliance issued a fresh rule in August 2018 and then a per-guild reference sheet, and none of the three settled it.

articles.title: Alovilatious Treaty
articles.summary: A multi-guild targeting arrangement of January 2018, assembled by Titans Valor's leader IceResistance and announced in the Coalition's own general channel on 22 January, aimed at making Hall of Fame's holdings untenable. His name for it lasted about an hour before the Coalition replaced it with a nickname derived from a pasta shape — and five weeks later he denied that any of it had existed.

articles.title: Angels of Eternal
articles.summary: Angels of Eternal [AoE] was a Wynncraft guild admitted to the Federation in February 2018 on a minute's conversation and no recorded vote, on the strength of its war players. By June it held no assigned territory and its own advocate warned the leadership it would defect; its leader went to HackForums on 21 July and the guild left the next day, then took more ground that August than in any other month of its recorded life.

articles.title: Aphelion
articles.summary: Aphelion [Aph] was a small Wynncraft guild founded in March 2018 that joined the Federation on 22 July on a written application, was given three territories two months later because it had not been fighting, and resigned in October after its leaders argued in the alliance's own channel that it had only one member who could defend anything.

articles.title: Arenos
articles.summary: Paladin A'renos organised Ordo Malleus in November 2015 and founded the Emperium of Wynn in April 2017, opening and keeping the forum thread of each. He officiated the Emperium's Emperator election.
articles.body:
## [[ordo-malleus|Ordo Malleus]]

The alliance thread "-= Ordo Malleus =-" was opened by Paladin A'renos on 6 November 2015 and ran to 296 replies before it was locked, its last post falling on 10 March 2016{{cite:forums-wynncraft-com-forums-guilds-72-prefix-id-82-order-post-date-direction-asc|complete census of Alliance-prefixed threads, page 1}}. A'renos was then a chief of Kangronomicon; he recruited the member guilds and created the alliance's leader chat{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L148–190, composed 22 Feb 2018}}. Within weeks, [[drew1011|Drew1011]] canvassed the other leaders and secured agreement to move alliance business to a new chat excluding A'renos, citing A'renos's manner toward them{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L186–190, composed 19 Jan 2018}}.

A'renos afterwards left Kangronomicon and bought the guild WynnTheory [WTh], admitted to Ordo Malleus on 3 February 2016 over Drew1011's objection{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L366–370, composed 19 Jan 2018}} and on the alliance's roster that 20 February{{cite:thread-109350|post #11, Drew1011, 20 Feb 2016}}. A'renos left Wynncraft after the alliance collapsed on 9 March 2016 and did not reappear for about a year, returning through an Ordo Malleus reunion Discord in early 2017; at Drew1011's request there, the deleted Ordo thread was restored{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L462, L692–695}}.

## The Emperium of Wynn

On 7 May 2017 A'renos opened the thread of the [[emperium-of-wynn|Emperium of Wynn]], describing it as "a Dynamic alliance that was formed on the 21st of April with the goal of uniting guilds of all levels and experience"{{cite:thread-188024|post #1, 7 May 2017}}. He kept the thread, defined its offices{{cite:thread-188024-p05|post #82, 16 Jun 2017, quoting the opening post}} and ran its monthly member awards{{cite:thread-188024-p03|post #60, 22 May 2017}}.

![Discord announcement by A'renos: "the time has come for the alliance to elect the @Emperator... If you would like to vote for @Nitrogen2Oxygen Please vote [N]. If you would rather vote for @Drew1011 Please vote [D]". The reaction tallies below read D = 30 and N = 31. The message's date was never recorded.](/images/chronicles/storytime/37-image.webp)

His departure was noted by another member on 4 September 2017 — "Such a sad time. Arenos leaves, [ElegantDeath] leaves and now my bot gets hecked"{{cite:thread-188024-p08|p8 #149, Nitrogen2Oxygen, 4 Sep 2017}} — though he returned on 17 October 2017 to write "bumity bump bump lets get this back up", one of the thread's last two posts{{cite:thread-188024-p08|p8 #154, 17 Oct 2017}}.

articles.title: Arkada
articles.summary: Titans Valor's Aedile and "chief negotiator", and author of a near-contemporaneous memoir of the Luna-Terra war of 2019.

infobox.label: Known for
infobox.value: The "Inside Myself" memoir of the [[luna-terra-war|Luna-Terra war]] (Sep 2019)

articles.body:
In July 2019 Arkada - forum name Leonhart_Arkada, and Aedile, or "chief negotiator", of [[titans-valor|Titans Valor]] [ANO], the guild founded by [[IceResistance]]{{cite:thread-252647|post #1, 20 Jul 2019}} - authored "An Argument Against The Current Monopoly On Territory", describing [[Luna]] as "the four most powerful guilds on Wynn" and comparing its dominance to the [[the-federation|Federation]]'s{{cite:thread-252647|post #1, 20 Jul 2019}}; [[drew1011|Drew1011]] replied with the era's standard defense of mega-alliance cycles{{cite:thread-252647|post #15, 29 Jul 2019}}.

Around 14 September 2019, with the [[luna-terra-war|Luna-Terra war]] still in motion, he published "Inside Myself - Recent Wynncraft Guild History" on Wattpad under the alias A_Challenger_Arrives - a near-contemporaneous memoir, written as events unfolded rather than years later{{cite:wattpad-com-784189853-inside-myself-recent-wynncraft-guild-history|c. 14 Sep 2019}}. It records that [[Valkyrie]] was "now calling themselves the Luna alliance"; that [[Terra]] formed from multiple small alliances merging "nearly 15 guilds", including The Ascendancy in which Titans Valor fought; that Terra's weekend raid conquered all Luna territories except [[kingdom-foxes|Kingdom Foxes]]' within six hours; and that Luna's organized counter-raid of 14 September failed{{cite:wattpad-com-784189853-inside-myself-recent-wynncraft-guild-history|c. 14 Sep 2019}}. As a participant's memoir it is partisan by nature, but its closeness to the events makes it the era's most valuable single narrative source.

articles.title: Artemis
articles.summary: Artemis was the dominant war alliance of the 2020 territory map, founded on 30 October 2019 by Imperial, Paladins United and Caeruleum Order. Its roster transformed almost completely across 2020 — by December both surviving founders were on the opposing side — and it collapsed on 11 May 2021 together with its rival Goose.

articles.title: The Artemis-Goose era
articles.summary: From the disbanding of DiamondDeities in January 2020 to the Great Collapse of 11 May 2021: Artemis held the map, its own founders drifted into the opposition that became Goose, and both alliances died on the same day. It is also the era in which the community began writing its own record down.
articles.body:
{{map:2020-12-19|The map at the height of the Goose-Artemis war}}

The Artemis-Goose era opens with the last aftershock of 2019 - [[Nitrogen2Oxygen]] disbanding [[DiamondDeities]] on 8 January 2020, which ended [[Horologium]] and birthed Lux Nova{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}} - and closes with the only day on which both major alliances died at once.

## Artemis transformed

[[Artemis]], founded on 30 October 2019 by [[Imperial]], [[Paladins United]] and Caeruleum Order{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}, became the era's map holder - but not with its founding roster. By March 2020 [[Kingdom Foxes]] was a member and [[ShadowFall]] held a leadership seat{{cite:thread-263975-p02|p2 #36, GoulartJJ, 9 Mar 2020}}; by December 2020 a megalist post described Artemis as 'the war alliance made up of all the current massive land holding guilds', including [[Titans Valor]]{{cite:thread-278112|p1 #10, Pally, 2 Dec 2020}} - while founders Paladins United and Imperial had drifted out and appear on the opposing side. The exact join and leave dates of this transformation were never documented.

## The chroniclers

Almost everything known about this era's alliances was written by a handful of identifiable people, and their guild affiliations matter to how the claims should be weighed. [[the-forum-megalist|The megalist]] itself was created and maintained by [[sg-voltage|Sg_Voltage]], whose own guild is unknown - a neutral registrar{{cite:thread-278112-wb20210704|post #1, capture of 4 Jul 2021}}. The December 2020 account of [[Hestia]] and Artemis was posted by [[paladinsorcerer|Pally]] of Titans Valor, a member of both{{cite:thread-278112|p1 #10, Pally, 2 Dec 2020}}. The 'Guild Moderators' thread that names the anti-Artemis coalition was written by Sheepn of Diablo [DXI], a coalition guild{{cite:thread-279337|post #1, Sheepn, 18 Dec 2020}}. The first written use of the name [[Goose]] came from 99loulou999 of The Dark Phoenix [TNI], with Eden's Lev98bug confirming his own guild's membership half an hour later{{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #71-73, 19 Jan 2021}}. The 1 February 2021 side-switch report is [[urbymine]]'s, a former Chief of [[Avicia]]{{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #76, urbymine, 1 Feb 2021}}. The only [[Niflheim]] roster ever posted was written by HungHung of Avicia{{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #146, HungHung, 7 Jul 2021}}. A two-part illustrated roster of Goose was drawn by [[drasalia|Drasalia]] of ChinaNumberOne{{cite:thread-289196|post #1, 30 Mar 2021}}{{cite:thread-289556|post #1, 6 Apr 2021}}. Every one of these writers was reporting on a bloc they belonged to, except Sg_Voltage.

## The social layer

Alongside the war blocs ran an unusually rich community-alliance layer: [[Hestia]] (formed ~mid-2020: Titans Valor, Empire of Sindria, Lux Nova, Paladins United, later Emorians and HackForums){{cite:thread-278112-p07|p7 #140, Pally, 6 Jun 2021}}, [[Niflheim]] (Avicia, IceBlue Team, ShadowFall, TheNoLifes){{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #146, HungHung, 7 Jul 2021}}, the [[Empire of Nemract]] (a political union of [[The Simple Ones]] and Mystic Woods from 17 August 2020, complete with an empress and court titles){{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}, and the perennial [[Valkyrie]].

## The rise of Goose

In December 2020 an 'unnamed group of anti-Artemis guilds' - [[Avicia]], [[Emorians]], [[Eden]], Ultra Violet, Diablo, Bovemists, The Dark Phoenix, and ex-founders Paladins United and Imperial among them - erupted against the map holder{{cite:thread-279337|post #1, Sheepn, 18 Dec 2020}}: 913 territory exchanges that month, after months of skirmishing{{cite:territory-exchanges|December 2020 territory exchange volume}}. By 19 January 2021 the coalition carried the name [[Goose]]{{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #71-73, 19 Jan 2021}}. It grew through spring: 'BNU(IBT), SHY and TNL are all goose now', urbymine recorded on 1 February 2021{{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #76, urbymine, 1 Feb 2021}} - ShadowFall switching sides from Artemis leadership - and by late March it had absorbed the future [[Khaos]] core ([[Aequitas]], WheresTheFinish, ChinaNumberOne, Fuzzy Spiders, Eden){{cite:thread-289196|post #1, 30 Mar 2021}}. Goose took map control as the [[goose-artemis-war|Goose-Artemis war]] ground on{{cite:territory-exchanges|Goose-Artemis war volumes, spring 2021}}.

The new arrivals were not all new guilds. Aequitas had existed since November 2019{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-aequitas|creation date 24 Nov 2019, retrieved 2 Sep 2026}} but only became publicly visible in this window: FrozenGalaxy opened its recruitment thread on 3 January 2021{{cite:thread-280525|post #1, thread created 3 Jan 2021}}, added it to the megalist a fortnight later{{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #66, FrozenGalaxy, 17 Jan 2021}}, and by 30 March it was one of the twelve guilds in Drasalia's fanart roster{{cite:thread-289196|post #1, 30 Mar 2021}}.

Mid-era, the game itself changed: version 1.20 'Gavel Reborn' (20 January 2021){{cite:thread-281822|post #1, 20 Jan 2021}} rebuilt [[territory-warfare|territory warfare]] around war towers and a guild resource economy, and introduced the in-game ally system{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, 'Guilds & Wars' sections, 23 Nov 2020}} (see [[the-diplomacy-update|The Diplomacy update]]). During the February 2021 argument over the rework, Eden members described crawling through Emorians territory held at medium and high defence{{cite:thread-286375|post #10, Plymouth, 20 Feb 2021}}.

## Profession Heaven's neutrality

On 25 January 2021 the warring blocs jointly granted [[Profession Heaven]] neutral status as a public profession-XP guild, protected by both Goose and Artemis and given Silent Expanse territory{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}} - a protection honoured by successor alliances for over five years. The guild had been founded five days earlier by [[crokee|Crokee]]{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-profession-20heaven|creation date 20 Jan 2021, retrieved 2 Sep 2026}}{{cite:thread-285237|post #1, Crokee}}; who brokered the pact was never recorded.

## The Great Collapse

On 11 May 2021 Goose and Artemis both collapsed on the same day - [[the-great-collapse|the Great Collapse]]. Thirteen guilds, including [[The Aquarium]], formed [[Valhalla]]; nine formed [[Khaos]]{{cite:thread-278112-p07|p7 #134-137, 25 May 2021}}; and the [[the-realignment-era|realignment era]] began with the two new blocs already at war.

articles.title: Astrafteri Affinity
articles.summary: The Astrafteri Affinity, written Astrafterí Affinity and shortened to Astra, was a Wynncraft alliance of 2016 founded by coralialia. It mixed small guilds with large ones, took in HackForums during that guild's expulsion from Ordo Malleus, and decayed through the summer of 2016.

infobox.label: Members named
infobox.value: [[hackforums|HackForums]], [[blacklisted|Blacklisted]], The Sebbelonien Plebs, Cats and Turtles, Dragons Arise, Holders of LE

articles.body:
## Founding

coralialia, posting as qqcora, wrote in June 2016: "refer to the alliance i created, astraffinity, which is a combination of many small guilds and big guilds, including hax"{{cite:thread-130386-p02|post #30, 9 Jun 2016, quoting coralialia}}. [[drew1011|Drew1011]], her guild leader at the time, wrote that she founded it after leaving Holders of LE, "to rival Ordo, as she had begun to hate both Arenos and Kru"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L352–353, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 26 Feb 2018}}, and placed the founding in about January 2016. No reason for its creation was recorded at the time.

By 11 February 2016 [[hackforums|HackForums]]' recruitment thread listed "Astrafterí-affinity" under **Alliances** in its opening post{{cite:thread-109319|post #13, 11 Feb 2016, quoting the HackForums opening post}}. The alliance's own thread, "✯ Astrafterí Affinity ✯", was posted on 3 April 2016 — by LordMuttonChops, not by coralialia — and drew 14 replies before being locked{{cite:forums-wynncraft-com-forums-guilds-72-prefix-id-82-order-post-date-direction-asc|complete census of Alliance-prefixed threads, page 1}}.

## The name, reused

The name came back eighteen months later: when five guilds walked out of the [[coalition|Coalition]] in February 2018 they were recorded calling themselves the Astrafteri Affinity, before settling on [[alliance-alliance|Alliance Alliance]].{{cite:federation-founding-week-2018-discord-private|February 2018}} Nobody recorded whether they knew whose name they had taken.

On 17 February 2018, the day after the walkout, the [[kingdom-foxes|Kingdom of Foxes]]' Viceroy learned the new opposing alliance had chosen that name and recognised it at once — as one founded years earlier by an officer who had left [[holders-of-le|Holders of LE]] after a dispute over an expulsion.{{cite:ordo-malleus-informal-power-discord-private|17 Feb 2018}} That remark is the only contemporaneous evidence that an alliance of the name existed before 2018 and who made it; everything else about its founding comes from accounts written later.

## Membership and character

The Sebbelonien Plebs, [[blacklisted|Blacklisted]], Cats and Turtles and Dragons Arise were members{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L352–359, composed 19 Jan 2018}}. Drew1011 wrote that he joined Holders of LE to it in March 2016 as a hedge while [[valkyrie|Valkyrie]] membership was being negotiated{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L466, composed 23 Jan 2018}}. Its founder put its size at "over 10 guilds, and every single one of them would back hax up if anyone tried to do something like this" — a claim made in the middle of an argument on an anti-HackForums thread{{cite:thread-130386-p02|post #30, 9 Jun 2016, quoting coralialia}}. Later that month she distinguished it from the informal understanding then holding the map: told by an UltimateXeons member that "our alliance with Hax and Lir" was letting three guilds keep their territory, she replied that this was "a mutual land agreement" and pointed him at the Astrafteri thread as "the actual alliance"{{cite:thread-133666|post #16, qqcora, 28 Jun 2016}}.

## HackForums and the alliance's end

In Drew1011's account, HackForums' rise ran through the alliance: "In Astra their power grew exponentially. They no longer had a massive list of allies that they could not attack, and had much more freedom in wars." As the alliance's guilds went inactive, "Astra eventually died, but Hax remained. They stayed in an alliance with [[libertas|Libertas]], and divided all of Wynn amongst themselves and a few others such as [[blacklisted|Blacklisted]]"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L508–512, composed 23 Jan 2018}}. He gave no dates for any of it{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L518, composed 23 Jan 2018}}.

On one point the contemporaneous record differs from his sequence. He places HackForums' move into Astra after the collapse of [[ordo-malleus|Ordo Malleus]] on 9 March 2016; the HackForums opening post already listed the alliance on 11 February 2016{{cite:thread-109319|post #13, 11 Feb 2016}}, during the weeks the same account says HackForums was expelled from Ordo{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L333–342, composed 19 Jan 2018}}. The alliance's last recorded activity was the closure of its thread; the final post is dated 14 September 2016{{cite:forums-wynncraft-com-forums-guilds-72-prefix-id-82-order-post-date-direction-asc|complete census of Alliance-prefixed threads, page 1}}.

articles.title: Aurelion
articles.summary: Aurelion was a four-guild community alliance formed in February 2017 around House of Sentinels, with Hippies of Snuggles, The Dark Phoenix and Dragons Arise joining over the following fortnight. It ran its own Discord and last appears in April 2017; no war activity is recorded for it.
articles.body:
## History

House of Sentinels, founded on 2 July 2016 and describing itself as "a place of respite for those who need it", named itself "a member guild of Aurelion, a community alliance", with a dated join for each member{{cite:thread-135191|post #1, as last revised 29 Apr 2017}}:

| Guild | Joined |
|---|---|
| House of Sentinels | 14 Feb 2017 |
| Hippies of Snuggles | 15 Feb 2017 |
| The Dark Phoenix | 26 Feb 2017 |
| Dragons Arise | 27 Feb 2017 |

The alliance ran a Discord server open enough that outsiders used it as a point of contact: an applicant to House of Sentinels wrote on 30 April 2017 that "when I went on the Aurelion Discord, I asked if I could claim refugee status and someone told me to apply"{{cite:thread-187152|post #20, 30 Apr 2017}} — the last mention of Aurelion anywhere, and a sign it was still operating that spring.

House of Sentinels' 2017 council was Pyrias, Pretzule, wrxryuu, [[killerfish|Killerfish]], ChaChaChaChino and 01100110111;{{cite:thread-135191|post #1, as last revised 29 Apr 2017}} by 30 April 2017 Pretzule led it and it had begun "focusing on warring with other guilds and maintaining territory";{{cite:thread-187152|post #1, Pretzule}} and it went on to become one of the four founding guilds of the [[coalition|Coalition]] in October 2017.{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}

## Membership

The four guilds above are the complete known membership. No founding announcement was ever posted, and who led the alliance was never recorded.

## Legacy

Aurelion left no record of warring, no dissolution notice and no successor. Its interest lies in what it says about the road to the Coalition: seven months before that alliance was founded, its future core guild was already the anchor of a small community bloc with its own Discord, recruiting refugees from collapsing guilds. Dragons Arise belonged in the same period to another community alliance, Lux Imperius{{cite:thread-109350|post #1, "Old alliances" section}} — an illustration of how loosely the [[early-guild-era|early guild era]]'s community pacts overlapped.

articles.title: Avicia
articles.summary: Wynncraft guild founded in 2018 by birdiefly209. The last guild standing when Luna wiped the map in 2019's alliance wars, a member of Goose, Niflheim, Valhalla, Vanir, Cucumber Company, Adonis and smtn elf, half of the Avocado Aquarium pact, and a belligerent in the largest war ever recorded, against Aequitas in 2025.

articles.title: Avicia-Sequoia war
articles.summary: Avicia's war with the young Sequoia: skirmishes through spring 2023, a main eruption from 30 October to 20 November 2023 peaking at 1,454 territory exchanges per week, and a second round in January 2024.
articles.body:
The Avicia-Sequoia war was fought between [[Avicia]], a veteran of every major bloc since 2019, and [[Sequoia]], a guild barely a year old — founded 14 October 2022{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-sequoia|guild creation date, 14 Oct 2022}} — whose rise it did nothing to stop.

{{map:2023-10-30|The map when the main eruption began}}

{{war-chart:Avicia|Sequoia|2023-10-15|2024-02-13}}

## Background

The war belongs to [[private-diplomacy-era|the private-diplomacy era]]: it was never declared, never discussed on the forums, and its cause was never named{{cite:territory-exchanges|no written record of this war exists}}. Skirmishing between the two guilds is visible through spring 2023{{cite:territory-exchanges|Avicia-Sequoia skirmishing, spring 2023}}, while Avicia was still in [[smtn elf]] and then in the [[Avocado Aquarium]] pact.

## Course of the war

The main eruption ran from 30 October to 20 November 2023, peaking at 1,454 territory exchanges per week. A second round followed in January 2024{{cite:territory-exchanges|war windows and weekly peak, 30 Oct – 20 Nov 2023 and Jan 2024}}{{cite:chronicle-records|Avicia-Sequoia war}}. Which side held the advantage is not known.

## Aftermath

Sequoia's rise continued regardless of the war: from mid-2024 it won seven consecutive [[guild-seasons|guild seasons]]{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|Seasons 19–25, 24 Jun 2024 – 20 Jul 2025}}. Sequoia and [[Aequitas]] would later fight the decade's closing wars, including [[aequitas-sequoia-war|the ongoing war of 2026]]; Avicia went on to fight [[aequitas-avicia-war|the largest war ever recorded]] in late 2025.

articles.title: Avocado Aquarium
articles.summary: Avocado Aquarium was the two-guild war pact of Avicia and The Aquarium after they quit smtn elf in June 2023, waging a sniping and claim-taking campaign against their former allies into early 2024. The pair ran shared infrastructure including the joint subguild Avoquarium [HQs]; the pact's name was never written down while it existed.

articles.title: bitesizedbee4
articles.summary: The Titans Valor member who wrote and signed the first six volumes of the guild's newsletter, Titan Times, between May and October 2022 - the volumes that date Cucumber Company's formation and its rename to Smtn else.
articles.body:
bitesizedbee4, credited in the newsletter as Bee, signed volumes 1 to 6 of [[Titans Valor]]'s newsletter [[titan-times|Titan Times]], published between 8 May 2022{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol1|vol. 1, 8 May 2022, closing signature}} and 12 October 2022{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol6|vol. 6, 12 Oct 2022, closing signature}}, writing each of them alone. Volume 1's closing remarks describe the work as an inheritance rather than a founding - 'I was really unsure about taking over the Times on my own, and spent a lot of days putting it off because I didn't want to fall short of anyone's expectations'{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol1|vol. 1, 8 May 2022, closing remarks}} - though what preceded volume 1, if anything, is not recorded.

Volume 7 (16 December 2022) expanded the newsletter to a team of writers; Bee contributed the article 'Events: A Deeper Dive on Their Impacts', built on a member survey about in-game and guild-hosted events, and the volume closed 'Thank you Snazz, Geb, and Bee for writing this volume!'{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol7|vol. 7, 16 Dec 2022}}. The same volume lists bitesizedbee4 among members promoted to Sorcerer, noted as 'now Artificer'{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol7|vol. 7, 16 Dec 2022, promotions}}. She is still the narrating voice of the Ocean Trials explainer in volume 8 of 18 February 2023 - 'Hey Bee, what's Ocean Trials?'{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol8|vol. 8, 18 Feb 2023}} - after which the newsletter's bylines pass to other writers{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol10|vol. 10, 23 Apr 2023, bylines}}.

Her volumes are the principal dated record of the alliance politics of 2022. Volume 1 places the formation of [[Cucumber Company]] at the start of guild Season 5{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol1|vol. 1, 8 May 2022}}, and volume 6 records its archiving and rename to 'Smtn else' at the start of Season 8{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol6|vol. 6, 12 Oct 2022}} - see [[smtn elf]].

articles.title: BuildCraftia
articles.summary: BuildCraftia [BCr] was a Wynncraft war guild of 2017–2019: an Emperium of Wynn member, one of the two War Syndicate guilds that fought back hardest in the Gavel Invasion, a founding guild of the Federation, expelled from it in March 2018 over a territory seizure, and for six months afterwards the alliance's most persistent opponent.

articles.title: C0rupted
articles.summary: A Titans Valor member, a writer for the guild newsletter Titan Times from volume 12 (February 2024) to volume 21 (May 2026), and the lead developer of the rewrite of the guild's Discord bot, Valor.

infobox.label: Known for
infobox.value: [[titan-times|Titan Times]] writer, vols. 12-21; rewrite of the Valor Discord bot

articles.body:
C0rupted, a member of [[Titans Valor]] [ANO] and a developer on the guild's software, introduced himself in volume 12 of its newsletter [[titan-times|Titan Times]] (20 February 2024) as 'the new writer, C0rupted, taking up the mantle'{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol12|vol. 12, 20 Feb 2024}}, wrote volume 13{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol13|vol. 13, 22 Mar 2024}} and volume 14{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol14|vol. 14, 24 May 2024}}, and from volume 19 onward covered the Brilliance cabinet, the guild's technical team{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol19|vol. 19, 2 Aug 2025, Brilliance cabinet}}{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol21|vol. 21, 18 May 2026, Brilliance cabinet}}. He was still on the masthead in volume 21, the last published volume{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol21|vol. 21, 18 May 2026, masthead}}.

He overhauled the guild's Discord bot{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol14|vol. 14, 24 May 2024, Brilliance cabinet}}; the project, originally planned as a lightweight spin-off called Valor Lite, grew into a full rewrite 'with C0rupted leading the charge on the massive slash command overhaul', giving the bot a new command framework built on Discord's slash commands{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol20|vol. 20, 23 Nov 2025}}. By November 2025 he had 'officially become a Titan'{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol20|vol. 20, 23 Nov 2025, promotions}}.

![Example output of the -guild command on Titans Valor's Discord bot Valor, shown in Titan Times vol. 13 (22 March 2024): a guild's level, owner, member count, territory count, war count and creation date, above a list of the members online.](/images/chronicles/media/c0rupted-59a7fc93.webp){{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol13|vol. 13, 22 Mar 2024}}

He won the guild's Ocean Trials 'Champion of the Ocean' title for guild Season 24 with 1,360 wars, and placed second in Season 25 with 2,390{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol19|vol. 19, 2 Aug 2025, Seasons 24 and 25 Ocean Trials}}. He passed the guild's Strategist test twice, in May 2024 and again in August 2025{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol14|vol. 14, 24 May 2024, strategist promotions}}{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol19|vol. 19, 2 Aug 2025, strategist promotions}}; the repetition was never explained.

articles.title: Calluum
articles.summary: Owner of Titans Valor, which he joined in April 2021. Titan Times marked his two-year mark as leader in February 2024 and interviewed him in November 2025, where he described taking the role because 'no one else wanted it when pally was stepping down'.

infobox.label: Role
infobox.value: Owner; on the guild's Sage Council by May 2022

articles.body:
Calluum joined [[titans-valor|Titans Valor]] [ANO] on 4 April 2021 and held the owner slot as of September 2026, with roughly 671 billion guild XP contributed{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-titans-20valor|v3/guild response, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}.

He sat at the Sage Council tier of the guild's new hierarchy in May 2022{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol1|vol. 1, 8 May 2022}}, and thereafter organised events and provided prizes — running the guild's Secret Santa in December 2022, for example{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol7|vol. 7, 16 Dec 2022}}. His name was also rendered 'Callum', sometimes within a single volume of [[titan-times|Titan Times]]{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol7|vol. 7, 16 Dec 2022}}; volume 20 warned readers not to confuse him with another member, 'Mayor callluuum'{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol20|vol. 20, 23 Nov 2025}}.

## Leadership of Titans Valor

Volume 12, of 20 February 2024, congratulated 'Calluum for hitting the two-year mark as our leader'{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol12|vol. 12, 20 Feb 2024}}, which would place the start of his tenure around February 2022. That sits awkwardly against the same newsletter's earlier record of the handover: volume 6, of 12 October 2022, still announced 'the long term hiatus of ANO's founder, IceResistance', and volume 9, of 25 March 2023, is the first to call [[iceresistance|IceResistance]] the guild's 'previous owner'{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol6|vol. 6, 12 Oct 2022}}{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol9|vol. 9, 25 Mar 2023}}. The two datings were never reconciled.

Interviewed for volume 20 on 23 November 2025 — introduced as 'our glorious leader Cal' — he described how he came to the role: 'No one else wanted it when pally was stepping down, so I realised I'd need to step up and take on the mantle.'{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol20|vol. 20, 23 Nov 2025}} The succession thus ran IceResistance, then a leader he called 'pally', then Calluum. Who 'pally' was is not known. [[paladinsorcerer|PaladinSorcerer]] posted as 'Pally' for Titans Valor in 2020 and 2021{{cite:thread-278112|post #10, 2 Dec 2020}}, but Titan Times volume 3, of 12 June 2022, lists him among recipients of the Veteran Medal, 'granted to distinguished former members of ANO'{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol3|vol. 3, 12 Jun 2022}}.

## Views

In the same interview he described the guild landscape as having deteriorated over his time in it: 'Everything was entirely different, guilds were entirely roleplay and prestige driven rather than materialistically like they are these days', and, asked whether the changes had been for better or worse, 'I would definitely say for worse. Guild changes have forced smaller communities out and pushed an incredibly stale narrative of large guilds dominating the entire map.' His proposed remedies were to make defending worth its effort, 'reduce guild member caps and the maximum number of defendable territories to prevent megaclaims', and reduce guild XP from guild raids{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol20|vol. 20, 23 Nov 2025}}. The complaint about large guilds monopolising the map is the same one the warring community raised against the [[gavel-reborn|1.20 rework]] in 2021.

He remained an active warrer as well as owner, placing third in Titans Valor's internal war leaderboard for [[guild-seasons|Season 28]] with 381 wars, and announcing a data-collection collaboration with the group Wynn Analytics{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol21|vol. 21, 18 May 2026}}.

articles.title: Coalition Civil War
articles.summary: The February–March 2018 war between the Coalition and Alliance Alliance, the breakaway bloc formed by five of its member guilds. The newly formed Federation took the map on 21 February 2018 and ended the war on 19–20 March by reducing Alliance Alliance to a single territory.

infobox.label: Outcome
infobox.value: The [[the-federation|Federation]] took the map on 21 Feb 2018 and reduced [[Alliance Alliance]] to one territory on 19–20 Mar 2018; both belligerent alliances ceased to exist

articles.body:
The newly formed [[the-federation|Federation]] took control of the map on 21 February 2018{{cite:territory-exchanges|356 of 383 territories, 21 Feb 2018}}, and the war ended on 19–20 March, when Alliance Alliance was reduced from 72 territories to one{{cite:territory-exchanges|Alliance Alliance from 72 territories to one, 19–20 Mar 2018}}{{cite:community-guild-timeline|20 Mar 2018 entry}}, opening the [[federation-era|Federation era]].

{{map:2018-02-17|The map when the Coalition split}}

## Background

The Coalition was founded in October 2017 by [[Kingdom Foxes]], KingdomPhoenixes, Gilded Sparrows and House of Sentinels{{cite:community-guild-timeline|Oct 2017 entry}}. It took control of the Wynn Province on 23 November 2017, wiped War Syndicate on Christmas Day, and from then on held full dominance of the map{{cite:community-guild-timeline|23 Nov and 21–25 Dec 2017 entries}}.

## Course of the war

On 16–17 February 2018, five member guilds — [[HackForums]], [[Paladins United]], House of Sentinels, [[Emorians]] and Kangronomicon — left the Coalition over map disputes and formed Alliance Alliance together with [[Fantasy]] and Necronomicon, declaring war on their former alliance. (The community timeline image dates the split to 16 February{{cite:thread-265297|post #1, the community guild-timeline image}}; the Timeline document says 17 February{{cite:community-guild-timeline|17 Feb 2018 entry}}.)

The alliance's own channels count six withdrawals that evening rather than five, adding [[kingdomphoenixes|KingdomPhoenixes]], and give the order: HackForums first, then Paladins United and House of Sentinels within minutes, then KingdomPhoenixes, Kangronomicon and Emorians.{{cite:coalition-fracture-2018-discord-private|Coalition general channel, 16 Feb 2018}} Only five of the six left over the redistribution; KingdomPhoenixes went for reasons of its own and was inside the Federation within a day.{{cite:coalition-fracture-2018-discord-private|Coalition guild-leaders channel, 16 Feb 2018}} Two of the departing guilds were taking territory from guilds that had stayed within hours of announcing they were leaving, and the remaining members reported the same evening that one of the departed had already been allocated territory across an entire province in a new and still-unnamed alliance.{{cite:coalition-fracture-2018-discord-private|Coalition general channel, 16 Feb 2018}} The eight guilds left behind recruited outside help rather than fold, drawing in Sins of Seedia and Avos Air as active participants.{{cite:coalition-fracture-2018-discord-private|16–18 Feb 2018}}

The counter-offensive was run from a written plan. One member guild circulated a shared strategy document, reviewed by its allies, proposing that attacks be concentrated on a single rival guild to drain its treasury rather than spread across the front; on 18 February the successor alliance's guilds drove two guilds of the rival bloc off the territory map entirely.{{cite:coalition-fracture-2018-discord-private|strategy document and counter-offensive, 18 Feb 2018}} At least one guild changed sides during the fighting, joining the successor alliance on the condition that it actively attack the bloc it had just left.{{cite:coalition-fracture-2018-discord-private|February 2018}}

The split ended the Coalition as an entity almost at once: its remnant merged with the remains of War Syndicate into a new alliance, the Federation, founded and led by [[Drew1011]]{{cite:thread-265297|post #16, Lego_DW, 4 Apr 2020}}{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}. Three days later the Federation destroyed HackForums' territorial holdings in a single half-day operation — see [[the-wipe-of-hackforums|The wipe of HackForums]].

Daily bloc holdings across the war{{cite:territory-exchanges|daily ownership reconstruction, 5 Feb – 10 Apr 2018}}:

| Date | Federation | Alliance Alliance | Territories on the map |
|---|---|---|---|
| 17 Feb | 28 | 337 | 376 |
| 19 Feb | 134 | 187 | 379 |
| 20 Feb | 272 | 38 | 383 |
| 21 Feb | 356 | 24 | 383 |
| 2 Mar | 164 | 157 | 383 |
| 3 Mar | 43 | 308 | 383 |
| 4 Mar | 114 | 236 | 383 |
| 19 Mar | 371 | 1 | 383 |
| 20 Mar | 380 | 2 | 383 |

Alliance Alliance held most of the map immediately after the split — 337 of 376 territories on 17 February against the Federation's 28{{cite:territory-exchanges|337 of 376 territories, 17 Feb 2018}}; the breakaway bloc "had the map before the night was over"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|part 17, composed 11 Jul 2018}}. The Federation reversed that within four days and took the map on 21 February, holding 356 of 383 territories, or 93%{{cite:territory-exchanges|356 of 383 territories, 21 Feb 2018}}.

Alliance Alliance retook most of the map for three days at the start of March. Federation holdings fell to 164 territories on 2 March and to 43, or 11%, on 3 March, with Alliance Alliance back at 308, before recovering to 114 on 4 March and to roughly 300 from 6 March{{cite:territory-exchanges|Federation 43 of 383 territories, 3 Mar 2018}}. The reversal followed a mob update that took effect on 1 March{{cite:drew1011-storytime|part 17, composed 30 Aug 2018}}; it was the only interruption to the bloc's map control, "aside from ~3 days in March"{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}.

The war ended on 19–20 March 2018. Alliance Alliance fell from 72 territories to one on 19 March, and the Federation reached 380 of 383 territories, or 99%, on 20 March{{cite:territory-exchanges|Alliance Alliance from 72 territories to one, 19–20 Mar 2018}}. That was the elimination of the opposing bloc rather than the moment the Federation took the map, which had happened a month earlier{{cite:community-guild-timeline|20 Mar 2018 entry}}.

No war chart exists for this conflict: the fighting involved two multi-guild blocs rather than a single pair of guilds, and the exchange log begins only in January 2018{{cite:territory-exchanges|the exchange log begins in January 2018}}.

## Aftermath

With the war over, Alliance Alliance dissolved and several of its guilds — Fantasy, Paladins United and Emorians among them — joined the Federation{{cite:chronicle-records|Coalition, Alliance Alliance and Federation}}, which went on to hold the entire map for 8 months and 25 days{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}, until [[the-federation-dies|its death in November 2018]]. The Federation's genealogy remained disputed among veterans: Lego_DW later wrote that 'Coa and WS merged... this was a creation of fed'{{cite:thread-265297|post #16, Lego_DW, 4 Apr 2020}}, while Slayne claimed in 2018 to have created it via Alliance Alliance{{cite:thread-237070-p03|p3 #45, Slayne, 14 Nov 2018}}.

articles.title: The Coalition Under Attack, February 2018
articles.summary: Much of the fighting around the Coalition in its last fortnight was not between alliances. A player pursued a campaign of his own against the alliance's principal rival and was offered a role in its server; a guild taking its ground said it only wanted to annoy one enemy; and the alliance argued with its own members over who was fighting where.

infobox.label: Times
infobox.value: Alliance clock, eight hours behind UTC

articles.body:
Times here are the alliance's own clock, which ran eight hours behind UTC that winter.

The organised side of the fighting in this fortnight — the multi-guild arrangement assembled against the [[coalition|Coalition]] — is at [[alovilatious-treaty|the Alovilatious treaty]]. What follows is the rest of it.

## A contest of speed

The alliance's running conflict with [[hackforums|HackForums]] was fought as a contest over speed rather than as a campaign. Through early February 2018 members on both sides needled each other in the Coalition's own war channel about which was taking territories out from under the other.{{cite:coalition-under-attack-february-2018-discord-private|early Feb 2018, the needling}} A war-leader answered a report that HackForums had got there first by saying the alliance simply had to be faster still.{{cite:coalition-under-attack-february-2018-discord-private|early Feb 2018, the war-leader's answer}} Members called it a free-for-all war between the two guilds.{{cite:coalition-under-attack-february-2018-discord-private|the members' phrase}} That was their phrase and not a statement about the alliance's pool of open ground, which in this period existed only as black areas on two map images and was never written out by name.{{cite:coalition-standing-documents-january-2018-discord-private|the January free-for-all pool as two images}}

Two of the guilds attacking the alliance had stopped acting together by 12 February. A war-leader told the war channel that [[angels-of-eternal|Angels of Eternal]] and [[titans-valor|Titans Valor]] were separate.{{cite:coalition-under-attack-february-2018-discord-private|12 Feb 2018, the two guilds separate}} He added that Angels of Eternal had by then given up its attacks.{{cite:coalition-under-attack-february-2018-discord-private|12 Feb 2018, the attacks given up}} The roll of guilds attacking under the arrangement itself is at [[alovilatious-treaty|the treaty]], and Angels of Eternal is not on it.{{cite:pasta-treaties-2018-discord-private|the guilds attacking under the first arrangement}}

## A campaign of one

Not everything attacking the Coalition belonged to any bloc. On 3 February 2018 the alliance's leadership discussed a player running a campaign of his own against HackForums.{{cite:coalition-under-attack-february-2018-discord-private|3 Feb 2018, the campaign described}} His stated aim was to take the guild's first-place ranking.{{cite:coalition-under-attack-february-2018-discord-private|3 Feb 2018, the stated aim}} A war-leader reported that he had no particular grudge against the alliance, that he would keep going whatever anyone said, and that he meant to hand over to another player when he tired of it.{{cite:coalition-under-attack-february-2018-discord-private|3 Feb 2018, the war-leader's report}} The next day a member of the leadership proposed inviting him into the alliance's server temporarily and giving him a role, on the grounds that he was active in wars and had a view worth hearing.{{cite:coalition-under-attack-february-2018-discord-private|4 Feb 2018, the proposal}} Whether the invitation was ever made was never established.

On 13 February a member reported that the same player had become the leader of [[hall-of-fame|Hall of Fame]], and said he was rejoining that guild because of it.{{cite:coalition-under-attack-february-2018-discord-private|13 Feb 2018, the report}} It is one member's report in passing. Other members were still describing a different person as that guild's leader on 19 and 28 February.{{cite:coalition-under-attack-february-2018-discord-private|19 and 28 Feb 2018, the other account}}

## One target only

A guild attacking the alliance's ground told it that it was interested in one target. On 13 February 2018 a member of the Coalition's moderation reported that a representative of Avos Air had told her the guild only wanted to annoy [[paladins-united|Paladins United]].{{cite:coalition-under-attack-february-2018-discord-private|13 Feb 2018, the stated target}} The alliance's leader asked why and got no answer in the channel; a member speculated it was a reaction to another guild taking Corkus.{{cite:coalition-under-attack-february-2018-discord-private|13 Feb 2018, the question and the speculation}} Members also noted that the guild was defending its captures with a single creature, which is not the behaviour of a guild trying to hold ground.{{cite:coalition-under-attack-february-2018-discord-private|13 Feb 2018, the single creature}} Three days later Avos Air was one of two guilds the Coalition remnant brought in as active participants against the guilds that had left, Paladins United among them.{{cite:coalition-fracture-2018-discord-private|16-18 Feb 2018, the outside help}} Nothing in the record joins the two.

## An argument over a jungle territory

The alliance also fought with its own members over war timing. On 3 February a war-leader of [[kingdom-foxes|Kingdom Foxes]] told a member of Paladins United in open channel to get out of a jungle territory his guild was already fighting for, saying she had plainly seen Kingdom Foxes was there.{{cite:coalition-under-attack-february-2018-discord-private|3 Feb 2018, the instruction}} She answered that she had been told the previous holder was leaving and had attacked before seeing anyone.{{cite:coalition-under-attack-february-2018-discord-private|3 Feb 2018, her answer}} The war-leader replied that he was the one running his guild's wars, not the person she had spoken to; other members stepped in and the argument stopped there.{{cite:coalition-under-attack-february-2018-discord-private|3 Feb 2018, the close}}

Paladins United was still a Coalition member on 3 February and walked out on the 16th.{{cite:coalition-fracture-2018-discord-private|the departing guilds, 16 Feb 2018}} This is the only friction between the two guilds inside the alliance in the fortnight, and nothing in the record joins it to the walkout.

## Not an alliance war

That the fortnight was fought by individuals and opportunists as much as by alliances is this article's reading of the four episodes above, and nobody in the period said it. It is half a picture by construction: the organised half is at [[alovilatious-treaty|the Alovilatious treaty]], and the votes that broke the alliance at [[coalition-three-maps-february-2018|its three maps]].

articles.title: Voting in the Coalition
articles.summary: Between 15 January and 8 February 2018 the Coalition recorded ten results on nine motions in its guild leaders' channel: two guilds admitted, two bids refused, two territory maps approved, a waiting rule adopted, a guild readmitted, and one motion about its own procedure. It acted on majorities it could see and wrote the count down afterwards, so several of its decisions took effect before the vote carrying them had closed.

articles.title: CoCK collapses
articles.summary: The Council of Canyon Kingdoms collapsed on 23 Nov 2019 when The Ascendancy bloc departed, two days after Titans Valor and DiamondDeities left — ending the alliance formed from Terra's victorious core just ten weeks earlier.
articles.body:
The [[Council of Canyon Kingdoms]] — CCK, or CoCK — was formed on 15 Sep 2019 by the victorious core of [[Terra]]: [[Kingdom Foxes]], [[DiamondDeities]], [[Titans Valor]], [[The Simple Ones]], [[Fantasy]], Phantom Hearts and Empire of Sindria{{cite:community-guild-timeline|15 Sep 2019 entry}}. It outlived its parent by only three weeks.

## The collapse

The end came in stages. Kingdom Foxes left at the start of November, as [[terra-falls|Terra fell]]; Phantom Hearts had already abandoned the council in early October{{cite:community-guild-timeline|2 Nov 2019 and the undated Sep–Oct 2019 entries}}. On 21 Nov 2019 Titans Valor and DiamondDeities departed, and on 23 Nov the bloc known as The Ascendancy left, collapsing the alliance{{cite:community-guild-timeline|21 and 23 Nov 2019 entries}}.

The Ascendancy was created on 27 Apr 2019{{cite:thread-265297|post #1, the community guild-timeline image}} and departed on 23 Nov{{cite:community-guild-timeline|23 Nov 2019 entry}}; its roster was never recorded.

## Aftermath

The council's fragments regrouped within days: on 1 Dec 2019 DiamondDeities, Titans Valor and The Simple Ones formed [[Horologium]], while [[Imperial]], Paladins United and Caeruleum Order had already founded [[Artemis]] on 30 Oct{{cite:community-guild-timeline|30 Oct and 1 Dec 2019 entries}}. Horologium lasted five weeks before [[diamonddeities-disbanded|DiamondDeities' disbandment]] took it down; Artemis went on to dominate 2020.

articles.title: Concordia
articles.summary: Concordia was the Wynncraft war alliance of autumn 2015, founded by the guild Validus to break the hold of Kangronomicon and Nether's Ascent on the territory map. It peaked in October 2015, was answered by the creation of Ordo Malleus on 6 November, and was declared disbanded on a forum thread two days later.

infobox.label: Peak size
infobox.value: Not recorded; four guilds took part in the October 2015 assault

articles.body:
## The record

The narrative of Concordia comes almost entirely from one partisan account, written in February 2018 by [[drew1011|Drew1011]], who fought against the alliance. Only its end has independent documentation.

## History

### Formation and growth

Validus's chief [[tangler]] began recruiting [[holders-of-le|Holders of LE]] on 5 July 2015 with, in Drew1011's summary, "many plans to revolt against Fuq & TNA and bring them down from their role as the two guilds that controlled the map"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L82–87, composed 19 Jan 2018}}. Holders of LE joined — "After a very long and diplomatic conversation with him, we joined their alliance, Concordia", Drew1011 wrote in mid-2017{{cite:the-emperial-truth|Drew1011's Emperator application essay, mid-2017}} — then left in August 2015 for Kangronomicon, and Validus declared hostilities on 16 August{{cite:drew1011-storytime|forum post by tangler, dated 16 Aug 2015, reproduced as a screenshot at L96, composed 19 Jan 2018}}.

The alliance grew through the autumn. Drew1011 called its "growth and takedown of the remnants of Legio" "completely unprecedented and unexpected"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L143, composed 19 Jan 2018}} — Legio Praetoria being the March 2015 alliance of Kangronomicon, Nether's Ascent, [[imperial|Imperial]] and KnightOfValor, which had already collapsed in mid-2015{{cite:community-guild-timeline|2015}}. The only members known by name are Validus and Historical [UEZ], led by 3zPz{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L133, L200–201}}.

### The October 2015 assault

In October 2015 around four Concordia guilds, Validus the strongest among them, attacked Kangronomicon and Nether's Ascent simultaneously{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L119–126, composed 19 Jan 2018}}. Drew1011, then leading Holders of LE as a Kangronomicon ally, wrote that he warred alone for roughly four hours because the rest of his guild was unavailable, and that the attack was repelled{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L126–129}}. A territory map he reproduces as "the aftermath of the attack" shows Holders of LE and Kangronomicon holding most of the province with Validus reduced to two tiles{{cite:drew1011-storytime|territory map reproduced as a screenshot at L129}}.

A second map, from late September or early October 2015, shows the opposite: Validus and Travellers holding the overwhelming majority of the province, Kangronomicon absent from it entirely, and Nether's Ascent's eastern block untouched{{cite:drew1011-storytime|territory map reproduced as a screenshot at L145}}. The two images are undated in themselves; the captions are Drew1011's.

### Defeat and disbandment

Concordia was answered on 6 November 2015 by the creation of [[ordo-malleus|Ordo Malleus]], seven guilds under Paladin A'renos and Dar_Krusos{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L169–179, composed 19 Jan 2018}}{{cite:forums-wynncraft-com-forums-guilds-72-prefix-id-82-order-post-date-direction-asc|Alliance-prefix thread index}}. Drew1011 attributes its defeat to Ordo's territory-assignment system, under which each member guild was given specific territories to hold: "We attacked those territories and defended them religiously, and before long Concordia gave up on touching those territories"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L197–199, composed 19 Jan 2018}}.

Historical left Concordia for Ordo Malleus, and its leader 3zPz posted a thread titled "Concordia Disbanded" on 8 November 2015; it drew 27 replies and 4,049 views, was locked, and was last posted in by Ferne on 10 November 2015{{cite:forums-wynncraft-com-forums-guilds-72-prefix-id-82-order-post-date-direction-asc|Alliance-prefix thread index}}. Drew1011 places the thread "3 days after Ordo was created", which would be the 9th — one day later{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L203, composed 19 Jan 2018}}. The disbandment was contested: "although Ezura commented on the thread and said that it had not been disbanded, that was when most people began to consider the alliance dead"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L203–204, composed 19 Jan 2018}}.

## Membership

No roster of Concordia was ever published. Two member guilds are known by name — [[validus|Validus]], its founder, and Historical [UEZ] under 3zPz{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L133, L200–201}} — and [[holders-of-le|Holders of LE]] belonged briefly in mid-2015{{cite:the-emperial-truth|Drew1011's Emperator application essay, mid-2017}}. "Around 3-4" guilds took part in the October assault{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L125, composed 19 Jan 2018}}.

## Legacy

Concordia's direct successor was [[vesta|Vesta]], created on 10 December 2015 by 3zPz "from the remnants of Concordia" and dead within a month{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L289–311, composed 19 Jan 2018}}{{cite:forums-wynncraft-com-forums-guilds-72-prefix-id-82-order-post-date-direction-asc|Alliance-prefix thread index}}. Its larger legacy is [[ordo-malleus|Ordo Malleus]], created "for the sole purpose of defeating Concordia"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L179, composed 19 Jan 2018}}, which outlived it by four months and set the pattern — assigned territories, a leader chat, admission by vote — that later war alliances of the [[early-guild-era|early guild era]] reused{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L197–199, L250–254, composed 19 Jan 2018}}. The community guild-timeline gives Concordia a single line: "Late 2015 — Concordia Wars began somewhere here"{{cite:thread-265297|post #1, DerpyEmerald24's guild-history timeline image (i.imgur.com/seklYAQ.png), 28 Jul 2020}}.

articles.summary: A Wynncraft war alliance of 2018 assembled to fight the Federation, known only from the records of the alliance it attacked. Its September offensive left the Federation's smallest guilds holding with two defenders apiece; it was finished by 15 September with every guild gone but two, and rebuilt within three days by the same leader.
