articles.title: Council of Canyon Kingdoms
articles.summary: The Council of Canyon Kingdoms (CCK or CoCK) was a Wynncraft war alliance of autumn 2019, formed on 15 Sep 2019 by seven guilds drawn from both sides of the war that had just ended. It collapsed on 23 Nov 2019 when The Ascendancy bloc departed, two days after Titans Valor and DiamondDeities left.

articles.title: Crokee
articles.summary: Founder of Profession Heaven, the profession-XP guild granted protected neutrality by both Goose and Artemis in January 2021, and the author of the rules that made that neutrality internal law.
articles.body:
Crokee founded [[profession-heaven|Profession Heaven]] [PROF], created on 20 January 2021 to hold the south-eastern Dernic profession territories and share their guild-XP boosts with any player who wanted them{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records: Profession Heaven created 20 Jan 2021}}. Five days after the guild's creation it was granted protected neutrality by both [[goose|Goose]] and [[artemis|Artemis]], then at war; no surviving public source names the brokers of that arrangement{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records: the 25 Jan 2021 Goose–Artemis protection pact (date only; brokers unrecorded)}}.

Crokee opened the guild's forum thread on 9 February 2021 and used it to write neutrality into the guild's own law. War members were required to "Keep the guild as neutral as possible towards all other guilds. No bias towards any guild", to fight only defensively — "You may NOT war to take any territory outside of SE, except for FFAs" — and to "Be able to communicate with other guilds while keeping an unbiased stance towards them"{{cite:thread-285237|post #1 (OP), thread opened 9 Feb 2021}}. Permanent members had to "agree to not have ANY affiliation with any prior major guild that held several territories over long periods of time. Meaning to resolve any potential conflicts of interest relating to other guilds", and were barred from cycling out into major guilds{{cite:thread-285237|post #1 (OP)}}.

The open-door mechanics were unusual: anyone could join as a temporary member with "no requirements... except to join the guild Discord", with no obligation to do anything guild-related, and the guild kept room for "a full server + 41 permanent members" of profession grinders{{cite:thread-285237|post #1 (OP)}}.

articles.title: Cucumber Company
articles.summary: Cucumber Company was the war alliance of the great 2022 realignment, merging the ex-Valhalla and ex-Khaos worlds into a fourteen-guild bloc formed for guild Season 5. Its roster, posted to the forum megalist on 26 June 2022, was the last public alliance roster ever; it was archived and renamed 'Smtn else' at the start of Season 8.
articles.body:
## History

### Formation
The exact formation date was never recorded. The war between [[Khaos]] and the ex-[[Valhalla]] guilds was still running in January 2022; by 8 May 2022 [[titan-times|Titan Times]] described “our first season being a part of the new Cucumber Company war alliance”{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol1|vol. 1, 8 May 2022}}, placing the founding around the start of guild Season 5 in spring 2022. The ex-Khaos and ex-Valhalla guilds stopped fighting each other and began trading territory as allies in May–June 2022.{{cite:territory-exchanges|territory_exchanges map-data analysis}}

### The last public roster
On 26 June 2022 a member (TherapueticLiz of Sins of Seedia) posted the full fourteen-guild roster to the [[the-forum-megalist|megalist]]: [[Aequitas]], [[Titans Valor]], [[Avicia]], Blacklisted, KongoBoys, Empire of Sindria, Gang of Fools, [[Kingdom Foxes]], The Clowns, Nefarious Ravens, Sins of Seedia, [[The Aquarium]], Wynn Legacy and [[Profession Heaven]].{{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #160, 26 Jun 2022}} Twelve days later the megalist's alliance section was deleted, and no public alliance roster was ever posted again.{{cite:thread-278112-p09|p9 #161, 7 Jul 2022}} Titans Valor's Discord bot consumed an alliance-claims feed built on Avicia's site code between April and December 2022, the two guilds sharing alliance infrastructure across this window.{{cite:github-com-titantimes-valor|repository commit history, Apr–Dec 2022}}

Membership shifted at the edges. IceBlue Team was a founding member that had left by 12 June 2022; Gang of Fools joined that same month;{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol3|vol. 3, 12 Jun 2022}} and Kingdom Foxes left around July 2022, when it entered sustained war with bloc guilds.{{cite:territory-exchanges|territory_exchanges map-data analysis}} Both Kingdom Foxes and Gang of Fools appear on the June roster yet fought bloc guilds in adjacent months.

### Rename
At the start of Season 8 (autumn 2022), “Cucumber was archived. The new alliance name is called Smtn else”, per Titan Times vol. 6 — the same issue that records Gang of Fools having “left and betrayed the alliance”.{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol6|vol. 6, 12 Oct 2022}} The bloc's history continues under [[smtn elf]].

## Membership
Joins are approximated to the Season 5 boundary; the roster is as of 26 June 2022.

{{alliance:Cucumber Company}}

## Legacy
Cucumber Company ended the two-bloc war era of 2021 by absorbing both sides, and its June 2022 roster post became a historical landmark by accident: the deletion of the megalist's alliance section twelve days later marks the start of the [[private-diplomacy-era|private-diplomacy era]]{{cite:thread-278112-p09|p9 #161, 7 Jul 2022}}, in which alliances ceased to be publicly recorded.

articles.title: Cucumber Company becomes Smtn else
articles.summary: At the start of Season 8 (autumn 2022) Cucumber Company was archived and renamed 'Smtn else' — as Gang of Fools left and Paladins United, The Simple Ones and TerraLune joined — then renamed 'smtn elf' for Christmas 2022 and never changed back.
articles.body:
At the start of guild Season 8, in the autumn of 2022, [[Cucumber Company]] — the fourteen-guild super-alliance of the 2022 realignment — changed its name. "Cucumber was archived. The new alliance name is called Smtn else," recorded Titans Valor's newsletter, the Titan Times, which also reported that Gang of Fools had "left and betrayed the alliance" and welcomed three new members: [[Paladins United]], [[The Simple Ones]] and TerraLune{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol6|vol. 6, 12 Oct 2022}}.

The transition came at the season boundary, around 25 September 2022{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. The membership otherwise carried over: the change was a rename, not a reformation{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol6|vol. 6, 12 Oct 2022}}.

## The second rename

For Christmas 2022 "Smtn else" became "smtn elf" — and was never renamed back{{cite:cameron-oral-history|Cameron (TAq veteran) oral testimony, fact-checked against map data}}. By 17 February 2023 a forum post was calling [[smtn-elf|smtn elf]] "unquestionably the greatest super-alliance of 2023."{{cite:thread-306790|Wynncraft forums thread 306790, 17 Feb 2023}}

Under that accidental permanent name the alliance dominated the map into 2023, until [[The Avocado split]] and [[smtn-elf-fades-away|its quiet dissolution]] that summer.

articles.title: DiamondDeities
articles.summary: Federation-era guild created on 8 April 2018 by the leadership of LE Flowers, who dissolved that guild and founded a new one the same day rather than merge into an existing member. Aesir Pact member, SOL and Terra belligerent, Council of Canyon Kingdoms member and co-founder of Horologium, it was disbanded by its leader Nitrogen2Oxygen on 8 Jan 2020, with most members regrouping as Lux Nova.

infobox.label: Founded
infobox.value: 8 Apr 2018, by the leadership of LE Flowers

articles.title: DiamondDeities disbanded
articles.summary: Nitrogen2Oxygen dissolved DiamondDeities on 8 Jan 2020, taking the Horologium alliance down with it; most remaining members regrouped as Lux Nova the next day.
articles.body:
On 8 Jan 2020 [[nitrogen2oxygen|Nitrogen2Oxygen]] dissolved [[DiamondDeities]], one of the central guilds of the post-Federation era — and took [[Horologium]] down with it, the three-guild alliance de-facto dissolving the same day. Most remaining members regrouped as Lux Nova the next day{{cite:community-guild-timeline|8–9 Jan 2020 entries}}.

## The guild's arc

DiamondDeities packed its history into under two years. It was created on 8 April 2018 by the leadership of LE Flowers, a founding-era member of [[The Federation]]{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}, who dissolved that guild and started a new one the same day rather than merge into either of the two the alliance offered them{{cite:le-flowers-to-diamond-deities-2018-discord-private|8 Apr 2018}}. On 18 Jul 2018 it was accepted into the [[Aesir Pact]]{{cite:thread-227373-p02|p2 #24, 18 Jul 2018}}, and its guilds were among the Federation's last defenders when [[the-federation-dies|the alliance fell]] that November{{cite:thread-236962|post #17, Ascended Kitten, 11 Nov 2018}}.

After the collapse it fought with [[sol|SOL]], signed the [[Treaty of Rodoroc]] with [[Kingdom Foxes]] (effective 2 Mar 2019), joined [[Terra]] for the [[Luna-Terra war]], and passed through the [[Council of Canyon Kingdoms]] into Horologium — five blocs in fourteen months{{cite:community-guild-timeline|Treaty of Rodoroc, Terra, CoCK and Horologium entries, 2019}}.

## Aftermath

Horologium's other members, [[Titans Valor]] and [[The Simple Ones]], were left allianceless as the map consolidated under [[Artemis]]. Lux Nova carried DiamondDeities' lineage onward, appearing later in [[Hestia]]{{cite:thread-278112|post #10, Pally, 2 Dec 2020}}, [[Valhalla]] and [[Vanir]]{{cite:community-guild-timeline|11 May and 28 Nov 2021 rosters}}.

articles.title: DogsAmongUs
articles.summary: DogsAmongUs [DAU] was a Wynncraft war guild of 2018, a War Syndicate member and a listed Coalition enemy that joined the Federation during the war of its founding week — and three days later became the first member to demand a region for what it had contributed. It renamed to White Lotus in August 2018.

articles.title: Drasalia
articles.summary: Member of ChinaNumberOne who drew the Goose alliance as twelve personified characters across two forum art threads in spring 2021 — the only visual record of an alliance roster in the guild community’s history.

infobox.label: Known for
infobox.value: The [[goose|Goose]] alliance fanart, 30 Mar and 6 Apr 2021

articles.body:
The captions were careful about their own limits: "Please understand that this is just my doodles of what I think the Guilds would look like if they were people. It's not representative of them by any means", and "There's a lot more and I only did the ones that I was more familiar with so I'm sorry if your guild is not on here."{{cite:thread-289196|post #1, 30 Mar 2021}} They also carry incidental political detail — TheNoLifes described as "the ones that know more about guild politics"{{cite:thread-289196|post #1, 30 Mar 2021}}, Eden as "the big bois who own a whole lotta territory", and [[avicia|Avicia]]'s claims as "currently located in the Sky Islands"{{cite:thread-289556|post #1, 6 Apr 2021}}.

Replies from Lalatera (Aequitas), ZrBence (IceBlue Team), DeathLucifer (TheNoLifes) and FrozenGalaxy (Aequitas) affirmed their guilds' membership of [[goose|Goose]]{{cite:thread-289196|posts #8, #10, #12 and #17, 30 Mar – 7 Apr 2021}}, at a time when [[the-forum-megalist|the megalist]]'s alliance column was the only other place alliances were written down.

articles.title: ElegantDeath

articles.title: Emorians

articles.title: Emorians and Avicia revolt
articles.summary: On 29 Aug 2019, after a leadership dispute, Emorians and Avicia left Luna and declared war on Imperial, spiralling into a large war over Gavel. Terra formed in the chaos, and within three weeks Luna had lost the map and collapsed.
articles.body:
## Background

[[Luna]] had [[luna-gains-full-map-control|held the entire map]] since 17 Jul 2019, when [[Avicia]] joined as the last guild standing outside it{{cite:community-guild-timeline|17 Jul 2019 entry}}. The alliance's unity did not survive the calm that followed.

## The revolt

On 29 Aug 2019, after a leadership dispute, [[Emorians]] and Avicia left Luna and declared war on [[Imperial]], Luna's core guild. The fighting spiralled into a large war over Gavel{{cite:community-guild-timeline|29 Aug 2019 entry}}{{cite:territory-exchanges|Emorians and Avicia exchanges against Imperial, Aug–Sep 2019}}. ThisIsMurica was kicked from Luna the next day for sending fighters to the rebels' side, and on 30 Aug [[Terra]] formed in the chaos, gathering Luna's enemies into a bloc{{cite:community-guild-timeline|30 Aug 2019 entries}}.

{{war-chart:Emorians|Imperial|2019-08-14|2019-10-03}}

{{map:2019-08-29|The map when the revolt began}}

## Aftermath

The revolt did not stay a revolt. Within a week it had merged into the decisive [[Luna-Terra war]]: The Simple Ones defected on 8 Sep and Terra took the map the same day; Kingdom Foxes left on the 18th and Luna collapsed{{cite:community-guild-timeline|8 and 18 Sep 2019 entries}}. Emorians' and Avicia's walkout thus began the three-week sequence that ended Luna's rule entirely.

articles.title: Emperium of Wynn
articles.summary: The Emperium of Wynn was a Wynncraft alliance founded on 21 April 2017 and dissolved that autumn, governed by an Emperator, a Shadow Advisor, a High Council and a bench of judges. By its fall, Angry_will was Emperator, Drew1011 Shadow Advisor, and Kingdom Foxes among its four remaining member guilds.

articles.title: Empire of Nemract
articles.summary: The Empire of Nemract was a political union of Wynncraft guilds headed by The Simple Ones, formed on 17 August 2020. Branded 'The Empire of Nemract ... | ILQ + Aeu' and governed by an empress and a court of titled officers, it grouped five guilds by November 2020 and was a member of Valhalla in 2021; no dissolution was ever recorded.

articles.title: Empire of Sindria
articles.summary: Wynncraft guild founded in March 2019, a founding member of the Council of Canyon Kingdoms and of the community alliances Hestia and Adonis. It fought in Valhalla, Vanir, Cucumber Company and smtn elf, and is one of the few guilds of its generation still holding territory in 2026.
articles.body:
Empire of Sindria [ESI] was created on 18 March 2019{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-empire-20of-20sindria|v3/guild response, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}. It has belonged to more community alliances than war alliances, and is among the longest-surviving map powers.

## History

### Council of Canyon Kingdoms (2019)

Within six months of its founding, ESI was one of the seven guilds that formed the [[council-of-canyon-kingdoms|Council of Canyon Kingdoms]] on 15 September 2019 out of the victorious [[Terra]] bloc, alongside [[kingdom-foxes|Kingdom Foxes]], [[DiamondDeities]], [[titans-valor|Titans Valor]], [[the-simple-ones|The Simple Ones]], [[Fantasy]] and Phantom Hearts. It stayed until the Council collapsed on 23 November{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}.

### Hestia (2020-2022)

ESI was a founding member of the community alliance [[Hestia]], described by [[paladinsorcerer|PaladinSorcerer]] in December 2020 as 'a community alliance between ANO, ESI, LXA, and PUN'{{cite:thread-278112|post #10, 2 Dec 2020}}. By 6 June 2021 the roster had grown to six guilds with [[Emorians]] and [[HackForums]], in an alliance that had 'been together for about a year now'{{cite:thread-278112-p07|p7 #140, 6 Jun 2021}}.

The guild was off the map during the [[goose-artemis-war|Goose-Artemis war]]: arguing about the [[gavel-reborn|1.20 rework]] in February 2021, ESI's _Eragon_ wrote that 'ESI currently doesn't hold territories'{{cite:thread-286375|post #3, 20 Feb 2021}}.

### Valhalla, Vanir and the 2022 realignment

After [[the-great-collapse|the Great Collapse]] of 11 May 2021 ESI joined [[Valhalla]] as a founding member, followed it into [[Vanir]] on 28 November, and remained until Vanir collapsed on 18 December{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. In the spring 2022 realignment it joined [[cucumber-company|Cucumber Company]] — appearing as '[ESI] - Empire of Sindria' on the last public alliance roster{{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #160, 26 Jun 2022}} — and carried through the rename into [[smtn-elf|smtn elf]] until that alliance's end in June 2023{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}.

### Adonis and after

As Hestia declined, ESI and [[titans-valor|Titans Valor]] founded the community alliance [[Adonis]] around May 2022; [[Avicia]] joined within weeks{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol1|vol. 1, 8 May 2022}}{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol3|vol. 3, 12 Jun 2022}}. Titans Valor's newsletter describes the arrangement in 2023 as 'a community alliance with [AVO] and [ESI] called Adonis', with ESI running item-design competitions and profession-themed games for the whole bloc{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol9|vol. 9, 25 Mar 2023}}. The relationship outlasted the war alliances entirely: ANO's newsletter records a joint ESI anniversary celebration in early 2025, 'a celebration of how long ESI has endured'{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol18|vol. 18, 13 Apr 2025}}, and another cross-guild anniversary collaboration with ESI in 2026{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol21|vol. 21, 18 May 2026}}.

As of September 2026 Empire of Sindria is at level 112 with 122 members, 69,059 recorded wars and 25 territories, under an owner who took the guild in February 2022{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-empire-20of-20sindria|v3/guild response, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}.

## Alliances

- [[council-of-canyon-kingdoms|Council of Canyon Kingdoms]] — 15 Sep – 23 Nov 2019 (founding member)
- [[Hestia]] — c. mid-2020 – Sep 2022 (community alliance){{cite:thread-278112|post #10, 2 Dec 2020}}
- [[Valhalla]] — 11 May – 28 Nov 2021
- [[Vanir]] — 28 Nov – 18 Dec 2021
- [[cucumber-company|Cucumber Company]] — 1 Apr – 25 Sep 2022{{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #160, 26 Jun 2022}}
- [[smtn-elf|smtn elf]] — 25 Sep 2022 – 30 Jun 2023
- [[Adonis]] — May 2022 onward (community alliance; co-founder){{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol1|vol. 1, 8 May 2022}}

articles.title: Espionage and infiltration
articles.summary: Infiltration, leaking and counter-intelligence in Wynncraft guild politics between 2015 and 2019. Alt accounts were the standard instrument, leadership channels leaked constantly, and the usual institutional answer to a leak was to build a smaller room rather than change who was in the larger one.

articles.title: Ex Nihilo
articles.summary: Ex Nihilo [Nih] was a Wynncraft guild created on 24 June 2018, the day its founder led a walkout from Hall of Fame. The Federation admitted it four days later; its first significant act inside the alliance was to expose another member; and two months on, its leadership and members left it to found Odysseia, leaving the guild an empty shell.

articles.title: Ezura
articles.summary: Leader of the guild Validus and founder of Concordia, the first bloc assembled against the Kangronomicon–Nether's Ascent duopoly of 2015. He contested the alliance's disbandment on the forum thread that announced it.

articles.title: Fall of Profession Heaven's neutrality
articles.summary: On 25 May 2026 KongoBoys began a sustained campaign against Profession Heaven — up to 1,700 territory exchanges a week — ending the neutral profession-XP guild's five years of protected status. Ongoing as of September 2026.
articles.body:
## Background

[[Profession Heaven]] had been a protected neutral guild since 25 Jan 2021, when [[Goose]] and [[Artemis]] jointly guaranteed its status and granted it Silent Expanse territory as a public profession-XP guild ([[Profession Heaven neutrality]]){{cite:community-guild-timeline|25 Jan 2021 entry}}. The protection carried through both alliances' successors, and Profession Heaven itself was a member of [[Cucumber Company]] and [[smtn-elf|smtn elf]] — as was KongoBoys, its future attacker{{cite:thread-278112-p08|post #160, TherapueticLiz, 26 Jun 2022}}.

## Course of the war

On 25 May 2026 KongoBoys began a sustained campaign against Profession Heaven, running as high as 1,700 territory exchanges a week — ending more than five years of neutrality{{cite:territory-exchanges|weekly capture volumes, from 25 May 2026}}. Like every conflict of the [[private-diplomacy-era|private-diplomacy era]], the war carried no declaration, no stated cause and no named coalition. The campaign is ongoing as of September 2026{{cite:territory-exchanges|KongoBoys-Profession Heaven exchanges continuing to September 2026}}.

{{war-chart:KongoBoys|Profession Heaven|2026-05-10|2026-09-02}}

{{map:2026-05-25|The map when the campaign began}}

## Aftermath

The attack closed the era's longest-standing diplomatic arrangement — the only guild ever protected by both sides of a map-wide war. Whatever caused the break between the two former smtn elf allies is unrecorded.

articles.title: Fantasy
articles.summary: Wynncraft guild of the Federation era: co-founder of Alliance Alliance and of the Aesir Pact, a Federation member until September 2018, and then the guild that fought the alliance hardest in the weeks before it collapsed.

articles.title: Fantasy turns on The Federation
articles.summary: Fantasy held assigned Federation territory until its departure was announced on 22 September 2018. It vanished from the map for a fortnight, returned in October fighting harder than it ever had, petitioned to rejoin in the middle of that fighting, and rejoined and left again on the same night, twelve days before the alliance died.

articles.title: The Federation's admissions, August 2018
articles.summary: Between 31 July and 3 September 2018 the Federation argued over, admitted and then expelled Metric, a guild whose leader had been attacking its members, on the case that an enemy taken in was one enemy fewer. It welcomed a second guild the same day it admitted the first, three and a half weeks after naming that guild among those handing territory to HackForums.

The first closed on four votes two and a half minutes after it opened; the last drew eighteen, in an alliance whose members put its size at twenty-one guilds.

articles.title: Federation admissions, March 2018
articles.summary: The Federation spent the first week of March 2018 winning a war and the second arguing about how many guilds it ought to contain. Seventeen of its guild leaders voted to admit nobody further until members had been removed, and the alliance then refused two applications in three days without either refusal mentioning the moratorium. It voted two landless members out on 12 March and did not remove them until 6 April.

articles.title: The Federation's announcements
articles.summary: The Federation carried its decisions to the whole membership in announcement channels, and its own members argued about what those announcements should say. In March 2018 members told a moderator that announcing a removal humiliated the man twice over; in September the alliance's founder confirmed he had worded an announcement so that it would not say a member had been thrown out; in October its war channel almost retaliated against a guild it had a treaty with.
articles.body:
On 1 September 2018 a member of [[the-federation|the Federation]]'s general channel read a form of words in a recent announcement and said what it meant: the phrasing pointed to a removal rather than a voluntary departure, because somebody who left was described differently.{{cite:federation-what-its-announcements-did-not-say-2018-discord-private|1 Sep 2018, the reading}} The alliance's founder confirmed that a removal was exactly what it meant.{{cite:federation-what-its-announcements-did-not-say-2018-discord-private|1 Sep 2018, the confirmation}} He had not been willing to write that they had left, because that was not what had happened{{cite:federation-what-its-announcements-did-not-say-2018-discord-private|1 Sep 2018, why not a departure}}, and had not been willing to say in an announcement that they had been removed, because in an announcement that would have been unkind.{{cite:federation-what-its-announcements-did-not-say-2018-discord-private|1 Sep 2018, why not a removal}} The announcement was accurate and incomplete at the same time, and was made so on purpose. It is one announcement and its author's account of writing it.

## Whether to announce it at all

The alliance had argued six months earlier about whether a removal should be published. On 5 March 2018 a moderator of the Federation's Discord announced a member's removal in the general channel and said he had enjoyed carrying it out.{{cite:federation-what-its-announcements-did-not-say-2018-discord-private|5 Mar 2018, the announcement}} Other members answered him in the same channel. They accepted that the person had been disruptive and that the removal was warranted{{cite:federation-what-its-announcements-did-not-say-2018-discord-private|5 Mar 2018, the removal accepted}}, but said that publicising it humiliated him further, that it made the alliance look bad, and that the removal by itself had already made the point.{{cite:federation-what-its-announcements-did-not-say-2018-discord-private|5 Mar 2018, the objections}} Server access as a sanction is at [[guild-community-and-institutions|guild community and institutions]].

## An announcement its members had not read

The channels could also carry more than the membership knew. On 2 October 2018 a member of the war channel asked who had just attacked a territory in Cinfras county and identified Minerva [Min] as the attacker; another concluded that a treaty had been broken and that retaliation should follow.{{cite:federation-what-its-announcements-did-not-say-2018-discord-private|2 Oct 2018, the alarm}} About thirteen minutes later the same channel had it the other way round: Minerva was assisting rather than attacking, and the arrangement with it stood.{{cite:federation-what-its-announcements-did-not-say-2018-discord-private|2 Oct 2018, the reversal}} A member directed the channel to the announcements, where it had been set down.{{cite:federation-what-its-announcements-did-not-say-2018-discord-private|2 Oct 2018, the arrangement located}} The alliance had announced that treaty the day before, giving its terms only by reference to the one [[titans-valor|Titans Valor]] had held.{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|10/1/2018}} Publication was not the same as the membership knowing, which is drawn here from this one morning.

Minerva's standing in the weeks before the treaty is at [[federation-who-was-an-ally-september-2018|who was an ally]].

articles.title: Attacking allies in the Federation, April–June 2018
articles.summary: The Federation had told itself in March 2018 that taking an ally's territory was the shortest road out of the alliance. Four more member-on-member attacks followed between April and June, and none of them reached the voting channel: each was closed by the offending guild's own leadership, in the room where the complaint was made, in minutes or hours.

articles.title: Attacking an ally, March 2018
articles.summary: Every Federation member could recite the rule that you did not take an ally's territory, and in March 2018 the alliance applied it once. A guild that was not a member took a member's city and settled it by private treaty; the alliance's subguild law was invented in a chat channel and contradicted within the hour; a guild leader refused to be ordered to stop defending an ally; and the only case the alliance handled end to end was an accident.

articles.title: Federation ballots, April–June 2018
articles.summary: The Federation was decisive about admissions and irresolute about expulsions through the quietest quarter of its life. Twenty of the twenty-one motions its voting channel carried between April and June 2018 still hold their reactions; the alliance gave every ballot a fixed lifetime of about a day in a vote that carried ten to nothing, and edited three motions after they had gone up — one of them at the minute a guild was being negotiated off the list that motion named.

infobox.label: Motions
infobox.value: 21 in the voting channel, 20 with reactions

infobox.label: Threshold
infobox.value: Two thirds on admissions, never stated on a motion

articles.body:
## Twenty-one motions in ninety days

Twenty-one motions went to [[the-federation|the Federation]]'s voting channel between 2 April and 30 June 2018, and twenty of them carry the reactions the guild leaders left on them.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|the voting channel, 2 Apr – 30 Jun 2018}}

Admissions were settled quickly and by wide margins. [[emorians|Emorians]] carried twelve to two on 11 April, Angelic eleven to nothing on the 12th and TheNoLifes ten to three on 3 May.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|the admission motions of Apr and May 2018}} Verinian Trials carried seventeen to one on 25 June and [[ex-nihilo|Ex Nihilo]] eleven to three on the 29th.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|the admission motions of 25 and 29 Jun 2018}} The two that failed failed by more: [[aphelion|Aphelion]] by one vote to fourteen on 10 April, and a guild that applied on 29 June after attacking a member's assigned land that morning, by two to fourteen.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|the Aphelion and 29 Jun admission motions}}

The expulsion motions are the opposite. The one of 4 April, which asked whether to remove the guilds that had never claimed the territory assigned to them, drew twelve for expelling all those it named, three for expelling some, one for expelling none and four abstentions, from twenty accounts; it is described at [[the-federation-april-2018|the Federation in April 2018]].{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|the inactivity motion's reactions, 4 Apr 2018}} Nine days later a motion to expel [[titans-valor|Titans Valor]] and Kasai Shinrai together with the leader they shared did not so much fail as dissolve: thirteen of twenty accounts abstained and four backed removal against three opposing it.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|the expulsion motion of 13 Apr 2018}} On 4 May the same expulsion was put again with one of the two guilds dropped from the charge, and carried fourteen to one with four abstentions.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|the expulsion motion of 4 May 2018}} Nothing was set down about what had changed between the two beyond the narrowing of the target.

## A ballot with a lifetime

On 4 May 2018 the alliance voted to give every ballot a fixed and reasonable limit — twenty-four hours was the figure put — after which voting ended and only the marks cast by then counted. It carried ten to nothing.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|4 May 2018, the time-limit motion}} Seven weeks later the alliance applied it twice in a fortnight. The motion admitting Verinian Trials on 25 June states its own closing time in its text; and on 29 June, when a leader announced that another admission had already lost, he was told that the day was not yet up and the result could still move.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|the rule in operation, 25 and 29 Jun 2018}}

One vote per guild was the standing position and the alliance restated it unprompted. On the evening of 13 April a member told the leadership channel that there was one vote to a guild and that a leader's mark overrode a co-leader's.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|13 Apr 2018, one vote per guild}} On 29 June a guild leader watching an admission ballot asked whether the alliance counted two votes to a guild or one, and was answered with the single word.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|29 Jun 2018, the question and the answer}} The same rule and how it was policed in July are at [[federation-map-votes-2018|the Federation's map votes]].

## The threshold, worked out in the channel

Two thirds was the test applied to admissions, and it was applied by arithmetic in conversation rather than read off the motion: no admission motion of the quarter states a threshold in its own text.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|the admission motions, Apr – Jun 2018}} Fifteen minutes into the admission ballot of 29 June a leader put the guild leaders present at twenty-seven and observed that ten votes against would end it; another answered that it was already over, gave the count as seventeen guilds voting with eight against, and said the motion could not reach two thirds in favour.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|29 Jun 2018, the arithmetic in the channel}} The reactions on that motion come to two in favour and fourteen against.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|the 29 Jun admission motion's reactions}} The two are not a disagreement to be settled. The first is a count taken a quarter of an hour into a ballot the alliance's own rule kept open for a day; the second is where the marks stood when they were exported, years afterwards. A stated threshold was in any case not a standing rule, and had to be read off each motion.{{cite:alliance-governance-mechanics-discord-private|thresholds, 2016–2019}}

## How these counts were taken

The marks on a Federation motion were placed by hand before anybody voted, so a raw tally begins with reactions that were never votes.{{cite:federation-ballot-seeding-march-2018-discord-private|13 Mar 2018, the founder's account of the practice}} The figures above have every account recorded on more than one option taken out, whoever it was.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|the correction applied to the twenty motions}} That is the wider of the two corrections available: an account sitting on every option offered was a placeholder holding the marks so that others could use them, which a member said outright on 30 March 2018, while an account on two options out of three is somebody who marked one and then thought better of it.{{cite:federation-voting-machinery-march-2018-discord-private|30 Mar 2018, the explanation}} Where the two operations part, the figures here are the lower of the two.

The mover was not the placeholder. On none of the fourteen motions of March 2018 did the member who put a motion sit on every option of it{{cite:federation-voting-machinery-march-2018-discord-private|multi-option reactions across the fourteen March motions}}; the motion admitting Aphelion on 10 April 2018 is the first in the channel where one did.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|the Aphelion motion's reactions, 10 Apr 2018}} How the March ballots were assembled is at [[federation-ballots-march-2018|the Federation's ballots in March 2018]], and the correction itself at [[alliance-governance|alliance governance]].

## Three motions were edited

The motion of 4 April 2018 went up at 10:05 on the export's clock and was edited at 10:52.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|the edit stamp on the motion of 4 Apr 2018}} Across exactly that interval the leadership channel was arguing about taking LE Flowers off the list of inactive guilds, from 10:19, and at 10:52 the officer running the vote reported that he had taken it off.{{cite:federation-inactive-guilds-april-2018-discord-private|4 Apr 2018, 10:19 and 10:52}} The motion as it stands names four guilds and not LE Flowers. What an edit altered was never kept, so what the guilds were first asked to vote on and what the alliance left behind are not certainly the same document; reading the edit as the removal is this article's, and only the coincidence of the minute was set down.

The motion of 11 April admitting Emorians was edited the following evening, twenty-one hours after it went up.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|the edit stamp on the motion of 11 Apr 2018}} The motion of 17 June setting out a temporary free-for-all rule was posted at 00:01 and edited at 07:42, and its own text says it is a revision put again to close loopholes found in an earlier vote; it is at [[federation-free-for-all-territories|the free-for-all territories]].{{cite:federation-map-by-image-june-2018-discord-private|17 Jun 2018, the motion and its edit stamp}}

## From ballot to announcement

Where the alliance announced a result the announcement follows within hours. TheNoLifes was announced a member at 21:07 on 4 May.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|the TheNoLifes announcement, 4 May 2018}} The motion expelling Titans Valor alone went up at 15:49 that same day and the expulsion was announced at 20:59, five hours and ten minutes later.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|the expulsion motion and its announcement, 4 May 2018}} The readmission carried on 12 June was announced at 21:59 on the 13th.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|the readmission announcement, 13 Jun 2018}} The motion admitting Verinian Trials at 13:50 on 25 June was followed at 14:17 by an announcement carrying two departures as well as the admission — [[paladins-united|Paladins United]] and [[kingdomphoenixes|KingdomPhoenixes]] gone, Verinian Trials in — the day described at [[the-federation-june-crisis|the June crisis]].{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|the motion and the announcement of 25 Jun 2018}} The motion admitting Ex Nihilo at 13:31 on 29 June was announced at 07:19 the next morning.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-april-june-2018-discord-private|the Ex Nihilo announcement, 30 Jun 2018}} These times are the export's clock, seven hours behind the capture log.

The four maps balloted in the same quarter were pictures rather than lists: [[federation-map-votes-2018|the Federation's map votes]]. What the written allocations said is at [[federation-territory-allocations|the territory allocations]].

articles.title: The Federation's ballots, August 2018
articles.summary: The Federation worked out what would carry an admission while the vote on it was still open, settling on twelve of seventeen guilds and then subtracting a mark that had never been a vote. Two motions on the last evening of the month show why a tally has to be read one motion at a time: on the first the member who put the motion held every option, and on the second nobody held two.

infobox.label: Threshold
infobox.value: Two thirds, applied to an admission

articles.title: The Federation's ballots, July 2018
articles.summary: Twelve of the eighteen motions the Federation's voting channel carried in July 2018 were neither map ratifications nor the attempt to expel three member guilds. They include a rule about consorting with the enemy whose result cannot be read off the motion, a refusal to widen the map-drawing franchise two days after a map was ratified, a survey of the alliance's guild leaders on which seventeen chose the same middle answer, and a guild asking to have almost all of its territory taken away.

infobox.label: Threshold
infobox.value: two thirds, stated off the motion rather than on it

articles.title: The Federation's ballots, March 2018
articles.summary: The Federation voted by having its guild leaders react to marks placed on a message, and somebody had to place the marks first. In March 2018 its founder said he marked every option himself when he set a motion up, and a one-member guild answered that this was the only way it kept a vote at all. The month's motions also show the threshold argued twice in three days, a ballot with a parking option for a member who had voted twice, and one carrying no marks at all.

infobox.label: Threshold
infobox.value: Two thirds, abstentions out of the total

infobox.label: Motions
infobox.value: 14 in the voting channel; 7 with an account on more than one option

articles.title: Choosing Targets in the Federation, March 2018
articles.summary: For the first week of March 2018 the Federation picked and dropped its enemies by asking in its war channel and being answered within the minute. The same channel served as its territory ledger, because the alliance had no automated capture record before the end of the month, and a request to lend a warrer between two member guilds was refused in it outright.
articles.body:
## Ask the channel

[[the-federation|The Federation]] acquired its apparatus over the course of March 2018 — a voting channel on the 7th{{cite:federation-funbari-onsen-admission-march-2018-discord-private|the voting channel's creation, 7 Mar 2018}}, a territory committee on the 25th{{cite:federation-map-making-march-2018-discord-private|25 Mar 2018, the two channels}} — and for the first week of the month it had none of it.

Targets were authorised on request. On the afternoon of 1 March 2018 a member asked the war channel whether the alliance was allied with the guild Prius Power; a senior member answered that it was not and told him to wipe them out, and he said he was attacking.{{cite:federation-choosing-targets-march-2018-discord-private|1 Mar 2018, the first target}} Six minutes later the same member asked what should be done about Kasai Shinrai [Two], which TheNoLifes [TNL] was destroying, and was told to take out TheNoLifes instead.{{cite:federation-choosing-targets-march-2018-discord-private|1 Mar 2018, the second target}} Two questions and two answers settled the war aims of an alliance of twenty guilds in under seven minutes.

De-listing did not require the alliance either. On the evening of 3 March the war channel recorded that TheNoLifes had surrendered — not to the Federation but to its member guild [[sins-of-seedia|Sins of Seedia]] — and had undertaken to stop attacking.{{cite:federation-choosing-targets-march-2018-discord-private|3 Mar 2018, the surrender}} In the same exchange a member said [[house-of-sentinels|House of Sentinels]] had not even fought back, and that he was removing them completely from what he was tracking.{{cite:federation-choosing-targets-march-2018-discord-private|3 Mar 2018, the guild dropped}} That was one member's working list and not a decision of the alliance, which took no view of either guild that week.

## The channel as ledger

The Federation had no automated capture feed until 30 March 2018, so for most of the month its only account of ground changing hands was somebody typing it in.{{cite:federation-choosing-targets-march-2018-discord-private|the hand-typed reports, March 2018}} On the morning of 2 March a [[kingdom-foxes|Kingdom of Foxes]] officer checked with a member of another guild whether the guild holding the city of Cinfras was the guild it appeared to be, was told it was, and typed the transfer into the channel by hand.{{cite:federation-choosing-targets-march-2018-discord-private|2 Mar 2018, the transfer typed in}} In the same minutes members said [[necronomicon|Necronomicon]] [Feq] was finished and should be swept, and that Sins of Seedia was already doing it.{{cite:federation-choosing-targets-march-2018-discord-private|2 Mar 2018, Necronomicon}}

The enemies of the week reached the record the same way. Members named Cryo Stasis repeatedly on 28 February and 1 March as attacking inside member guilds' territories, one asking outright whether it was allied{{cite:federation-choosing-targets-march-2018-discord-private|28 Feb 2018, whether Cryo Stasis was allied}} and another asking for help fighting it off.{{cite:federation-choosing-targets-march-2018-discord-private|1 Mar 2018, the call for help}}

## Lending a warrer

The argument about concentrating or spreading the alliance's strength was also an argument about lending people, and it was refused. On 5 March 2018 the leader of [[hall-of-fame|Hall of Fame]] told the leadership channel that Kingdom of Foxes had enough members, that the alliance gained fewer territories overall when it did not share them, and asked why Fox's strongest warrer could not join another guild for an hour.{{cite:federation-choosing-targets-march-2018-discord-private|5 Mar 2018, the request}} The Fox leader refused, saying he would not donate the alliance's best warrer.{{cite:federation-choosing-targets-march-2018-discord-private|5 Mar 2018, the refusal}} A member observed in the same conversation that the alliance had been dragging guilds into itself out of nowhere.{{cite:federation-choosing-targets-march-2018-discord-private|5 Mar 2018, the aside}} What the Corkus campaign had cost Hall of Fame by that day is at [[hall-of-fame|Hall of Fame]], and the rule against attacking the alliance's own members, stated in the war channel the following day, at [[federation-attacking-allies-march-2018|attacking allies in March 2018]].

The alliance's leader recorded on 1 March 2018 that tagging a guild had set off a flame war in the Kingdom of Foxes Discord, that he had not known that could happen, and that it was over by the time he wrote.{{cite:federation-choosing-targets-march-2018-discord-private|1 Mar 2018, the flame war}} Nine weeks later the same channel could no longer reconstruct which guild had overrun its members in the canyon at the start of the month.{{cite:federation-choosing-targets-march-2018-discord-private|May 2018, the guild nobody could name}} Nothing either conversation says settles which guild that was.

articles.title: The Federation era
articles.summary: The year 2018 in Wynncraft guild warfare: the Coalition Civil War, the rise of the Federation under Drew1011, its 8-month-and-25-day hold on the entire territory map, and its one-day collapse on 10 November 2018.

infobox.label: Key events
infobox.value: [[coalition-civil-war|Coalition Civil War]], [[the-wipe-of-hackforums|The wipe of HackForums]], [[the-federation-dies|The Federation dies]]

articles.body:
{{map:2018-06-01|The Federation's map at midsummer 2018}}

The Federation era is the first fully recorded period of Wynncraft guild warfare — the continuous territory-exchange log begins on 3 January 2018, weeks before the era's opening crisis{{cite:territory-exchanges|continuous exchange log from 3 Jan 2018}} — and it was dominated end to end by a single alliance.

## The Coalition fractures

On 16–17 February 2018, five guilds — [[HackForums]], [[Paladins United]], House of Sentinels, [[Emorians]] and Kangronomicon — left the map-holding [[Coalition]] over map disputes and formed [[Alliance Alliance]] together with [[Fantasy]] and Necronomicon, declaring war on their former allies{{cite:thread-265297|post #1, community guild-timeline image (imgur seklYAQ), 28 Jul 2020}}. The trigger came on 16 February, when the Coalition published a guild-by-guild division of the province of Wynn; [[Drew1011]] wrote that "within an hour of announcing the map... five guilds left Coalition", which then "attacked the rest of the Coalition, and had the map before the night was over"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|part 17, composed 11 Jul 2018}}. In response the Coalition remnant merged with the remains of War Syndicate into a new alliance: the [[the-federation|Federation]], founded and led by Drew1011{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}. (The founding credit is not undisputed: Slayne wrote on 14 November 2018, "In a way, you could say that I created Fed because I (along with some others) created Double AA" — a claim to have caused the Federation by co-creating Alliance Alliance{{cite:thread-237070-p03|p3 #45, Slayne, 14 Nov 2018}}. Every other account names Drew1011 the founder.) The [[coalition-civil-war|Coalition Civil War]] ran until 19–20 March 2018, when Alliance Alliance was reduced to a single territory; the Federation had taken the map a month earlier, on 21 February{{cite:territory-exchanges|daily ownership reconstruction, 5 Feb – 10 Apr 2018}}.

## Total war, total control

Three days after forming, the Federation attacked HackForums and [[the-wipe-of-hackforums|drove it off the map]], a year after its ~350-territory peak{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. Participants dated that to 19 February 2018 and put the guild at 111 territories, but territory exchanges have it holding 96 at the start of the 19th and gaining through that day to 108 by midday; it reached zero at 18:00 UTC on the 20th, held four again by midnight and fourteen by dawn on the 22nd{{cite:territory-exchanges|HackForums holdings reconstructed from the last capture on each territory, 19-22 Feb 2018 UTC}}. The Federation's own war channel reported it cleared twice on the 20th and attacking again in between — see [[federation-war-fortnight-february-2018|the first fortnight of war]]. The Federation took Llevigar on 17–18 February, bankrupting Emorians after an attack opened by Snowythewolf of Hall of Fame; then the swamp, the Dark Forest and the Light Forest; then Aldorei overnight, taken by [[iceblue-team|IceBlue Team]]'s night shift. Drew1011 wrote that "at the very latest hours of the 19th, Snowy announced it was time to attack Hax. At the time they held 111 territoires. Less than 10 hours later, they had none."{{cite:drew1011-storytime|part 17, composed 30 Aug 2018}} His under-ten-hours figure is shorter than the under-twelve hours of other participant accounts. On 22 February 2018 the leaderboard's largest holders showed only 43 territories{{cite:thread-219744|post #1, 22 Feb 2018}} — guilds neither bloc was fighting, such as Blacklisted, drifted to the top of the table for about a day.

From 21 February the Federation held the entire map for 8 months and 25 days, with a single ~3-day interruption in early March{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}{{cite:territory-exchanges|daily ownership reconstruction, 5 Feb – 10 Apr 2018}}. On 16 April 2018 all 15 territory holders were Federation guilds, 384 territories in total, led by [[Kingdom Foxes]] with 82{{cite:pre2018-territory-snapshots|16 Apr 2018}}. The alliance grew to 37–40 member guilds{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}. Within it formed the [[Aesir Pact]] (25 March 2018) — sister guilds Fantasy, Sins of Seedia and IceBlue Team, joined by [[DiamondDeities]] in July, 'especially dedicated to Gavel'{{cite:thread-227373|post #1, OP as edited 21 Jul 2018}} — while [[Valkyrie]] persisted alongside as a community layer.

### When the map was won

The Federation's takeover came on 21 February 2018, when it held 356 of 383 territories (93%) against Alliance Alliance's 24{{cite:territory-exchanges|356 of 383 territories, 21 Feb 2018}}. That is four days after the 17 February split, close to Drew1011's "Three days after the Civil War had begun, Federation had won the map"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|part 17, composed 30 Aug 2018}}, and it fits the "8 months and 25 days" of his tribute, a span that counts back from 10 November 2018 to mid-February{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}. During the 1–5 March relapse the Federation fell to 43 territories (11%) on 3 March, with Alliance Alliance back at 308{{cite:territory-exchanges|Federation 43 of 383 territories, 3 Mar 2018}}.

The community timeline dates map control to 20 March{{cite:community-guild-timeline}}, but that date belongs to a different event: on 19–20 March Alliance Alliance fell from 72 territories to one and the Federation reached 99% of the map{{cite:territory-exchanges|Alliance Alliance from 72 territories to one, 19–20 Mar 2018}} — the elimination of the opposing bloc and the end of the war, not the day the map changed hands.

The March interruption followed a mob update that took effect on 1 March 2018, after which Alliance Alliance attacked Gavel "using broken defenses that the vast majority of players were unable to overcome". Tntdestroyd coordinated the first days of the response — Drew1011 wrote that coordination passed to himself on 3 March — and the map was retaken in full "by the 5th". Paladins United was admitted to the Federation on 7 March at Slayne's request, and House of Sentinels left Alliance Alliance on 12 March{{cite:drew1011-storytime|part 17, composed 30 Aug 2018}}. Drew1011's November tribute thanks Tntdestroyd "for fighting hard to reclaim the map back in March"{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}.

## How the bloc was run

How the bloc was governed was barely recorded. The alliance was run through a Discord-hosted council of guild leaders deciding by two-thirds majority; Drew1011's tribute thanks AurumKitsune of KingdomPhoenixes "for setting up the discord and coming up with things such as the 2/3 majority voting rule that contributed greatly to its success"{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}. The structure was not designed but inherited — the alliance "copied the exact same structure that Coalition had", Drew1011 wrote — and its name began as a joke about the Coalition's own naming{{cite:drew1011-storytime|part 17, composed 30 Aug 2018}}. Drew1011 said he had "tried to not thank co-leaders and only mention the leaders"{{cite:thread-237070-p02|p2 #35, Drew1011, 13 Nov 2018}}; the tribute's roll of credited names thus approximates who sat in that council.

Warfighting was concentrated in a smaller group still. Answering the tribute on 13 November 2018, the member Lego_DW named "the absolute gods of war this alliance created" — himself, 21(n), Goden, _Antho74_, InnerJoker, 0x7cf and snowy — as the people who "really held the alliance together in terms of war power"{{cite:thread-237070|post #18, Lego_DW, 13 Nov 2018}}. Goden, a Kingdom Foxes officer who rose from recruit to guild leader inside the era, is the only one of them recorded elsewhere.

## Fantasy's war

The era's one sustained challenge came from within, and came late. Fantasy's departure was announced on 22 September 2018 and it [[fantasy-turns-on-the-federation|fought the alliance through October]], rejoining and leaving again on the same night of the 29th{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|9/22/2018 and 10/29/2018}}. Its heaviest fortnight against member guilds was its last, and it was still fighting them in the week the alliance died{{cite:territory-exchanges|Fantasy against the 4 June 2018 assignment list, weekly, FFA excluded}}. Fantasy's earlier movement between the blocs is contested: its Alliance Alliance membership is recorded as ending on 19–20 March 2018, while Drew1011 wrote that its leader defected to the Federation mid-battle on 18 February in a deal he negotiated himself{{cite:drew1011-storytime|part 17, composed 30 Aug 2018}} — a stint boundary and a decision, measured differently. The alliance's first published territory assignment, on 21 February, gives Fantasy the mid canyon.{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|2/21/2018}}

The bloc's two-thirds voting threshold was adopted on 19–20 February 2018, days after its founding and immediately after a disputed admission vote; within six weeks it was the alliance's central political grievance and had produced its longest war.{{cite:alliance-governance-mechanics-discord-private|threshold change, 19–20 Feb 2018}}{{cite:buildcraftia-war-2018-discord-private|Federation leadership channels, March 2018}} The mechanics of that government are described at [[alliance-governance|alliance governance]].

August 2018 is the best-documented month of the era and the heaviest month of fighting in it: 41,920 territory captures, more than a quarter of the seven-month log, for a net movement of seventeen territories across the [[the-federation|Federation]]'s fourteen member guilds.{{cite:federation-august-2018-discord-private|August 2018: 41,920 captures; Federation guilds net +17}} It was neither the alliance at its height nor the alliance losing ground, but maximum exertion with almost no effect.

## The collapse

At around 3 AM EST on 10 November 2018, one guild left the Federation — and the alliance [[the-federation-dies|cascaded apart within a day]]{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}. The Hive had left a month earlier, then Odysseia; [[Imperial]]'s exit 'snowballed into a major attack on Fed together with the enemy alliance [Ent]'; Arisen followed; and after 14 hours of constant warring the Aesir guilds quit, ending the Federation{{cite:thread-236962|post #17, Ascended Kitten, 11 Nov 2018}}. The [[aesir-pact|Aesir Pact]] did not end with it: its three guilds withdrew as a bloc that morning and carried on as an alliance in their own right until they gave up the Canyon in January 2019, admitting a new member on written terms on the 17th{{cite:aesir-pact-2018-discord-private|withdrawal, admissions and dissolution, Nov 2018 – Jan 2019}}. The opposing bloc was named only as [Ent], a tag corresponding to no alliance otherwise recorded. 'What killed Federation was... internal affairs', wrote Drew1011 in his tribute three days later{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}.

The alliance's last crisis was a surplus rather than a shortage. On 30 October 2018 its leaders counted eleven member guilds where a month earlier there had been eighteen, and its map-maker told them the alliance held more territory than it could hand out: four guilds were already over forty territories and about eighty stood unassigned, and member guilds were refusing the ground they were offered.{{cite:federation-more-map-than-guilds-2018-discord-private|30 Oct 2018, the count, the figures and the refusals}} The map drawn in answer threw a whole region open because there was nobody to give it to, carried unanimously on 2 November and was never announced — see [[federation-the-last-map-2018|the Federation's last map]].{{cite:federation-more-map-than-guilds-2018-discord-private|30 Oct – 2 Nov 2018, the Ragni decision and the vote}}{{cite:federation-last-declaration-october-2018-discord-private|no announcement, 2–10 Nov 2018}}

Players outside the bloc described the era as a three-way division. Writing on the tribute thread two weeks after the collapse, one of them named the sides — "those sides being Federation and Anti-Fed, along with us neutrals of course" — and said he had respect for both.{{cite:thread-237070-p04|p4 #64, aNameless, 25 Nov 2018}}

## Aftermath

The winter of 2018–19 was an interregnum: per the community timeline, 'all guilds keep to themselves with valk owning most of Gavel'{{cite:thread-265297|post #1, community guild-timeline image (imgur seklYAQ), 28 Jul 2020}}, and Kingdom Foxes and Imperial were the top territory gainers{{cite:territory-exchanges|net territory gains, winter 2018-19}}. In the post-collapse chaos [[SOL]] was created — the alliance against which [[Luna]] would form in February 2019, opening [[the-alliance-wars-of-2019|the alliance wars of 2019]].

articles.title: The Federation explaining itself, 2018
articles.summary: Between 18 July and 31 August 2018 the Federation's members spent an unusual amount of time explaining to one another where the alliance had come from. Asked who had founded it, the leadership channel produced two answers in the same minute; asked how it would end, the general channel produced three, one of which came true ten weeks later. None of these explanations may be dated from the day it was given, and one of them is flatly wrong about a departure five weeks old.

infobox.value: the founder's serialised history, instalment of 30 Aug 2018

articles.body:
In the ten days from 18 to 27 July 2018 [[the-federation|the Federation]] renamed itself, surveyed its own guild leaders, failed to expel three member guilds and lost four.{{cite:federation-late-july-2018-discord-private|14 Jul 2018}}{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|Drew1011, 7/22/2018 and 7/25/2018}} Its channels through those days and through the August that followed carry a run of retellings of the alliance's own origins, and the retellings disagree with each other and with the dated record.{{cite:federation-origins-as-told-july-2018-discord-private|18 – 27 Jul 2018}}{{cite:federation-told-in-august-2018-discord-private|13 – 31 Aug 2018}}

## Who founded it

Asked in the leadership channel on 27 July who had founded the alliance, one member said it had been founded by the remains of the rebel [[war-syndicate|War Syndicate]] and of the [[coalition|Coalition]].{{cite:federation-origins-as-told-july-2018-discord-private|27 Jul 2018, the first answer}} Another said [[kingdom-foxes|Kingdom of Foxes]] [Fox] and [[sins-of-seedia|Sins of Seedia]] [SDU], technically, and immediately qualified how much work that word was doing.{{cite:federation-origins-as-told-july-2018-discord-private|27 Jul 2018, the second answer}} Neither was corrected. The exchange had begun with members asking whether [[imperial|Imperial]] [Imp] or Kingdom of Foxes was the alliance's senior guild, and being told it was neither.{{cite:federation-origins-as-told-july-2018-discord-private|27 Jul 2018, the question}} The dated record of the founding is at [[the-federation-founding-night|the founding night]].

Two days earlier the founder had given the other side's genealogy in three sentences, to a member who said he had lost track of the alliance names. Round Table had been the first alliance, he said, and the man who became the Federation's principal enemy was expelled from it and founded CGoW in its place.{{cite:federation-origins-as-told-july-2018-discord-private|25 Jul 2018, the lineage}} Round Table then died, and only CGoW remained.{{cite:federation-origins-as-told-july-2018-discord-private|25 Jul 2018, what was left}} It is the winning side's account of an enemy's origins and it explains a hostility rather than fixing a chronology.

## The room that governed two alliances

The most substantial of the July retellings is about a channel. On 18 July the founder described a private room shared by a small number of leaders he trusted above the rest: it had begun in the Coalition and continued for a while in the Federation.{{cite:federation-origins-as-told-july-2018-discord-private|18 Jul 2018, the private channel}} Its value, he said, was that problems could be worked through there without unsettling anybody else.{{cite:federation-origins-as-told-july-2018-discord-private|18 Jul 2018, what it was for}} It had died, he said, around the time [[buildcraftia|BuildCraftia]] [BCr] was expelled, and was so thoroughly dead that he had been able to shut it.{{cite:federation-origins-as-told-july-2018-discord-private|18 Jul 2018, when it died}}

The alliance had a room of that description. BuildCraftia's expulsion was raised in a leaders' back-channel at 19:14 UTC on 30 March 2018 and was through the voting channel and announced inside forty-six minutes, and four guilds had used the same channel that week to plan the invasion of a fifth.{{cite:federation-buildcraftia-expulsion-march-2018-discord-private|19:14 to 20:00 UTC, 30 Mar 2018}} Whether it is the room he was describing was never established; the names differ and nobody in either conversation joined them. The dates agree.

In the same conversation he named the deletion of the Coalition's Discord server as one of the most memorable days in the history of both alliances, said he had built the replacement, and said the leadership had put it back together in a single night so as not to be disorganised for long; another member said he remembered it.{{cite:federation-origins-as-told-july-2018-discord-private|18 Jul 2018, the deletion recalled}} That is a second witness to [[the-coalition-discord-deletion|an event the contemporaneous messages already establish]], and adds nothing to its date.

## Somebody else's peak

On 27 July the war channel argued about whether [[hall-of-fame|Hall of Fame]] [HoF] had ever been any good. A member said the guild's peak belonged to the end of a civil war inside the Coalition.{{cite:federation-origins-as-told-july-2018-discord-private|27 Jul 2018, the peak}} The founder agreed with him.{{cite:federation-origins-as-told-july-2018-discord-private|27 Jul 2018, the founder's agreement}} Another then found and posted a record of the first time the guild had reached first place in the territory rankings and put the date at 22 December, saying it fell during [[war-syndicate|the invasion of Gavel]], which opened on 21 December 2017.{{cite:federation-origins-as-told-july-2018-discord-private|27 Jul 2018, the ranking}}{{cite:drew1011-storytime|part 14, composed 22 Mar 2018}} No year was given in the conversation. Members remarked that the three guilds at the top of that ranking would never be seen there together again; one of them left the alliance two days later.{{cite:federation-origins-as-told-july-2018-discord-private|27 Jul 2018, the three guilds}}{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|Drew1011, 7/25/2018}}

## The instalment of 30 August

On 30 August the founder posted a long instalment of his serialised history covering 17 to 19 February 2018 — six months after the events, by the leader of the side that won them.{{cite:drew1011-storytime|part 17, composed 30 Aug 2018}} What it says about the alliance's name, its structure, its size and [[fantasy|Fantasy]]'s change of sides is at [[the-federation|the Federation]].

The chief of Hall of Fame who opened the war on [[emorians|Emorians]]' Llevigar territories fought so long that the leaders of [[the-hive|The Hive]] joined her guild in order to war for it overnight and let her sleep.{{cite:drew1011-storytime|part 17, composed 30 Aug 2018}} Kingdom of Foxes came out of the fighting with a rallying cry — "Death to the avaricious!", shouted at the start of every war, taken from something a member had said in the heat of it.{{cite:drew1011-storytime|part 17, composed 30 Aug 2018, the rallying cry}}

## The month it told its own story

On 29 August four guild leaders in the leadership channel went round the table on why their guilds existed at all. Sins of Seedia had been created only so that its members would not have to keep forming party chats to talk to one another, and its leader agreed when a member put it to him that he had spent his assets on a guild to avoid making parties.{{cite:federation-told-in-august-2018-discord-private|29 Aug 2018, Sins of Seedia}} The founder said he had created two guilds himself: a subguild of an older one that was never used, and [[foxton-legacy|Foxton Legacy]] [Eon], which proved unnecessary because he managed to buy the original Kingdom of Foxes back from its holder.{{cite:federation-told-in-august-2018-discord-private|29 Aug 2018, the founder's two guilds}} A member said [[the-divine-swords|The Divine Swords]] [DsQ] existed because its parent guild had filled up.{{cite:federation-told-in-august-2018-discord-private|29 Aug 2018, the Divine Swords}} Fantasy's leader said she had made only one guild and had run it from an alternate account because of a guild glitch.{{cite:federation-told-in-august-2018-discord-private|29 Aug 2018, Fantasy}}

A week earlier the general channel had spent ten minutes predicting how the alliance would end. Asked outright how it would die, one member answered toxicity and was told that this kills people rather than alliances.{{cite:federation-told-in-august-2018-discord-private|22 Aug 2018, the question}} A guild leader gave three routes: that their enemies would organise well enough to out-war them; that guilds would become less active until the alliance was weak; or that there would be a dramatic falling-out.{{cite:federation-told-in-august-2018-discord-private|22 Aug 2018, the three routes}} Nobody in the conversation chose between them.{{cite:federation-told-in-august-2018-discord-private|22 Aug 2018, no conclusion}} A member said it would go the way of an older alliance — slowly weaker as people drifted off for other things, and then suddenly gone; another said that alliance had died because of BuildCraftia's leader, and a fourth that it would not have fallen at all if nobody had betrayed it.{{cite:federation-told-in-august-2018-discord-private|22 Aug 2018, the older alliance}} The Federation dissolved in a single morning ten weeks later, closest to the third of the three routes.{{cite:federation-collapse-2018-discord-private|10 Nov 2018}} They were listing the obvious possibilities in the month the alliance was at its largest, which is what makes the list worth keeping rather than any accuracy in it.

## What a retelling could not get right

On 13 August a member told the general channel that Hall of Fame had been the first guild to leave the alliance.{{cite:federation-told-in-august-2018-discord-private|13 Aug 2018, the claim}} It had not. [[paladins-united|Paladins United]] removed itself on 25 June 2018, and [[titans-valor|Titans Valor]] and [[angels-of-eternal|Angels of Eternal]] were recorded as having left in the announcements channel on 22 July, three days before Hall of Fame and Verinian Trials went on the 25th.{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|Drew1011, 6/25/2018, 7/22/2018 and 7/25/2018}} The earliest of the three departures he was wrong about had been announced to the whole alliance seven weeks before he spoke, and the nearest of them three weeks.

Two smaller things said in the same fortnight carry no date at all. On 19 August a member remarked in passing that he was having flashbacks of a sixteen-hour war in which rival guilds had tried to wipe Kingdom of Foxes off the map entirely, and that the guild had survived it; nothing in the passage says when.{{cite:federation-told-in-august-2018-discord-private|19 Aug 2018, the sixteen-hour war}} On 28 August a guild leader said, in a joking exchange about people's histories, that he had once been a chief in a guild, had destroyed it and taken it over, and offered this as a lesson in guild takeovers.{{cite:federation-told-in-august-2018-discord-private|28 Aug 2018, the takeover}} Neither can be attached to an event.

How the serialised history was written, and the two passages in it that can be checked against dated announcements, are at [[guild-histories|guild histories]].

articles.title: The Federation's Founding Membership
articles.summary: Of the twenty-two guilds named in the Federation's founding territorial settlement of 21 February 2018, nine had been Coalition members and six were on the Coalition's own list of enemies. The alliance did not recruit its way from eight surviving guilds to twenty-two in five days; it changed sides with guilds it had been fighting.

articles.title: The Federation's free-for-all territories
articles.summary: The Federation kept a short list of territories that belonged to no member guild and that any of them could take from any other — the only ground inside the alliance on which its own guilds were allowed to compete. It published the list beside its territory allocation from March 2018 and amended it far more often than it published it, in a committee channel and without announcement. Two of the surviving declarations were edited after posting, so neither states the pool on its own date.

articles.title: The Federation's history, disputed inside it
articles.summary: The Federation's own past was argued over in its leadership channel while one of its founders was still writing it down. Between March and October 2018 two of its leaders gave incompatible accounts of what the alliance was and what it had succeeded, and three of them gave incompatible accounts of who had ended HackForums' hold on the map. None of the disputes was settled, and all of them were had in public by men holding office at the time.

articles.title: The Federation's last motions
articles.summary: Ten substantive motions went to the Federation's voting channel between 30 September and 2 November 2018, and the reactions on all ten survive. The procedure worked to the end — a motion, a ping, twenty-four hours, a two-thirds majority — while everything it was for went away. One motion everybody described is not in the channel, and the last two things posted there were jokes, put up after the alliance had dissolved.
