articles.body:
[[the-federation|The Federation]]'s voting channel was built in March 2018 in four days, while it was being used, and by the autumn it was the most settled thing the alliance had: a motion, a ping to the guild leaders, twenty-four hours, two-thirds.{{cite:federation-voting-machinery-march-2018-discord-private|the rule, March 2018}} Between 30 September and 2 November 2018 it carried ten motions.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|the ten motions}} Its procedure kept working while the thing it governed disappeared; saying so is this article's.

## The ten

| Motion | Tally |
|---|---|
| A treaty with Minerva, 30 Sep | 11–3 |
| Readmitting [[fantasy|Fantasy]], 11 Oct — withdrawn by its mover next day | 10–5 raw, 9–4 net |
| Fantasy again, 19 Oct: readmission, a pact, or refusal | 10 / 0 / 6 raw, 9 / 0 / 5 net |
| The application of Azeron, 22 Oct | 5–11 |
| The application of Artemis League, 23 Oct | 7–6 |
| Removing the alliance's noticeboard channel, 26 Oct | 9–2 raw, 8–1 net |
| Readmitting Fantasy for the Air Temple, 29 Oct | 13–3 raw, 12–2 net |
| Expelling [[the-divine-swords|the Divine Swords]], 30 Oct | 8–2 |
| The alliance's last territory map, 1 Nov | 11–2 raw, 10–1 net |
| A truce covering Audux, 2 Nov | 10–2 raw, 9–1 net |

The dates are as the motions were timed on the export's clock, seven hours behind UTC; the map motion falls on 2 November in the capture log's clock and is dated that way at [[federation-the-last-map-2018|the Federation's last map]].{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|the motions and their timestamps}}

A tally is not the vote as cast. It is the reactions still attached years afterwards, and reactions could be added or removed at any time, so every figure is good to about one vote.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|the tallies as exported}} The net column removes accounts sitting on every option of a motion — a placeholder holding the emoji so others can react rather than a vote. Five of the ten carry one, and on the map motion it was the mover.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|the five placeholder accounts}} On the motions of 26 and 30 October the mover reacted to one option only, which is a vote and stands.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|the movers' own marks}}

One of the ten also has a figure given at the time. On 15 October a member put the count on the Fantasy motion of the 11th at about eleven to four, and said the leadership had discussed closing it early because it had already cleared two thirds.{{cite:federation-fantasy-second-petition-october-2018-discord-private|15 Oct 2018, the count as given}} The reactions as they stand give ten to five, and nine to four with the placeholder taken out.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|11 Oct 2018, the reactions as exported}} The two were taken four days apart and measure different moments; direction and margin agree and the exact figures do not. The second petition is at [[fantasy-turns-on-the-federation|Fantasy turns on the Federation]].

## The twenty-four hours, running

The treaty with Minerva went up at 15:49 UTC on 30 September.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|30 Sep 2018, 15:49 UTC}} At 15:31 the following day a leader told the territory committee it would pass in eighteen minutes if nobody voted against it, and at 15:50 the committee recorded that it had.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|1 Oct 2018, the countdown}} The alliance announced it eight minutes later, on terms it described as the arrangement [[titans-valor|Titans Valor]] had held before: member guilds were not to attack Minerva except to reclaim their own assigned ground.{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|10/1/2018}}

## Both applicants were refused

Azeron applied on 22 October and lost by five to eleven; that afternoon a member asked in the alliance-general channel whether it had really applied, a leader said it had, and another said it had been turned down, inside seven hours of the motion going up.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|22 Oct 2018, the refusal reported}} The war channel had identified the guild as a subguild of the enemy alliance's principal guild five weeks before it applied, and had disputed the identification in the same days — see [[confederation|the Confederation]].

Artemis League applied the next evening and drew seven to six, which under the alliance's two-thirds was a defeat and not a near miss.{{cite:federation-voting-machinery-march-2018-discord-private|the two-thirds rule}} Neither guild appears in the announcements as having joined, and both announcement channels were searched from 22 October to 10 November.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|both announcement channels, 22 Oct – 10 Nov 2018}} The last guild the alliance admitted was Minerva, on 27 October.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|27–29 Oct 2018, the admission}}

## Neither membership motion produced what it was for

On 29 October the alliance voted thirteen to three, twelve to two net, to take Fantasy back in exchange for the Air Temple.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|29 Oct 2018, the motion}} The readmission was announced at 15:29 and the guild's departure at 23:12 the same evening.{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|10/29/2018}} The next afternoon it voted eight to two to expel the Divine Swords, the motion resting on that guild's warriors having left rather than on any offence.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|30 Oct 2018, the ground of the motion}} The expulsion was announced twenty-one minutes after the motion closed, at 21:24 UTC, and the territory committee was speaking of it as done forty-seven minutes later.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|30 Oct 2018, the announcement and the committee}} That guild had been discussed in committee nineteen days earlier as the alliance's most attacked and its most worn out, and the argument then was about halving its holdings.{{cite:federation-map-round-october-2018-discord-private|11–17 Oct 2018}}

## The last motion the alliance passed

It was about a member guild moving house. On 2 November a leader of [[emorians|Emorians]] proposed that Audux, the guild account Emorians was moving to, be truced with the alliance and allowed to hold that guild's assigned territory in the manner of Minerva and Titans Valor; it carried ten to two, nine to one net, and was announced the next day.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|2 Nov 2018, the truce}} The motion text carries an edit stamp nine minutes after posting, and only the revised wording came down, so what the leaders reacted to is not certainly what now stands.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|2 Nov 2018, the edit stamp}} The swap itself had been exempted from any vote a fortnight earlier — see [[alliance-governance|alliance governance]].

The map motion of the night before is the only one in the window whose mover sits on every option, and taking that placeholder out leaves ten to one rather than the flawless result a participant reported that morning.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|the map motion as exported}} Both are measurements of the same vote and both give a wide margin.

## A motion everybody describes and nobody can find

No motion to remove [[aphelion|Aphelion]] is in the voting channel, although participants speak of one and the guild resigned rather than face it. On the afternoon of 19 October members of the territory committee argued that it could not hold its ground, one asked for a kick motion and another offered to write it.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|19 Oct 2018, the committee}} At 23:46 UTC a leader said a vote was already beyond reach at six against.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|19 Oct 2018, 23:46 UTC}} At 00:09 UTC on the 20th the guild's leader announced its resignation in the announcements channel, referring to having seen the vote.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|20 Oct 2018, the resignation}} The next evening a member told the general channel that a vote to remove it had existed and that it had left before the vote ended.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|21 Oct 2018, the account of it}}

The channel, searched across the whole of October and November, holds no such motion.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|the voting channel, Oct – Nov 2018}} The six-against figure reported that night matches exactly the six reactions on the reject option of the Fantasy motion running in the same minutes.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|the 19 Oct Fantasy motion's reject column}} Either a motion was made where the record does not reach and then deleted, or the vote everyone was watching was about a different guild. Nothing settles it, and a guild left the alliance on the strength of it.

## The channel outlived the alliance by a day

At 02:56 UTC on 11 November 2018 a motion went up proposing that the alliance's founder be named Emperor of the Federation, its two options both meaning yes — eight hours and forty-eight minutes after a leader had posted in the same server that the Federation was gone.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|11 Nov 2018, 02:56 UTC}} A second joke motion followed that evening, was closed a minute later by the founder in the character of Emperor, and drew a one-word protest about suppression.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|11 Nov 2018, the second motion}} Those are the last four messages in the room where the alliance had decided everything for eight months. The collapse itself is at [[the-federation-dies|the Federation dies]].

## The office was cited in earnest ten months later

On the evening of 3 September 2019, arguing in [[terra|Terra]]'s war channel with [[titans-valor|Titans Valor]]'s leader about which of them still owned the dissolved alliance, the founder gave that imperial style as the ground of his authority over whatever remained of it.{{cite:federation-authority-claimed-september-2019-discord-private|3 Sep 2019, the office invoked}} The motion that conferred it had gone up after the alliance was already gone, and could not be voted against.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|11 Nov 2018, 02:56 UTC}}

Forty-three minutes later, at 20:26 and still in the same channel, he took it apart himself. Shown the motion, a member was told by him that both of its reaction options were affirmative, and which emoji was which — a raised thumb and a joined finger and thumb.{{cite:federation-authority-claimed-september-2019-discord-private|3 Sep 2019, 20:26, both options affirmative}} The member called the ballot fixed, and he answered that it had been entirely lawful and democratic.{{cite:federation-authority-claimed-september-2019-discord-private|3 Sep 2019, the answer}} The reading of the motion given here is the reading its own beneficiary gave it, a year and a half after the vote and within the hour in which he had leaned on it.{{cite:federation-authority-claimed-september-2019-discord-private|3 Sep 2019, the two exchanges}} The argument the office was invoked in is at [[titans-valor|Titans Valor]].

articles.title: The Federation's leadership churn, October 2018
articles.summary: The Federation is usually described as having lost guilds in its last six weeks. It was also losing the people who ran them: at least six member guilds changed, lost or temporarily handed over their leadership between the end of September and 10 November 2018, a seventh found its guild was registered to somebody who had stopped playing, and three new guilds were founded out of the churn, one of which began taking Federation territory within hours.
articles.body:
[[the-federation|The Federation]] is usually described as having lost guilds in its last six weeks. It was also losing the people who ran them, and the two are not the same thing. Reading the leadership churn as a loss of its own is this article's; nobody in the alliance set the changes side by side.

## Six guilds and their chairs

On 7 October 2018 a leader told the leadership channel that [[nethers-ascent|Nethers Ascent]] had a new leader, and had to explain to another leader who that was.{{cite:federation-leaders-changed-october-2018-discord-private|7 Oct 2018}} On the 9th the leader of Arisen said in the advisory council that his guild had a leader's seat free because one of its three had stood aside for a while, and that it ran on a three-leader system.{{cite:federation-leaders-changed-october-2018-discord-private|9 Oct 2018}} On the 11th, during the map negotiation, a member said that he and another member were temporarily leading [[aphelion|Aphelion]] in its leader's place; the guild resigned from the alliance eight days later.{{cite:federation-leaders-changed-october-2018-discord-private|11 Oct 2018}}{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|20 Oct 2018, the resignation}}

On the evening of 19 October the leader of [[paladins-united|Paladins United]] asked in the guild-leaders channel that their access to it be withdrawn, saying they were pausing that guild in order to level a different one; two hours later another member of the guild was given the leadership role in the channel.{{cite:federation-leaders-changed-october-2018-discord-private|19 Oct 2018}} On the 24th [[thenolifes|TheNoLifes]]' head of war and effective co-leader was reported as having quit, and the alliance's founder asked what had happened; on the 31st the guild's leader told the channel that the officer was back.{{cite:federation-leaders-changed-october-2018-discord-private|24 and 31 Oct 2018}} No reason for either is published here.

On the evening of 31 October an account that had been posting in the leadership channel under its own handle for weeks introduced itself there under a different name as the new leader of [[diamonddeities|DiamondDeities]], and was met with jokes.{{cite:federation-leaders-changed-october-2018-discord-private|31 Oct 2018}} It is somebody announcing a leadership change rather than an established one: the name given belonged to a person other members knew, and nothing else says the guild changed hands. That guild sat on the [[aesir-pact|Aesir Pact]]'s council through November and December.{{cite:aesir-oligarchy-founded-2018-discord-private|the council, Nov – Dec 2018}}

## A guild attached to an account

A seventh member had a stranger problem. [[emorians|Emorians]] was registered to somebody who had stopped playing, so that if that person never came back to hand over ownership the guild could not be transferred; through October it was quietly levelling a second guild, Audux [uxu], to move into.{{cite:federation-leaders-changed-october-2018-discord-private|October 2018}} The alliance agreed that the swap would need no vote{{cite:federation-guild-swap-2018-discord-private|22 Oct 2018}}, and on 2 November it voted the new account a truce and the right to hold Emorians' assigned ground — the last motion it ever passed.{{cite:federation-last-motions-2018-discord-private|2 Nov 2018, the truce}} The new account was already fighting: its first capture falls on 20 October, thirteen days before the truce.{{cite:territory-exchanges|first capture by Audux, 20 Oct 2018 11:10 UTC}} The alliance had discovered that its membership was attached to accounts rather than to people.

## Three guilds made out of the churn

On 21 October a member reported in the leadership channel that a player had left the Federation for a new guild and was attacking that member's assigned territory.{{cite:federation-leaders-changed-october-2018-discord-private|21 Oct 2018}} The log has the afternoon: from 15:38 UTC that day the new guild, Restive [xux], took forty-two territories from seven Federation member guilds, twenty-six of them from Paladins United.{{cite:territory-exchanges|Restive captures by defending guild, 21 Oct 2018 UTC, raw — the declaration of 12 Oct cannot be applied, its surviving text being a revision of 2 Nov}} By the 24th it was identifiable in a status readout at level twenty-three with a single member, and a leader remarked that its tag copied Emorians' new account.{{cite:federation-leaders-changed-october-2018-discord-private|24 Oct 2018, the readout}} Members of the war channel disagreed about where its founder had come from, one saying Emorians and the other [[kingdom-foxes|Kingdom Foxes]], and nothing chose between them.{{cite:federation-leaders-changed-october-2018-discord-private|25 Oct 2018, the disagreement}}

On 24 October an automated notice recorded the creation of Fluffy Unicorns [FuI] at 06:55 UTC with three members; its first capture followed seventeen minutes later.{{cite:federation-leaders-changed-october-2018-discord-private|24 Oct 2018, the creation notice}}{{cite:territory-exchanges|first capture by Fluffy Unicorns, 24 Oct 2018 07:12 UTC}} The notice names one person as its owner and a leader in the channel named two; which is right went unsettled.{{cite:federation-leaders-changed-october-2018-discord-private|24 Oct 2018, the owners}} One of the two had given up ownership of [[fantasy|Fantasy]] at 22:17 the previous evening, and the leader asked, half seriously, whether that meant Fantasy had stopped being a threat.{{cite:federation-leaders-changed-october-2018-discord-private|23–24 Oct 2018, the Fantasy ownership change}} It had not: the alliance voted Fantasy back in five days later and the guild was gone again the same night.{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|10/29/2018}}

## The last admission

The Federation admitted one more guild through all of this. Minerva [Min] was welcomed in the leadership channel from 23:35 UTC on 27 October and announced on the 29th as having joined on the Saturday, the 27th.{{cite:federation-leaders-changed-october-2018-discord-private|27–29 Oct 2018}} Leaders described it as a large guild; one said it had been Libertas before, which is that leader's statement and nothing else in the alliance's channels supports it; another asked whether it could war enough to sustain territory.{{cite:federation-leaders-changed-october-2018-discord-private|27–29 Oct 2018, what the leaders said}} It announced its own departure on 10 November in terms that said the departure did not mean anything.{{cite:federation-leaders-changed-october-2018-discord-private|10 Nov 2018}} It was right: the alliance [[the-federation-dies|dissolved that morning]].

## A departure that was not a founding

One item does not hold up. On 7 November a leader remarked in the leadership channel that a further member had left Emorians and set up a guild of their own, and a leader of that guild answered that the person had left it long before and that the remark was wrong.{{cite:federation-leaders-changed-october-2018-discord-private|7 Nov 2018}} No guild name appears in the exchange. What the passage supports is a remark and its correction, and nothing more.

articles.title: The Federation's Lists and Truces, February 2018
articles.summary: In its first fortnight the Federation kept an ally list and an enemy list, both maintained by one officer and amended by asking her in open channel, and members treated them as settling who could be attacked. Neither list survives. What the lists could not record was a truce, and on 24 February 2018 the alliance could not establish whether it had one.

articles.title: The Federation's map votes, 2018
articles.summary: The Federation ratified every territory map in a vote of its guild leaders before publishing it, from the two allocations of March 2018 to the four image sets of June and the six put to the channel between July and September. The five summer maps carried by seventy-five reactions to four, each drafted in a committee channel and put to a private show of reactions among the same leaders first — a count that ran as close as ten to eight.

articles.title: The Federation's member guilds, July 2018
articles.summary: The Federation's July 2018 is usually told as a story about the alliance. Underneath it the member guilds were changing hands, losing their seats in its leadership channel and disappearing, and in every recorded case the alliance found out afterwards. What a guild was worth to the people running them was put at sixty stacks of emeralds, and the price of founding one at five.

articles.title: Who was in the Federation, and who could say
articles.summary: The Federation announced every change to its membership in a dated channel, and its members still could not say who was in it. Between July and October 2018 a guild was admitted, a guild expelled for spying and three guilds lost; two months later members of the war channel could not place the month of a departure announced to all of them, and three weeks after another they were asking one another whether it had been announced at all.

infobox.label: Notice channel
infobox.value: Alliance announcements, dated and addressed to the whole membership

articles.body:
## A departure nobody could date

[[the-federation|The Federation]] told its whole membership at 11:22 in the morning on 25 July 2018 that [[hall-of-fame|Hall of Fame]] and Verinian Trials were leaving and had partnered with the opposing alliance, and that they should get ready to war.{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|Drew1011, 7/25/2018 11:22 AM}} Two months later a member of the war channel began an anecdote about it, was asked which month it had happened in, named one month, corrected himself to another and said he did not know.{{cite:federation-membership-as-remembered-2018-discord-private|24 Sep 2018, the month asked for}} He had been present for it.

A second member gave the reason the departure had mattered inside the alliance, and it is his account alone: another member guild had been preparing for weeks to leave over friction with Hall of Fame, and was overtaken when Hall of Fame went first.{{cite:federation-membership-as-remembered-2018-discord-private|24 Sep 2018, the plan that was overtaken}} He said he had been party to it.{{cite:federation-membership-as-remembered-2018-discord-private|24 Sep 2018, his part in the plan}} The guild he meant went unnamed, and no vote or notice of the plan was ever made.

## An admission fixed twice over

The alliance admitted Arisen [Ris] on 28 August 2018, and the day is fixed by its own two channels rather than by anybody's memory: the application went to the guild leaders in the voting channel that afternoon, and the admission was announced to the whole alliance at 9:54 that evening.{{cite:federation-membership-as-remembered-2018-discord-private|28 Aug 2018, the application put to the guild leaders}}{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|Drew1011, 8/28/2018 9:54 PM}}

Either side of it the informing channels carry only approximations. On the 27th the alliance's founder told the war channel that the guild's leader intended to join eventually and was helping in the meantime, and that this was why nobody was attacking it.{{cite:federation-membership-as-remembered-2018-discord-private|27 Aug 2018, the day before}} Two days after the announcement a member referred in passing to the guild as already inside.{{cite:federation-membership-as-remembered-2018-discord-private|30 Aug 2018, the guild taken as a member}} Neither remark could date the admission. Between them they bracket it.

## Two days, or three

The shortest membership the alliance ever announced ran from 30 August to 2 September 2018. It admitted Metric [Met] after a month of argument{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|Drew1011, 9/1/2018}}, announced at 8:32 on the morning of the 2nd that evidence had arisen that the guild "only joined the alliance to spy and cause internal chaos and has been removed from the alliance as a result"{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|Drew1011, 9/2/2018 8:32 AM}}, and gave the six Rymek territories it had been assigned to [[nethers-ascent|Nether's Ascent]] the following evening.{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|Drew1011, 9/3/2018 6:09 PM}} How the alliance came to admit a guild whose leader had been attacking its members is at [[federation-admissions-august-2018|the August admissions]].

Two days after the expulsion notice its own leaders disagreed about how obvious the infiltration had been. The founder told the leadership channel that the guild had been poor at concealing itself and had been present for two days; a second member said it had concealed itself well enough; a third that it had looked suspicious from the start.{{cite:federation-membership-as-remembered-2018-discord-private|4 Sep 2018, the three views}} The two days is his figure, given four days after the fact; the alliance's own notices span three. It had allotted six territories to a guild it expelled inside the week.

## A month before the council was told

Two member guilds went in the last week of August when their leaderships and active fighters walked into a new guild, [[odysseia|Odysseia]], formed on 24 August 2018. [[lunatic|Lunatic]]'s departure was clarified to the alliance on the 31st.{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|Goden, 8/31/2018 7:50 PM}} [[ex-nihilo|Ex Nihilo]]'s never was.{{cite:federation-lunatic-mox-departure-august-2018-discord-private|both announcement channels, 20 Aug – 15 Sep 2018}}

The alliance's advisory council had the change explained to it on 22 September, four weeks later. A member told the council that the two guilds were no longer in the alliance because they had merged into a third, and that the successor should not become a serious threat; he had to correct his own spelling of one of the two tags in the middle of it.{{cite:federation-membership-as-remembered-2018-discord-private|22 Sep 2018, the explanation to the council}} Two other members answered that both predecessor guilds had in any case been effectively abandoned before the merger.{{cite:federation-membership-as-remembered-2018-discord-private|22 Sep 2018, the answer given}}

## Finished, or merged

The alliance announced on 22 September 2018 that [[fantasy|Fantasy]] was no longer in the Federation and had "merged into SDU kinda".{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|9/22/2018}} That is a merger and not an ending, and the guild went on acting afterwards — [[fantasy-turns-on-the-federation|it attacked the alliance in October]].

Two days after the notice, members of the war channel described the guild as finished and put its holding at about ten territories.{{cite:federation-membership-as-remembered-2018-discord-private|24 Sep 2018, the guild called finished}}

Three weeks after that, members of the same channel were still asking one another when the guild had left and whether the departure had been announced at all. They were told that it had been, some time ago.{{cite:federation-membership-as-remembered-2018-discord-private|15 Oct 2018, the question asked again}}

## What a notice did and did not do

The alliance's notices were written and dated and went to the whole membership, and it issued one for every change above but a single departure.{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|7/25, 8/28, 8/31, 9/1, 9/2, 9/3 and 9/22/2018}} Not one of the conversations that followed them gave a date. Reading the two runs against each other is this article's: a broadcast channel made a record, and the interval before the membership knew what was in it ran to weeks.

articles.title: The Federation's purge proposal, 2018
articles.summary: Between 30 August and 4 September 2018 the Federation debated suspending the rule that its member guilds did not attack one another, for a fixed period in which the whole territory map would be open. Its founder refused, saying the event would finish with half the alliance's leaders disliking one another, and the motion lost without a guild in favour. The leaders settled instead that two guilds could arrange such a thing between themselves.

articles.title: Reading the Enemy, February 2018
articles.summary: In the last ten days of February 2018 the Federation worked out who its enemies were from the game's map alone, and produced two accusations of currency duplication, three conclusions that guilds had joined the other side, one decision to leave a guild alone and a judgement that an opponent was going broke. None of it was settled, and exactly one member argued back.

infobox.label: Times
infobox.value: Alliance clock, eight hours behind UTC

articles.title: Southern Corkus, August 2018
articles.summary: The Federation readmitted Paladins United on 22 August 2018, and a leader of the guild told the leadership channel three days later that several guilds had given it to understand it would have the southern half of Corkus almost at once. He would not name them. The answer he was given was that a guild joins on the conditions in force when it joins, and the map gave his guild the ocean islands instead.

articles.title: Federation Territory Allocations
articles.summary: The Federation wrote a complete guild-by-guild division of the map out in words six times between 21 February and 4 June 2018, and from 16 June published it as region images instead, roughly weekly through the summer. The four written allocations of 21 February to 22 April show its ground concentrating into a handful of guilds, and they were disputed from the week they began; the last publication of the series, on 10 September, is a census of the whole map.

articles.title: The Federation's territory committee
articles.summary: The channel that drew the Federation's territory map, created on 25 March 2018 in the week its map fights produced an invasion and an expulsion, and running to the alliance's last month. Between 6 and 16 September 2018 it acquired a drawing tool, a canvass of the member guilds and a way to reject a map, and lost both of the people who built them inside a fortnight. No office was ever created for the work.

infobox.label: Threshold
infobox.value: Two thirds of member guild leaders

articles.title: The Federation's last map
articles.summary: The Federation's final territory map was drawn against a surplus. On 30 October 2018 the alliance counted eleven member guilds where a month earlier it had counted eighteen, and its map-maker told the leaders there was more territory than there were guilds to hold it. The answer was to stop assigning: a whole region was thrown open because nobody could be given it. The map carried unanimously on 2 November and was never announced.

articles.title: The Federation under attack, July 2018
articles.summary: In July 2018 the Federation stopped being the alliance that chose whom to attack. Its smaller guilds were being retaken within a quarter of an hour, one guild's officer was bought for thirty liquid emeralds, and its own leadership counted almost forty territories in enemy hands by the 18th and thirty-seven by the 30th. A guild it had refused admission took ten territories in three days, six of them on ground the alliance had itself declared open.

articles.title: The Federation's war effort, September 2018
articles.summary: In September 2018 the Federation held the whole territory map and could not get its guilds to fight for it. Member guilds were wiped one at a time, a midnight call for help went unanswered, and the guild doing about a quarter of the alliance's fighting was told to war less.
articles.body:
In September 2018 [[the-federation|the Federation]] still held the territory map and had held it since February. What it could not do that month was field its member guilds. Reading the episodes below as one failure of attendance rather than a run of separate defeats is this article's; each of them was recorded on its own.

## A quarter of the alliance's wars

On 11 September 2018 members of the [[kingdom-foxes|Kingdom of Foxes]] complained in the war channel that their share of the alliance's territorial losses was out of proportion to their war effort. The alliance's map-maker answered that they should war less and that nobody forced the guild to fight as much as it did.{{cite:federation-nobody-came-september-2018-discord-private|11 Sep 2018, war less}} Allies had lately been warring more to help one another, he added, so it was not as though the guild carried the alliance entirely.{{cite:federation-nobody-came-september-2018-discord-private|11 Sep 2018, allies helping}} The alliance's founder replied that the guild still did about a quarter of the wars of the whole alliance, and confirmed the figure when asked whether he meant that month.{{cite:federation-nobody-came-september-2018-discord-private|11 Sep 2018, the quarter}} Its Viceroy had put the same fraction to the leadership channel two days earlier, in an argument about the map.{{cite:federation-territory-committee-2018-discord-private|9 Sep 2018}}

The capture log bears it out. Across September the guilds named in the alliance's published assignments made 20,202 captures, and Kingdom Foxes made 3,857 of them — about a fifth of the total, and more than any other member guild.{{cite:territory-exchanges|captures by Federation assignment-list guilds, 1–30 Sep 2018 UTC, raw: 20,202 total, Kingdom Foxes 3,857, Odysseia 3,280}} The figure is raw. No free-for-all ground can be taken out of a September 2018 count: the declaration in force at the start of the month was borne on a map image whose territory names were never written out, and the text of the declaration that replaced it on the 8th is a revision made on the 11th of a pool that was altered twice in committee inside two days and again later without announcement.{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|Viaire, 8/30/2018 10:28 AM and 9/8/2018 1:46 AM}}{{cite:free-for-all-amendments-2018-2019-discord-private|the edit audit, 11 Sep 2018}} Both proportions above would fall if it could.

Asked why the guild was no longer consistently first as it once had been, one of its members answered that they were caring less.{{cite:federation-nobody-came-september-2018-discord-private|11 Sep 2018}} On the measure the log offers it was still first, and first on the whole map: no guild in the game made more captures that month.{{cite:territory-exchanges|top attackers server-wide, 1–30 Sep 2018 UTC, raw: Kingdom Foxes 3,857, Odysseia 3,280, HardcoreGamerzThree 2,478}} What its members were ranking themselves on was not stated.

## Wiped one at a time

On 3 September the map-maker reported in the war channel that a member guild was being wiped.{{cite:federation-nobody-came-september-2018-discord-private|3 Sep 2018}} The following evening a member who asked why an attacking guild had twenty territories was told it was because it had wiped that guild and another member.{{cite:federation-nobody-came-september-2018-discord-private|4 Sep 2018}} On 16 September a member reported that [[imperial|Imperial]] had been wiped, and one of that guild's own members said five guilds or more were attacking them.{{cite:federation-nobody-came-september-2018-discord-private|16 Sep 2018}} On the 19th, as members watched a guild's holdings collapse, its representative said it had been wiped earlier that evening by three named guilds and could not fight for the free-for-all territories.{{cite:federation-nobody-came-september-2018-discord-private|19 Sep 2018}} That is four wipes of member guilds reported inside seventeen days, all of them from the Federation's own war channel. Members read it as the method they had watched the [[confederation|Confederation]] use all summer — concentrating on one guild at a time rather than spreading the effort — and nothing written on the other side survives to say whether that is how it was meant.

The log gives the scale of two of them. [[the-divine-swords|The Divine Swords]] lost 342 territories in the first six days of September and took 342 back, to and from twenty-two different attacking guilds.{{cite:territory-exchanges|The Divine Swords captures and losses, 1–6 Sep 2018 UTC, raw}} Imperial lost 155 on 16 September alone, to sixteen.{{cite:territory-exchanges|Imperial losses by attacking guild, 16 Sep 2018 UTC, raw}} Five guilds or more was an understatement.

The alliance was counting the same pressure itself, and publishing the count. Its weekly update for the nine days to 1 September put the fighting at 15,120 wars; the update covering the following eight days put it at 8,741, its author hoping aloud that the opposing bloc was slowing down.{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|Drew1011, 9/1/2018 and 9/9/2018 weekly updates}}

## Nobody was warring

On the evening of 17 September the map-maker asked in the war channel whether anybody could join his guild for a while to help hold off an attacker. He was fighting alone, he said, and they were defending with a thousand mobs.{{cite:federation-nobody-came-september-2018-discord-private|17 Sep 2018, evening}} Two and a half hours later the alliance's founder pinged the war role: [[titans-valor|Titans Valor]] needed help, it was fighting the opposing alliance and it was genuinely on its own.{{cite:federation-nobody-came-september-2018-discord-private|17 Sep 2018, the war-role ping}} One member said he could not help for four hours.{{cite:federation-nobody-came-september-2018-discord-private|17 Sep 2018, the one answer}} At one minute past midnight the founder pinged the role again and wrote that not a single guild was warring.{{cite:federation-nobody-came-september-2018-discord-private|18 Sep 2018, 00:01}} Members gave reasons for not coming; none of them came.

Titans Valor was where the founder said it was. The six hours of pings fall across 17 and 18 September in the capture log's clock, which runs seven hours ahead of the messages, and in those two days the guild took thirty territories from [[buildcraftia|BuildCraftia]] and lost seven to it,{{cite:territory-exchanges|exchanges between Titans Valor and BuildCraftia, 17–18 Sep 2018 UTC, raw: 30 taken, 7 lost}} while losing fourteen to [[blacklisted|Blacklisted]] and thirteen to [[kingdomphoenixes|Kingdom Phoenixes]].{{cite:territory-exchanges|Titans Valor losses by attacking guild, 17–18 Sep 2018 UTC, raw: Blacklisted 14, KingdomPhoenixes 13. The declaration in force was the map-only one of 10 Sep 2018, whose territory names were never written out, so no free-for-all ground can be subtracted}} The four counts are raw; that week's open ground was never written out by name. It was fighting three guilds of the opposing bloc at once, which is what he had said.

## The defence they had asked for

In the same message in which he said he was fighting alone, the map-maker observed that his guild's assigned defence was three hundred while the attacker was using a thousand, so the territories went much faster than they needed to.{{cite:federation-nobody-came-september-2018-discord-private|17 Sep 2018}}

Those caps were the member guilds' own, and the alliance published them. Its weekly update of 1 September carried a list, compiled by a member, of what each guild wanted its territories defended with: one asked for fewer than 300 level-50 mobs, another for fewer than 500, two for no high-level mobs at all, and one for "more mobs for more money."{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|Drew1011, 9/1/2018}} The alliance spent that month arguing about how heavily allies should defend one another's land. The guilds asking for light defences knew what they were buying.

## Counting who turned up

The complaint the alliance kept making about itself was that its guilds would not fight for each other, and on 28 September 2018 a member did the obvious thing and counted. Late that evening a member associated with [[diamonddeities|DiamondDeities]] complained in the war channel that [[thenolifes|TheNoLifes]] was not helping during an attack on [[the-divine-swords|the Divine Swords]], named the territory TheNoLifes had attacked instead, and tagged that guild's members.{{cite:federation-helpfulness-tables-september-2018-discord-private|28 Sep 2018, the accusation}} TheNoLifes' representative answered that he could not be permanently available, that the call had come at an unreasonable hour for him, and that nobody was entitled to anything from him; the complainant said tagging was the only way he had of making the guild's captains aware of the alliance's warnings channel, and the territory coordinator observed that he was tagging people who were not in the server.{{cite:federation-helpfulness-tables-september-2018-discord-private|28 Sep 2018, the answer}} Forty minutes later the complainant posted three tables.{{cite:federation-helpfulness-tables-september-2018-discord-private|28 Sep 2018, the tables}}

They are the only measurement of the alliance's own war effort anybody made. Covering the preceding 168 hours, they ranked the member guilds three ways: by wars fought, by territories taken from allies — which their author offered as a rough index of how much free-for-all fighting each guild did — and by territories taken from non-allies, which he offered as a measure of helpfulness.{{cite:federation-helpfulness-tables-september-2018-discord-private|28 Sep 2018, the three rankings}} The spread on the first is the striking figure: fifteen guilds were listed, [[kingdom-foxes|Kingdom Foxes]] led it on 908 wars in the week and the smallest member had done nine, a ratio of about a hundred to one inside one alliance.{{cite:federation-helpfulness-tables-september-2018-discord-private|28 Sep 2018, the first table}} TheNoLifes, the guild being accused that night, stood sixth of the fifteen; [[titans-valor|Titans Valor]], readmitted nine days earlier, thirteenth.{{cite:federation-helpfulness-tables-september-2018-discord-private|28 Sep 2018, the placings}}{{cite:titans-valor-guild-profile-discord-private|19 Sep 2018}}

The two counts the tables give of the alliance's own size can be reconciled against the capture log. Fifteen guilds is one fewer than the sixteen on the census of 10 September; [[fantasy|Fantasy]]'s departure was announced on the 22nd and Titans Valor was readmitted on the 19th, which leaves sixteen again.{{cite:federation-allocation-september-2018-discord-private|the table of 10 Sep 2018}}{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|9/22/2018}} Over the seven days the tables covered, exactly one of those sixteen — [[aphelion|Aphelion]] — took no territory at all, and exactly one, Arisen, took territory only from fellow members.{{cite:territory-exchanges|captures by the sixteen guilds of the 10 Sep 2018 assignment list, 168 hours to 12:00 UTC 28 Sep 2018, raw: Aphelion 0, Arisen 6 of 6 from members}} The third table has fourteen guilds and Arisen is the one missing from it.{{cite:federation-helpfulness-tables-september-2018-discord-private|28 Sep 2018, the third table}} Reading the log's two zeroes as the reason for the two counts is this article's.

The log also says what the third table was worth. Ranking the same guilds over the same week by total captures and then by captures taken off non-members produces nearly the same order: the same guild is first in both, and no guild moves more than three places.{{cite:territory-exchanges|the sixteen assignment-list guilds ranked by total captures and by captures off non-members, 168 hours to 28 Sep 2018 UTC, raw: Spearman 0.96 to 0.99 depending where the seven days are placed}} A column that ranks guilds the way the activity column already does adds nothing to it, and the alliance's argument that night was about which of the two it should believe.

It was rejected on method inside the minute, by the man who had been drawing the alliance's maps until two days earlier. The territory coordinator said the third table did not measure what it claimed to: a guild that would have helped but found the territory already being reclaimed by another ally scored nothing, so the only way to raise the figure was to take territories from the allies who were already handling them, which would make reclaiming less efficient rather than more.{{cite:federation-helpfulness-tables-september-2018-discord-private|28 Sep 2018, the objection}} The compiler answered that a guild never in time on any occasion had a problem of its own, and that anyone taking territories to improve his standing would be called out for it in that channel; the coordinator agreed that he would be, and that it would do the alliance no good.{{cite:federation-helpfulness-tables-september-2018-discord-private|28 Sep 2018, the reply}} Nothing was settled.

Members were competing on participation informally at the same time. On the same night the coordinator explained that several of them had taken to putting the number of hours they had warred consecutively in brackets beside their display names, and named three others doing it.{{cite:federation-helpfulness-tables-september-2018-discord-private|28 Sep 2018, the hours in brackets}} Three days before, the war channel had answered the question of why calls to arms drew nobody: [[odysseia|Odysseia]]'s leader said only a few of those holding the war role actually helped, another said most people simply found the tag annoying, and three members in succession said they were unavailable when the calls went out.{{cite:federation-helpfulness-tables-september-2018-discord-private|25 Sep 2018}}

The verdict did not last a week. On 1 October the leader of DiamondDeities said in the same channel that he understood why his own guild did not help, having too few active players, but not why TheNoLifes did not; Odysseia's leader replied that he had never expected either of those two guilds to help and so was never angry with them.{{cite:federation-helpfulness-tables-september-2018-discord-private|1 Oct 2018}} On the 3rd, after TheNoLifes' representative offered his guild's help to anyone who asked for it, Odysseia's leader named TheNoLifes as the one guild turning out for assigned ground at all, and thanked [[emorians|Emorians]], Kingdom Foxes and [[paladins-united|Paladins United]] for covering two other areas.{{cite:federation-helpfulness-tables-september-2018-discord-private|3 Oct 2018}} Both verdicts are the same member's opinion five days apart.

Who the alliance's allies were in the week those tables measured is its own question, at [[federation-who-was-an-ally-september-2018|who was an ally]].

## Whole regions

On 24 September a Federation leader remarked in the leadership channel that [[buildcraftia|BuildCraftia]] now owned the Rodoroc territory and was taking over the Molten Heights.{{cite:federation-nobody-came-september-2018-discord-private|24 Sep 2018}}

The log has that fight, and it was smaller than the day around it. On 24 September BuildCraftia made 88 captures across the map and lost 88, of which fifteen were in the Molten Heights — Rodoroc, the Molten Heights Portal, the Active Volcano, Crater Descent, the Lava Lake Bridge and Lava Lake — contested there with [[thenolifes|TheNoLifes]], [[imperial|Imperial]], [[odysseia|Odysseia]], [[diamonddeities|DiamondDeities]], [[sins-of-seedia|Sins of Seedia]] and two guilds outside the alliance.{{cite:territory-exchanges|BuildCraftia captures and losses, 24 Sep 2018 UTC, raw: 88 taken, 88 lost, 15 of each in the Molten Heights}} The rest of its day was in Gavel and Wynn.{{cite:territory-exchanges|BuildCraftia captures by territory, 24 Sep 2018 UTC}} None of it would have counted three weeks earlier: Rodoroc, the Molten Heights Portal, the Active Volcano, Crater Descent, the Volcanic Slope and the Lava Lake Bridge had all been on the alliance's free-for-all list of 6 August and were taken off it on 8 September, leaving only Lava Lake and Molten Reach open in that region.{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|8/6/2018 and 9/8/2018 free-for-all lists}} The Molten Heights became worth fighting over eighteen days before the fight.

Given the wipes and the unanswered calls, this article reads the pressure through the second half of September as continuous. No member of the alliance recorded it in those terms.

The capture log agrees and carries the recovery further: HackForums held nothing at six in the evening UTC, four territories by midnight and fourteen by dawn on the 22nd.

articles.title: Who was an ally, September 2018
articles.summary: Through September 2018 the Federation could not tell its own members which guilds belonged to it. Members attacked allies by mistake, the published membership list was out of date, one guild's status went undefined for five days, and the treaty with an outside guild was broken inside a week. The one list the alliance could produce was its enemy list, copied out of the enemy's own Discord.
articles.body:
For an alliance whose whole business was the allocation of ground, [[the-federation|the Federation]] was poor at telling its own members who its friends were. The episodes below fall inside four weeks of September 2018; reading them as one failure is this article's.

## Attacking your own side by accident

On 4 September 2018 a member found out inside five minutes that two of the guilds he had been fighting were in the alliance with him. He asked whether Arisen [Ris] was a subguild of [[sins-of-seedia|Sins of Seedia]], corrected himself to ask whether it was in the Federation, and was told it had been for some time; he replied that he might have attacked them twice, and apologised.{{cite:federation-who-is-an-ally-september-2018-discord-private|4 Sep 2018, Arisen}} Five minutes later he asked whether [[odysseia|Odysseia]] was an ally. Two members answered in the same second, one yes and one no.{{cite:federation-who-is-an-ally-september-2018-discord-private|4 Sep 2018, the two answers}} The one who said yes led Odysseia. He said he had attacked that guild as well.{{cite:federation-who-is-an-ally-september-2018-discord-private|4 Sep 2018, the admission}} Whether the second answer was meant seriously went unsettled; the questioner acted on the confusion either way.

## The list was out of date

The alliance's members said so in the same conversation. Immediately after the exchange above, a member said somebody needed to update the alliance information list, checked, found it had in fact been updated, and then observed that [[thenolifes|TheNoLifes]] was still not on it.{{cite:federation-who-is-an-ally-september-2018-discord-private|4 Sep 2018, the list}} TheNoLifes was at that date among the alliance's most active guilds by war count: three weeks later the only measurement of member activity anybody made put it sixth of fifteen.{{cite:federation-helpfulness-tables-september-2018-discord-private|28 Sep 2018, the first table}} The document that told the alliance who belonged to it had just been revised and still left that guild out.

## No official map

Three days later a member guild took a territory from Odysseia in the belief that Odysseia was still an enemy. A member reported the capture in the general channel and said the attacking guild had thought so; Odysseia's leader answered that the territory was his guild's assigned holding and pointed the channel at the noticeboard.{{cite:federation-who-is-an-ally-september-2018-discord-private|7 Sep 2018, the capture}} When the attacking guild's representative accepted the explanation, he added that there was no official map: one had been drawn and posted, and then deleted by its maker for correction.{{cite:federation-who-is-an-ally-september-2018-discord-private|7 Sep 2018, no official map}} Which map that was went unstated. The next allocation the alliance published, on 10 September, was itself revised the day after it went up, so nothing in it describes the map as it stood on the 7th.{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|Drew1011, 9/10/2018 2:54 PM and dwIcy, 9/11/2018}}

The allocations and how they were published are at [[federation-territory-allocations|Federation territory allocations]].

## One guild nobody could place

Minerva [Min] sat on the alliance's doorstep for at least five days without a status, and the alliance's leaders and members gave incompatible accounts of it. On 22 September, when the founder proposed replacing the enemy list, a guild leader asked whether Minerva belonged on it and was told it was not an enemy.{{cite:federation-who-is-an-ally-september-2018-discord-private|22 Sep 2018, not an enemy}} On the 27th members of the war channel asked whether they were supposed to attack it and received no, then yes, then an admission that nobody knew; a member asked outright for the position to be clarified.{{cite:federation-who-is-an-ally-september-2018-discord-private|27 Sep 2018, the war channel}} Odysseia's leader answered that Minerva was not in the Federation and that there was no agreement with it, and said he could not explain why two people associated with it held roles in the alliance's Discord.{{cite:federation-who-is-an-ally-september-2018-discord-private|27 Sep 2018, the answer}} He declined to explain the roles rather than guessing at them.

A pact with the guild was voted on the day before that exchange and failed, put again, and carried on 1 October; the alliance announced a treaty with it that day and gave its terms only by reference to the one [[titans-valor|Titans Valor]] had held.{{cite:federation-admissions-2018-discord-private|26 Sep and 1 Oct 2018}}{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|10/1/2018}} Minerva was admitted as a member five weeks later, on 27 October, and left on 10 November.{{cite:federation-leaders-changed-october-2018-discord-private|27 Oct and 10 Nov 2018}}

## A treaty that lasted a week

The treaty with Titans Valor was made on 8 September and disregarded inside a week, by member guilds and then by an officer.{{cite:federation-titans-valor-treaty-september-2018-discord-private|8 Sep 2018, the motion}} On 14 September Odysseia's leader posted in the war channel that two territories had passed from Titans Valor to other guilds, and restated the treaty's terms for his own members: leave Titans Valor alone except when reclaiming assigned ground or when a territory was free for all.{{cite:federation-who-is-an-ally-september-2018-discord-private|14 Sep 2018, the two transfers}} The next morning the alliance's territory coordinator reported a third, this one to the founder's own guild, [[kingdom-foxes|Kingdom Foxes]].{{cite:federation-who-is-an-ally-september-2018-discord-private|15 Sep 2018, the third}} Whether the three were captures or hand-overs was never said.

Odysseia's leader answered that the treaty and the vote behind it had evidently been pointless, and that it had been Sins of Seedia and [[fantasy|Fantasy]] first and now Kingdom Foxes as well.{{cite:federation-who-is-an-ally-september-2018-discord-private|15 Sep 2018, pointless}} Within the same minute an officer of the alliance said he wanted a share of Titans Valor's ground.{{cite:federation-who-is-an-ally-september-2018-discord-private|15 Sep 2018, the officer}} The guild was voted back into full membership four days later.{{cite:titans-valor-guild-profile-discord-private|19 Sep 2018}}

## Help that was not wanted

Where allies did turn out, the alliance had no way of saying whose fight it was. On 26 September an argument broke out in the war channel between Odysseia's leader and a representative of [[emorians|Emorians]] over help given in an area the first had not asked for it in.{{cite:federation-who-is-an-ally-september-2018-discord-private|26 Sep 2018, the argument}} Odysseia's leader said he had asked for help elsewhere because he already held half of the region in question and did not want the enemy taking ground nobody was watching, and that the ally had taken enemy territory his own guild had been about to reclaim, which slowed the reclaim — while saying he had been grateful for the effort.{{cite:federation-who-is-an-ally-september-2018-discord-private|26 Sep 2018, the complaint}} The Emorians representative said he had been criticised for helping.{{cite:federation-who-is-an-ally-september-2018-discord-private|26 Sep 2018, the answer}} A third member mediated, said the accusation was half true, and asked directly whether Odysseia's leader had objected to being assisted; a fourth said it was genuinely irritating when an ally took a territory you were about to take, and that the only remedy was to ask them politely to stay away next time.{{cite:federation-who-is-an-ally-september-2018-discord-private|26 Sep 2018, the mediation}}

Calls to arms had gone unanswered all month{{cite:federation-nobody-came-september-2018-discord-private|17–18 Sep 2018}}; here help arrived and was a problem, because an ally reclaiming a territory took the credit and the income for it. Setting the two side by side is this article's; the alliance had no rule about who was entitled to reclaim what. Its written answer to the neighbouring question, how heavily to defend an ally's ground, is at [[allied-defence|defending an ally's territory]].

## What it could describe

The one membership list the Federation produced without difficulty that month was somebody else's. On 22 September its founder copied the successor alliance's nineteen-guild roster out of that alliance's own Discord and asked the leaders whether it could replace the enemy list in the alliance's information channel; three agreed inside the minute.{{cite:federation-who-is-an-ally-september-2018-discord-private|22 Sep 2018, the roll}} The roster is at [[confederation|the Confederation]]. That the alliance could describe the other side's membership better than its own is this article's reading; nobody in it said so.

articles.title: In-game guild alliances
articles.summary: Wynncraft guilds can register each other as allies inside the game. It is a game-mechanical status — it sets a tax rate between their territories and lets them run guild raids together — and it does not indicate a political alliance.

infobox.label: Effect
infobox.value: Ally tax rate; joint guild raids from 2026

articles.body:
Guilds have been able to set each other as allies in game since version 1.20 of 20 January 2021 (see [[the-diplomacy-update|The Diplomacy update]]){{cite:thread-281822|post #1, 20 Jan 2021}}. The status applies the ally tax rate to the other guild's territories{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-war|attack-cost formula: allied guilds are charged the ally tax}}, and from 2026 lets allied guilds run guild raids together{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-version-2-2-1|Official Wynncraft Wiki, 'Version 2.2.1' (12 Jun 2026)}} — which is what it is mainly used for.

Registering an ally requires no political alignment and is neither announced nor explained anywhere outside the game. Guilds registered as in-game allies may be rivals, and may have recently fought each other, so these records cannot be read as blocs, pacts or reconciliations, and none of the wars of [[private-diplomacy-era|the private-diplomacy era]] can be reconstructed from them.

From June 2026 the ally system produced the first records of guild relationships made by software rather than written down by a person: [[Sequoia]]'s open-source client mod began capturing the game's alliance-formed and alliance-revoked chat lines, and from 30 July 2026 snapshotting a guild's ally list to a private backend{{cite:github-com-sequoiawynncraft-sequoia-mod|commit 69fb472, 12 Jun 2026}}. The individual registrations it captured are routine and are not recorded here.

articles.title: Foxton Legacy
articles.summary: Foxton Legacy [Eon] was the guild created on 24 November 2016 to revive the Kingdom of Foxes, which had been disbanded that July. A new name and tag were needed because the Fox name and tag had already been re-registered by outsiders.

infobox.label: Queen
infobox.value: Misty, also styled Pyrias and Teumessi

articles.body:
## The record

The name Foxton Legacy is known only from [[drew1011|Drew1011]]'s retrospective account, written in February 2018; no forum thread or roster uses either the name or the tag.

## Revival

[[lovelusting|LoveLusting]] had disbanded the [[kingdom-foxes|Kingdom of Foxes]] on 2 July 2016{{cite:community-guild-timeline|2 Jul 2016 entry}}. The decision to revive it came on 21 November 2016, when LoveLusting suggested doing so "in a half joking manner"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L590–591, composed 23 Jan 2018, re-posted 26 Feb 2018}}. Drew1011 brought in Misty (Pyrias), the founder of [[house-of-sentinels|House of Sentinels]], and then [[killerfish|Killerfish]], who agreed to serve as Viceroy{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L593–598, composed 23 Jan 2018}}.

The obstacle was the guild's own name. "After Ari disbanded Fox, a few rogue Hax members recreated it with the same name and tag. Unfortunately this meant we had to create a new name and tag for the guild."{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L599–601, composed 23 Jan 2018}} The re-registration took place on 3 July 2016, the day after the disbandment{{cite:community-guild-timeline|3 Jul 2016 entry}}, and the guild registered that day is the Kingdom Foxes still listed in the Wynncraft API{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-kingdom-20foxes|created field}}.

"So, on November 24th, we created Foxton Legacy [Eon]. Foxton Legacy because Ari's name in the guild lore was Arianna Foxton, and Eon to represent that her legacy would last an Eon."{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L602–603, composed 23 Jan 2018}} The Kingdom of Foxes' handbook separates the two acts: the guild was created on 24 November 2016 and declared as [Eon] on the 25th.{{cite:gdoc-1b8e1nh_ate9h69n|Section X: Historical Timeline, Nov 2016}} Its Guild History dates the establishment to 25 November.{{cite:gdoc-1kajulcrdc0cpf1j|Nov 2016}} The dynastic name outlasted the guild name: the Kingdom of Foxes' recruitment thread still heads its leadership block "The Royal Family | House Foxton"{{cite:thread-89227|post #1}}. Misty took the title Queen of the Foxes, Drew1011 that of King — "a title that no other has obtained" — and Killerfish that of Viceroy{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L604, composed 23 Jan 2018}}.

## Recovering the name

The Fox name and tag were recovered by negotiation from the outside player who was holding them on an alt account, and returned to the guild on 3 December 2016 together with the formation of its first State Council.{{cite:guild-lineage-and-succession-discord-private|revival, November–December 2016}}{{cite:gdoc-1b8e1nh_ate9h69n|Section X: Historical Timeline, Nov–Dec 2016}}

## Mottoes

The guild banner of the revival period carried the motto "Glory to the Rightful" beneath a quartered fox-and-wing crest.

On 7 February 2017 Drew1011 stepped down as King and LoveLusting was restored{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L652, composed 15 Feb 2018}}. "We chose a new motto, one fitting of the Queen's return, and of Fox's unwillingness to die 'Forever or Nothing.'"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L663–664, composed 15 Feb 2018}}

![Guild banner on a dark navy field: a crowned, laurel-ringed shield bearing a white howling fox on an orange ground, captioned "Kingdom of Foxes" with the motto "Forever or Nothing".](/images/chronicles/storytime/29-proxy.webp)

## The end of the name

Teumessi posted the Foxton Legacy thread on 1 December 2016, and on 3 December a negotiated deal returned the original Kingdom Foxes name and tag from the [[hackforums|HackForums]] members holding them; the guild's first State Council was formed the same day.{{cite:gdoc-1b8e1nh_ate9h69n|Section X: Historical Timeline, Dec 2016}}{{cite:gdoc-1kajulcrdc0cpf1j|Dec 2016}} LoveLusting left the guild on 10 December 2016, giving up the office of Council Designer.{{cite:gdoc-1b8e1nh_ate9h69n|Section X: Historical Timeline, Dec 2016}} Writing in mid-2017, Drew1011 described his own tenure without using the name at all — "From December 2016 to February 2017, I was King of the Foxes"{{cite:the-emperial-truth|Drew1011's Emperator application essay}} — which also gives December rather than November as the start of the revival period, a month later than his 2018 narrative. Both dates are his.

articles.title: Frank Wynncraft
articles.summary: A Wynncraft YouTuber, in-game name defervesco, a member of Aequitas. His video 'Wynncraft Warring - The Long Raid' (4 August 2024) is the only narrative account of any battle of the private-diplomacy era.
articles.body:
Frank Wynncraft's channel, created on 7 March 2024{{cite:youtube-com-feeds-videos-xml-channel-id-uctvz1ej1xkenlaitgsiol3g|channel feed, published date}}, is the source of [[the-long-raid|The Long Raid]] - the only first-person account of any battle of [[private-diplomacy-era|the private-diplomacy era]].

Under the name Defervesco he joined Wynncraft's moderation team on 3 November 2022, introduced as a trial moderator alongside Fleega and Lunatic_Lady and identified in the announcement as "also known as Frank"{{cite:thread-304707|post #1, Mimo, 3 Nov 2022}}.

His upload descriptions carry a standard footer - 'my ign is defervesco', 'guild is Aequitas' - repeated across eleven of the fifteen videos published between February and May 2026{{cite:youtube-com-feeds-videos-xml-channel-id-uctvz1ej1xkenlaitgsiol3g|standing description footer, uploads of Feb-May 2026}}. Defervesco circulated the video on the Wynncraft forums on 9 August 2024: 'Aequitas's claim in sky was under siege for some time last week. Enjoy this retelling of the war!'{{cite:thread-318070|post #1, Defervesco, 9 Aug 2024}}

'Wynncraft Warring - The Long Raid' premiered on 4 August 2024{{cite:youtube-com-watch-v-rlrh14ns6ok|premiered 4 Aug 2024}}, with the description 'Join Aeq for the small guild warring experience!'{{cite:chronicle-records|section 6, video description quoted in full}}. It records a roughly week-long siege of [[Aequitas]]'s claim in the Sky province, and the guild membership is part of how the raid is told: the account is a defender's, made from inside the besieged guild, and the attacking guild was never named{{cite:chronicle-records|section 6, attacker never named in any indexed text}}.

'Wynncraft Warring' is not a series: of the channel's thirteen videos as of May 2026, exactly one carries that title; the rest are build, market, raid and update videos{{cite:chronicle-records|section 6: Frank Wynncraft channel enumeration from the Wayback capture of 8 May 2026}}.

The player does not appear in Aequitas's 135-name member roster of 3 September 2026{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-aequitas|full member roster, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}. When or whether he left the guild was never recorded.

articles.title: FrozenGalaxy

articles.body:
FrozenGalaxy opened the recruitment thread of [[aequitas|Aequitas]] [Aeq] on 3 January 2021 and bumped it through that winter{{cite:thread-280525|post #1 (OP), thread opened 3 Jan 2021; posts #4–#5, Jan 2021}}; its rank system is styled on a courtroom, with the two "Justices" of a Supreme Court at the top — "Justice Frozenman [OWNER]" and "Justice Lalatera [CHIEF]" — above Judges, Attorneys, Advocates, Jury and Witnesses{{cite:thread-280525|post #1 (OP)}}. The guild's artwork is credited to Lalatera{{cite:thread-280525|post #1 (OP)}}. Aequitas was founded on 24 November 2019{{cite:thread-280525|post #1 (OP): "Est. November 24th 2019"}}, so the January 2021 thread marked a relaunch of public recruiting rather than the guild's creation.

On 17 January 2021 he added the guild to [[the-forum-megalist|the megalist]] — "Add Aequitas to the list tyvm <3 / Lvl. 48 Community and War" — its first public listing{{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #66, 17 Jan 2021}}. By the end of March, Aequitas was inside [[goose|Goose]]; FrozenGalaxy and Lalatera were among the members replying to [[drasalia|Drasalia]]'s Goose fanart of 30 March 2021{{cite:thread-289196|posts #10 and #17, 30 Mar and 7 Apr 2021}}. Aequitas went on into [[khaos|Khaos]] and then [[cucumber-company|Cucumber Company]]{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records: Aequitas membership stints}}.

articles.title: Gavel Reborn
articles.summary: Wynncraft version 1.20, released 20 January 2021, which rebuilt territory warfare from the ground up around guild war towers, a five-resource guild economy, headquarters and taxed trade routes — and abolished territory XP, the economic basis of the alliance order that preceded it.

infobox.label: Introduced
infobox.value: Guild war towers, guild resources, headquarters and trade routes, territory taxes, guild bank, Strategist rank, 4-letter tags

infobox.label: Removed
infobox.value: Territory XP, war servers, mob-wave wars

articles.body:
Version 1.20, titled 'Gavel Reborn', was released on 20 January 2021{{cite:thread-281822|post #1 (Salted), 20 Jan 2021}}{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-version-1-20|release date}}. Alongside housing, raids and a large Gavel rework, it replaced the guild war system that had stood since [[the-guild-update|the Guild Update]] of December 2014, and is the largest single mechanical break in the history of [[territory-warfare|territory warfare]]. The full changelog had been published two months earlier, on 23 November 2020{{cite:thread-277744|post #1 (Salted), changelog published 23 Nov 2020}}.

## What changed

Wars stopped spawning waves of mobs on dedicated war servers. In their place, attackers were sent to an arena containing a 'Guild Tower' — a boss the attacking party had to defeat — which the defending guild could buff with resources and special abilities at a continuing hourly cost{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, 'Wars' section, 23 Nov 2020}}. Wars were also moved off separate servers into ordinary game worlds{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, 'Other war-related changes', 23 Nov 2020}}.

Holding land now produced five resources — emeralds, wood, ore, fish and crop. A captured territory could be designated a Headquarters, toward which surplus resources flowed territory by territory, and from which upgrades were paid outward across the empire. Guilds set tax rates on other guilds' trade routes crossing their land, could improve individual territories at an hourly cost, and could have their routes cut off by an enemy; guilds could also ally to exchange tributes at a reduced tax rate{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, 'Guild Trading Routes' and 'Diplomacy' sections, 23 Nov 2020}}{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-war|Economy, Guild Headquarters and attack-cost sections}}. Attacking a territory now cost emeralds — initially either the guild's or the attacker's own{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, 'Other war-related changes', 23 Nov 2020}}. Elsewhere the update added a guild bank, a Strategist rank able to buy tower upgrades and territory bonuses, four-letter guild tags, a territory map on the L key, and raised the cost of creating a guild to 20 LE{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-version-1-20|Changes: Guilds}}.

![Official Wynncraft promotional screenshot for 1.20 showing the in-game Territory Map: connected territories, and a tooltip for Emerald Trail held by the guild Wynncraft giving its emerald and crop production rates.](/images/chronicles/media/gavel-reborn-5e73046b.webp)

The most consequential line in the changelog was one sentence long: 'Territories no longer generate XP.'{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, 'Other war-related changes', 23 Nov 2020}}{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-version-1-20|Changes: Guilds}} XP became a purchasable per-territory bonus instead{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-version-1-20|Changes: Guilds — territory bonuses}}.

## Design intent

The changelog stated the goal plainly: to 'allow large guilds to have a stable hold of some territories without needing to play 24/7 to defend it, and also give a chance for newcomers to get started without getting instantly destroyed by a guild with 80 territories'. It also named, in advance, the problem the community would spend the next month arguing about: “We're suspecting the first major problem we'll find will be unbreakable alliances. It'll depend on how easy it is to break those alliances and how greedy allies will be.”{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, conclusion, 23 Nov 2020}}

## Reception

The update landed in the middle of the [[goose-artemis-war|Goose-Artemis war]], one day after the first written use of the name [[Goose]]{{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #71, 19 Jan 2021}}, and the warring community's response split along the lines of that war rather than settling into a single verdict.

The first sustained critique came from xMini_ of [[Aequitas]], whose thread 'The Problem With 1.20 Guild Wars' opened on 22 January 2021{{cite:thread-282635|post #1 (OP as last edited 26 Jan 2021; replies begin 22 Jan)}}. He argued that headquarters-distance timers had shut warfare down across the map — 'If we were to try and attack Lava Lake, the timer to start the war would be more than 40 minutes' — and that abolishing territory XP had killed the free-for-all fighting that sustained day-to-day warring: 'Now with the 1.20 wars, there are no FFA's as terrs no longer give xp (another dumb idea). So basically its at a point now where you aren't warring unless you're being attacked.' He also mourned the political order the rework was meant to loosen: 'mega alliances are what made warring in Wynn fun and exciting in the first place. Now that it's gone, a lot of the action and excitement is gone', and noted that subguilds — 'some subs even became their own guild, thus diversifying the warring community' — had lost their function. He wrote from inside the winning bloc: “Look at Goose right now. We have the large majority of the map.”{{cite:thread-282635|post #1 (OP as last edited 26 Jan 2021)}}

A month later _Eragon_, posting for [[empire-of-sindria|Empire of Sindria]], made the opposite argument from the losing side, in 'The Issue With 1.20 Guild Wars': that the rework had failed to break monopolies at all. 'If a mega alliance is already in control of the map then, there is no real chance for smaller guilds to ever hold a territory longer than the cool down… yesterday we were warring in Rymek, and after we had taken 4 territories, the price went up from 4096 emeralds to 24k emeralds.' He added that towers now favoured wealth — 'the only way a guild can reliably take out any guild tower medium defense or above is if that war team is equipped with mythics' — and concluded that 'the guild update shifted from repetitive wars and an environment where it was hard to establish smaller guilds on the map, to an uncreative "build meta" and an environment where it is nearly impossible to establish smaller guilds on the map'{{cite:thread-286375|post #1, 20 Feb 2021}}.

He was answered point by point by [[99loulou999]] of The Dark Phoenix, then in Goose, who defended the system as a diplomatic game rather than a military one — 'Why would a smaller guild hold a territory by themselves if guild wars are a team game where diplomacy is the key?' — and attributed the Rymek price spike to a mass assault: 'every guild in artemis except probably 4 were warring the whole desert/savanah/rymek area currently held by Rays, so its normal that after 5h of constant warring the "pity price" (which nobody understands so far) rose up.' He also recorded the tax settings the community had converged on within a month: 'everyone's tax are on 80% for non ally and 1% for ally'{{cite:thread-286375|post #2, 20 Feb 2021}}. Rothboy of [[Eden]] argued the update had worked as designed — '1.20 successfully made it easier for smaller guilds to get on the map, that was the objective all along' — citing [[idiot-co|Idiot Co]] and [[profession-heaven|Profession Heaven]] holding land under Goose, and claimed the two blocs had simply read the new system at different speeds: 'Goose understood it and got the map asap while artemis failed to understand it and adopted the strategy to wait'{{cite:thread-286375-p02|p2 #26, 20 Feb 2021}}. DeathLucifer of [[thenolifes|TheNoLifes]] dismissed the whole genre of complaint — 'Stop using small guilds as a political tool' — observing that the objectors had not raised the issue while their own side held the map{{cite:thread-286375-p02|p2 #21, 20 Feb 2021}}.

## The war-cost reversal

One criticism produced a change. [[iceresistance|IceResistance]], founder of [[titans-valor|Titans Valor]], opened 'War Costs + Balances' on 31 January 2021, arguing that the update had turned guilds into 'Wynncraft's new money sink': 'In order to participate in the new war system, your members are forced to dish out their own emeralds — as if the new 20 le guild cost wasn't bad enough.' He also argued that the option was self-defeating even for those who used it, since paying from personal emeralds bypassed timers, taxes and route planning entirely{{cite:thread-284184|post #1, thread opened 31 Jan 2021 (OP last edited 19 Feb 2021)}}. He later added a single line at the top of the post: 'UPDATE: This has been changed, and the entire system is completely free to use now.'{{cite:thread-284184|post #1, update line, by 19 Feb 2021}}

The change came in the update's sixth hotfix, which removed personal-emerald attacks, made a landless guild's first attack free, and replaced the flat cost with a scale rising from 256 emeralds at one territory to 4,096 at four or more; the same hotfix cut tower upgrade prices, set a ten-minute post-capture immunity, and required three days' guild membership before warring{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-version-1-20|Hotfix #6: Guilds}}. IceResistance returned on 24 February to argue that the surviving 'pity cost' — the escalating price charged to guilds attacking a defender that was losing land quickly — had outlived its purpose: 'With personal le warring gone, pity is obsolete.' He reported prices 'upwards 44k+, again before tax'{{cite:thread-286748|post #1, 24 Feb 2021}}.

## Consequences

By removing territory XP, 1.20 removed the thing territorial claims had been for. Under the previous system a held territory generated XP for its holder, which is what made claims worth defending and made the free-for-all hotspots worth grinding{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, 'Other war-related changes', 23 Nov 2020}}; the alliance layer of 2019 and 2020 was built on distributing and protecting that income (see [[the-alliance-wars-of-2019|the alliance wars of 2019]] and [[artemis-goose-era|the Artemis-Goose era]]). Neither camp in the February 2021 argument thought the rework had ended alliance dominance: the pro-alliance critic and the anti-monopoly critic agreed that the map was still held by a bloc, and disagreed only about whether that was a fault{{cite:thread-282635|post #1 (OP as last edited 26 Jan 2021)}}{{cite:thread-286375|post #1, 20 Feb 2021}}. Both [[Goose]] and [[Artemis]] nonetheless collapsed on the same day less than four months later, on 11 May 2021 ([[the-great-collapse|the Great Collapse]]).

The systems introduced here define the modern game: the tax-and-route economy is still the basis of the attack-cost formula{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-war|attack-cost formula and tax rates}}, the ally setting introduced in the same update became the subject of [[the-diplomacy-update|the Diplomacy update]], and patch 1.20.3 of 5 July 2021 layered [[guild-seasons|guild seasons]] on top of it. Compare [[the-economy-update|the Economy Update]] of 2019, which reshaped the player economy but left war mechanics untouched.
