articles.title: Nitrogen2Oxygen
articles.summary: Emperator of the Emperium of Wynn (2017), elected over Drew1011 by 31 votes to 30; co-leader of DiamondDeities with Icey_Diamond, and the player who disbanded that guild on 8 January 2020, ending Horologium and the alliance wars of 2019.

infobox.label: Known for
infobox.value: Emperator of the [[emperium-of-wynn|Emperium of Wynn]] (2017); disbanding [[DiamondDeities]] (8 Jan 2020)

articles.body:
Nitrogen2Oxygen's career spans the era's bookends: he led its first grand experiment in mass alliance and ended its last.

## The Emperium of Wynn

In 2017 he was Emperator of the [[emperium-of-wynn|Emperium of Wynn]], the twelve-guild alliance founded on 21 April 2017, and sat among its Judges{{cite:thread-188024|post #1, 7 May 2017: "Current Emperator - Nitrogen2Oxygen", roster and Judges}}; he still held the office on 5 September 2017{{cite:thread-202724|post #7, Aya, 5 Sep 2017, quoting the opening post}}. The office made him "the main figure head and the leader of the Emperium of Wynn… Their word is law within the alliance"{{cite:thread-202724|post #7, Aya, 5 Sep 2017, quoting the opening post}}.

He was elected to it. The only account of the election is [[drew1011|Drew1011]]'s, who ran against him and lost. Paladin A'renos announced the election on standing down, non-members of the alliance were permitted to run, and three candidates came forward: Nitrogen2Oxygen, ElegantDeath and Drew1011. ElegantDeath withdrew and became Drew1011's campaign manager; the campaign opened with a debate run on presidential lines and the vote itself ran for a week.{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L768–787, composed 26 Feb 2018}} Drew1011 recorded the result as "an astoundingly close 30-31, with Nitro as the winner"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L794 and the accompanying screenshot, composed 26 Feb 2018}}.

![The Emperium of Wynn's Emperator election announcement, posted by Paladin A'renos, with the final reaction tallies: 30 for Drew1011, 31 for Nitrogen2Oxygen.](/images/chronicles/storytime/37-image.webp)

When the election happened is unresolved. Drew1011's narrative places it in the autumn of 2017, but Nitrogen2Oxygen is already named Emperator in the alliance's May 2017 roster{{cite:thread-188024|post #1, 7 May 2017}}, so the contest belongs earlier in the year than the narrative implies. Nitrogen2Oxygen ran the poll that made Drew1011 the alliance's Shadow Advisor on 31 August 2017{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L797–798 and the accompanying screenshot, composed 26 Feb 2018}}{{cite:thread-202724|post #7, Aya, 5 Sep 2017, quoting the opening post}}. The Emperium fell on 17 October 2017; by that date the opening post named a different Emperator, Angry_will{{cite:thread-202724|post #1, as last edited 17 Oct 2017}}, and [[drew1011|Drew1011]]'s profile records a one-day Emperator title on 15-16 October 2017{{cite:forums-wynncraft-com-members-drew1011-2157|Drew1011's Wynncraft forum profile (member 2157): title chain with dates}}. How the office passed between the three was never recorded.

## DiamondDeities

He then co-led the guild [[DiamondDeities]] [DDT] with Icey_Diamond{{cite:thread-227373|post #1, leader table, 5 Jun 2018 (ed. 21 Jul 2018)}}, and Drew1011's "Federation Tribute" credited them jointly each as "a most sincere and trusted friend" of the [[the-federation|Federation]]{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}. On the forums he posted under the alias Cloud Man{{cite:thread-236962-p02|p2 #27–#28, 11 Nov 2018 (the post is quoted back as "Nitrogen2Oxygen said")}}.

On 8 January 2020 he disbanded DiamondDeities - by then a Federation and [[aesir-pact|Aesir Pact]] veteran, an apparent [[SOL]] guild, a Treaty of Rodoroc signatory alongside [[kingdom-foxes|Kingdom Foxes]], and a founder of [[Terra]], the [[Council of Canyon Kingdoms]] and [[Horologium]] (1 December 2019). The disbanding dissolved Horologium the same day and marked the end of [[the-alliance-wars-of-2019|the alliance wars of 2019]]. Most remaining members regrouped as Lux Nova the next day{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records: Community Timeline — DiamondDeities disbanded 8 Jan 2020, Lux Nova regrouping}}. His role within DDT immediately before the disbanding is not known.

articles.title: Odysseia
articles.summary: Odysseia [Oys] was a Wynncraft guild founded on 24 August 2018 when the leadership and members of Ex Nihilo and Lunatic left both to combine. It lasted about two months, announced at the end of October that it was leaving the Federation and quitting the game, and had already placed its former members inside the alliance's other guilds.

articles.title: Ordo Malleus
articles.summary: Ordo Malleus, the Order of the Hammer, was the dominant war alliance of the winter of 2015-16. Founded on 6 November 2015 by seven guilds to defeat Concordia, it held the territory map through a system of designated territories, grew to twelve member guilds by February 2016, and broke apart over three days in March 2016 after three founding guilds left in sixteen days.

infobox.label: Founded by
infobox.value: Seven guilds, organised by Paladin A'renos, then a chief of Kangronomicon

infobox.label: Stated purpose
infobox.value: "Created for the sole purpose of defeating Concordia"

infobox.label: Alliance thread
infobox.value: Thread 93754, opened by Paladin A'renos on 6 Nov 2015; 15 pages, 296 replies, locked

infobox.label: Fate
infobox.value: Collapsed over three days of departures, 9–11 Mar 2016

articles.body:
## The record

The alliance's own thread — "**-= Ordo Malleus =-**", opened by Paladin A'renos on 6 November 2015, 15 pages and 296 replies, locked, last post by Ha_Ha_Redstone on 10 March 2016 — carries its opening post in the state it stood in on 9 March 2016, the day the collapse began{{cite:thread-93754|post #1, opening post as last edited 9 Mar 2016}}, an earlier state of that post quoted back within the thread in November 2015{{cite:thread-93754-p02|p2 #25, Tapu_Fini, 10 Nov 2015, quoting the opening post}}, and the replies of its first three weeks.{{cite:thread-93754-p03|p3 #60, 23 Nov 2015}}{{cite:forums-wynncraft-com-forums-guilds-72-prefix-id-82-order-post-date-direction-asc|complete census of Alliance-prefixed threads, page 1}} [[drew1011|Drew1011]], a founding member, wrote in 2018 that the thread had been deleted and was restored on request in early 2017, and that he had used it to recover dates: "many of the dates and minor events during the Ordo parts of this story would have been educated guesses without it."{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L692–695, composed 16 Feb 2018, re-posted 26 Feb 2018}} For the alliance's internal politics the principal witness is still that retrospective account of 2018, which is partisan, was written by a party to the disputes it describes, and is in most particulars the only witness for what it reports. A separate chronology, compiled afterwards, tracks admissions, refusals, expulsions and the collapse to the minute; it dates the alliance's creation to 8 November 2015, two days after the thread's own first replies.{{cite:gdoc-1csqnkuglsisvsvx|chronology, 27 Oct 2015 – 11 Mar 2016}}

## History

### Founding, 6 November 2015

The alliance was founded on 6 November 2015 by seven guilds: Kangronomicon [Fuq] led by Dar_Krusos ("Kru"); Holders of LE [HoL] led by Drew1011; Ha Ha United [HHU] led by Ha_Ha_Redstone ("Red"); End of Everything [EoE] led by "Shadow"; Hack Forums [Hax] led by TheDarkSoul; ToastedPandas [TnP] led by Yamipanda and [[killerfish|Killerfish]]; and Sinners [Snr] led by Rani.{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L169–178, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 22 Feb 2018}} Drew1011 gave the purpose in one sentence: "Ordo Malleus was created for the sole purpose of defeating Concordia."{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L179, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 22 Feb 2018}} Glitchedslayer likewise put the alliance at seven guilds{{cite:thread-143392|post #13, Glitchedslayer, 9 Aug 2016}}; the twelve-guild roster below dates from February 2016, after five further admissions.

The opening post named Kangronomicon as the founder and gave a guild count of eight — the seven guilds and the Wynn Wide Merchants Organisation [WWMO], a trading body "led by The Three Members of Four" that was carried on the roster to the end as an unofficial member.{{cite:thread-93754-p02|p2 #25, Tapu_Fini, 10 Nov 2015, quoting the opening post}}{{cite:thread-93754|post #1, opening post as last edited 9 Mar 2016}} Paladin A'renos, styled High Grand Master of the Ordo Malleus, claimed it for himself on the thread: what mattered was not how long a thing lasted but "the experiences, the relations you acquire and the friends you make ... That is why i have created this alliance."{{cite:thread-93754-p02|p2 #22, Paladin A'renos, 9 Nov 2015}}

The alliance was assembled by **Paladin A'renos**, then a chief of Kangronomicon, who recruited the member guilds and created the leader chat, while Dar_Krusos held the senior authority; the requirement that each member guild elect a council of four officers — a Diplomat, a War Commander, a Community Manager and a Merchant — came from Kangronomicon shortly before the alliance was announced.{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L148–162, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 22 Feb 2018}}

### Governance

The alliance ran on four tiers of coordination. Above the guild councils sat a **leader chat**; a superseded earlier chat was renamed "**The Board**" and "quickly became very inactive and was almost never used"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L190, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 22 Feb 2018}}. The rename followed a manoeuvre Drew1011 described carrying out himself within weeks of the founding: he canvassed the other member-guild leaders, secured a majority, and had alliance business moved to a new leader chat that excluded Paladin A'renos, citing A'renos's manner toward the other leaders{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L186–190, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 22 Feb 2018}}. Above the leader chat, Dar_Krusos later created a top tier called the "**Shadow Government**", described as "the highest leadership tier within the alliance", whose members were Drew1011, Killerfish, Yamipanda, Ha_Ha_Redstone and Rani{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L248–257, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 22 Feb 2018}}. The opening post set out what those councils were for. War Commanders led attacks and defence and coordinated with their counterparts in the other guilds; Diplomats were "the voice of the guilds", responsible for inter-guild relations and for resolving disputes; Community Managers ran events and kept the alliance's public reputation; and Merchants kept emeralds flowing into the guild banks. Councils could be elected by members or appointed by the guild leader, and merchant and community guilds were excused the War Commander requirement.{{cite:thread-93754-p02|p2 #25, Tapu_Fini, 10 Nov 2015, quoting the opening post}} Five alliance rules ran alongside them, of which the third was "Refrain from attacking allies' territories."{{cite:thread-93754|post #1, opening post as last edited 9 Mar 2016}} General business ran through a hundred-person Skype chat{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L344, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 26 Feb 2018}}, and new members of member guilds were asked to join "the Ordo Malleus skype chats".{{cite:thread-109350|post #11, Drew1011, 20 Feb 2016, quoting the opening post}} Voting was by guild rather than by person: when Killerfish was added to the leader chat, Drew1011 checked "to make sure that TnP still only had one vote when it came time to vote on things", and was assured they did.{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L253–254, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 22 Feb 2018}} Admissions and expulsions were decided by votes of the leaders.

The mechanism by which the alliance won the territory war was a system of assigned territories. "Each guild was designated certain territories to focus, and as long as we actually succeeded in defeating Concordia, we would get to keep them… We attacked those territories and defended them religiously, and before long Concordia gave up on touching those territories," Drew1011 wrote; Holders of LE held Nesaak and Mining Base, End of Everything was given the desert, and ToastedPandas held Ternaves.{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L197–202, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 22 Feb 2018}} The opening post's own allocation, published in November 2015, differs in its details and covers the whole map: Kangronomicon took Lusuco, Ragni, the City of Troms and Rymek; Holders of LE the Savannah and Nemract; Ha Ha United Nesaak and Ternaves; End of Everything Almuj and the desert; ToastedPandas the Ocean Islands and the Nether Portal; Sinners Nivla Forest and Time Valley; and HackForums the Jungle and Detlas.{{cite:thread-93754-p02|p2 #25, Tapu_Fini, 10 Nov 2015, quoting the opening post}} The blocks were reassigned as membership changed: by the winter Holders of LE was holding sixteen named Nesaak and Mining Base territories, Ha Ha United's original allocation.{{cite:gdoc-1sqfxhjwewtphua7|"Holders Of LE — A captain's guide", designated territories}} An associated tactic governed how allied territory was recovered: a guild retaking a territory for an ally left "minuscule defenses" so the owner could take it straight back, a rule whose breach later became a grievance against HackForums.{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L336–338, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 26 Feb 2018}}

![A territory map from Drew1011's account showing Ordo Malleus at its height, with every guild holding its designated block: ToastedPandas around Detlas and Ternaves, HaHaUnited around Nemract and the savannah, Sinners in Nivla Forest, Holders of LE at Nesaak Transition and HackForums at Elkurn.](/images/chronicles/storytime/12-image.webp)

### The Concordia war and the forum campaign against Ordo

The alliance's target, [[early-guild-era|Concordia]], was effectively finished within weeks. Drew1011 recruited Historical [UEZ] out of it, and its leader 3zPz posted a thread titled "Concordia Disbanded" — dated 8 November 2015, two days after Ordo's founding rather than the three Drew1011 recalled — after which, he wrote, "most people began to consider the alliance dead", although Ezura of Validus denied it in the thread itself.{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L203–204, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 22 Feb 2018}}{{cite:forums-wynncraft-com-forums-guilds-72-prefix-id-82-order-post-date-direction-asc|complete census of Alliance-prefixed threads, page 1: "Concordia Disbanded", 3zPz, Nov 8, 2015, 27 replies, locked}}

The alliance's dominance produced a public reaction on the forums. On 28 November 2015 tangler, a chief of Validus, opened "Come Join! The Odeus Anti-Validus Pact"{{cite:forums-wynncraft-com-forums-guilds-72-prefix-id-82-order-post-date-direction-asc|census of Alliance-prefixed threads, page 1}}, a thread in which, Drew1011 wrote, it "was revealed that Arenos had tried to bribe guilds in to joining Ordo Malleus"; he qualified the allegation — "I cannot entirely recall if this was true, but I believe I remember a discussion with Arenos where he admitted to it" — and said the thread devolved into A'renos and Ezura posting screenshots of each other before a moderator closed it.{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L215–226, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 22 Feb 2018}} The moderator Mekyr made the thread's last post the following day.{{cite:forums-wynncraft-com-forums-guilds-72-prefix-id-82-order-post-date-direction-asc|complete census of Alliance-prefixed threads, page 1: "Come Join! The Odeus Anti- Validus Pact", tangler, Nov 28, 2015, last post Mekyr, Nov 29, 2015}}

The same day a thread appeared under a new account called **TheOrdoSpies**, announcing that members of the alliance were passing information to Validus. Its text was never preserved. The account was banned and the thread locked the same day, and no moderator ever disclosed whose alt it was.{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L227–232, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 22 Feb 2018}}{{cite:forums-wynncraft-com-forums-guilds-72-prefix-id-82-order-post-date-direction-asc|complete census of Alliance-prefixed threads, page 1: "Ordo Spies", TheOrdoSpies, Nov 28, 2015, locked}} Drew1011 speculated that the account belonged either to tangler or to 3zPz.{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L231, composed 22 Feb 2018}} "All this talk of spies within Ordo made many of us paranoid," he wrote, with no evidence to act on.{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L232, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 22 Feb 2018}}

Part of the rival campaign was fought with fabricated material. A thread belonging to the case against Ordo Malleus carried a quotation from the alliance's own leader that had been edited and given to the wrong speaker.{{cite:ordo-malleus-informal-power-discord-private|2015, told January 2018}} That is one participant's account, given three years afterwards, and it is the earliest instance of these alliances fighting each other on the game's public forums rather than on the map.

![The thread posted by the account "TheOrdoSpies" on 28 November 2015, claiming that Ordo Malleus members were leaking to Validus. The account was banned and the thread locked the same day.](/images/chronicles/storytime/09-image.webp)

### Admissions, expulsions and the February 2016 roster

Historical [UEZ] was welcomed into the alliance on the thread on 12 November 2015{{cite:thread-93754-p03|p3 #42, Paladin A'renos, 12 Nov 2015}}{{cite:gdoc-1csqnkuglsisvsvx|entry of 11/12/15}} and left on 1 December; on that same day End of Everything was expelled by vote for failing to hold the desert it had been assigned, its territories passing to HackForums, a boss-killing service called the **Demon Hunters** was founded, and [[libertas|Libertas]] was admitted{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L234–247, composed 22 Feb 2018}}. Death Reapers were rejected on a first application and admitted on a second days later{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L233, L255–256, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 22 Feb 2018}}; grimmcat's White Wolves were revived to join{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L258–260, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 22 Feb 2018}}; Necronomicon [Feq] was promoted from Kangronomicon subguild to full member and complained about having no assigned territories until ToastedPandas and Holders of LE donated three each{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L261–268, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 22 Feb 2018}}. Megitsune [Bri], under Amaranthe, joined about a week after Gavel's release and left on 1 February 2016, its leader disbanding the guild rather than passing it on{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L326, L362–364, composed 26 Feb 2018}}. Applications were closed after Gavel because wars had stopped working, and reopened in late January{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L329, L361, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 26 Feb 2018}}; the dated chronology puts the closure on 28 December 2015, with Megitsune's admission, and the reopening on 29 January 2016.{{cite:gdoc-1csqnkuglsisvsvx|entries of 12/28/15 and 1/29/16}} It also fixes the intake of that winter: Death Reapers refused on 29 November and admitted on 7 December, Papa Johns [PPJ] refused on 4 December, Libertas admitted on 8 December, White Wolves on 13 December, and Heroes of Wynn still applying as late as 26 February 2016. On 16 December 2015 Holders of LE and ToastedPandas each gave up three territories for Necronomicon.{{cite:gdoc-1csqnkuglsisvsvx|entries of 11/29/15 – 2/26/16}} The alliance ran a fortnightly Nether games with Lightly Toasted Heroes from 10 February 2016.{{cite:gdoc-1csqnkuglsisvsvx|entry of 2/10/16}} WynnTheory [WTh], bought by Paladin A'renos after he left Kangronomicon, was admitted on 3 February 2016 over Drew1011's objection{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L366–370, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 26 Feb 2018}}, and The No Lifes and Ultimate Xeons followed within days{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L375–376, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 26 Feb 2018}}.

On 20 February 2016 the UltimateXeons owner motoki1 posted "Update: Joined the Alliance Ordo Malleus!"{{cite:thread-109350|post #7, motoki1, 20 Feb 2016}}, and the guild's recruitment thread carried an alliance section headed by a single rule, "Don't attack the territories that ally guilds own", above twelve guilds:{{cite:thread-109350|post #11, Drew1011, 20 Feb 2016, quoting the opening post}}

| Guild | Tag |
|---|---|
| Kangronomicon | Fuq |
| Ha Ha United | HHU |
| ToastedPandas | TnP |
| TheNoLifes | TNL |
| Holders of LE | HoL |
| Wynn Theory | WTh |
| Sinners | Snr |
| White Wolves | WWA |
| Necronomicon | Feq |
| [[libertas|Libertas]] | Lir |
| Death Reapers | DxR |
| UltimateXeons | UXs |

End of Everything, Historical, Megitsune and [[hackforums|HackForums]] are absent from the list, all having left or been expelled by then.

### The expulsion of HackForums

[[hackforums|HackForums]] was expelled and later readmitted. "I think you're forgetting that Hax was actually kicked out of Ordo", Drew1011 wrote in August 2016{{cite:thread-143392|post #7, Drew1011, 9 Aug 2016}}, and earlier that summer: "Hax was one of the original guilds, although we kicked them out, and then for some reason, let them back in"{{cite:thread-133666|post #6, Drew1011, 27 Jun 2016}}. Neither remark gave a date or a reason. The expulsion fell on 7 January 2016.{{cite:gdoc-1csqnkuglsisvsvx|entry of 1/7/16}} Immediately after TheDarkSoul was banned from the forums, Drew1011 raised the ban in the Shadow Government chat as reflecting badly on the alliance, Yamipanda moved a vote, and the vote to expel was unanimous or nearly so. The stated grievances were repeated accidental attacks on allied guilds and the practice of defending recaptured allied territory with full mob defences instead of the light defences the alliance's recapture tactic required.{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L333–342, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 26 Feb 2018}} HackForums is absent from the 20 February 2016 roster{{cite:thread-109350|post #11, Drew1011, 20 Feb 2016, quoting the opening post}}, and its own recruitment thread listed a different alliance — "Astrafterí-affinity" — on 11 February 2016{{cite:thread-109319|post #13, ThePastryMaster, 11 Feb 2016, quoting the opening post}}. Paladin A'renos re-invited the guild around late February 2016.{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L435–436, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 26 Feb 2018}}

The province's release reshaped the map it was fought over. Gavel opened on 21 December 2015 with every territory locked against attack for a fortnight, which froze ownership at the moment of release and handed a lasting advantage to whichever guild happened to hold the best ground when the lock came down.{{cite:ordo-malleus-and-the-first-alliances-discord-private|Gavel release, 21 Dec 2015}}{{cite:territory-economy-and-warfare-discord-private|Gavel release, December 2015}}

### The collapse, February–March 2016

Ordo Malleus fell on 9 March 2016{{cite:thread-265297|post #1, the community guild-timeline image (imgur seklYAQ)}}.

Drew1011 called his account of the collapse the most partisan part of his story: "in no part of this story will this be made more apparent than in the collapse of Ordo. Parts of it will contain my biased perspective. If you ask others who were here, they might give a completely different perspective."{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L393–397, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 26 Feb 2018}} He described the leadership as having drifted into two informal factions — one around Paladin A'renos with Dar_Krusos and Rani, one around himself with the ToastedPandas leaders and Ha_Ha_Redstone — and said nobody acknowledged the split at the time.{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L404–410, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 26 Feb 2018}}

ToastedPandas left on 22 February 2016, after which Dar_Krusos left the Shadow Government{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L381–385, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 26 Feb 2018}}. On 25 February a row broke out over A'renos having invited another guild, Sleeping Knights, into a "sub-alliance" without the other leaders' approval; Drew1011 created a chat excluding him and moved to expel WynnTheory, and the motion failed, with most leaders abstaining or declining{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L414–431, composed 26 Feb 2018}}. Ha Ha United left about 3 March{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L438–439, composed 26 Feb 2018}}. Drew1011 withdrew Holders of LE on 9 March 2016 at approximately 5:27 PM EST, and the alliance ended the same day: "The alliance would crumble a mere 16 days after TnP left."{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L390, L454, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 26 Feb 2018}}

The guild that announced first had already secured a place in another alliance before it did so — two places, in fact, by its leader's own later account: one in [[valkyrie|Valkyrie]] arranged months earlier, and a fallback through a friend if that failed.{{cite:ordo-malleus-and-the-first-alliances-discord-private|the collapse of 9 Mar 2016}}{{cite:illustratus-naming-discord-private|January 2018}} He describes the withdrawal as prepared rather than reactive.

In his withdrawal message he wrote that "instead of this alliance being a balance between all the guilds, it become more of a dictatorship between Kru and Arenos", and gave as his ground that Ha Ha United and ToastedPandas had been Holders of LE's closest allies and that their departure had left his guild alone on one side of an unnamed dispute.{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L454–455 and the accompanying screenshot, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 26 Feb 2018}}

![Drew1011's message withdrawing Holders of LE from Ordo Malleus on 9 March 2016, the departure that ended the alliance.](/images/chronicles/storytime/15-image.webp)

The community timeline dates the collapse two days later: "11th Mar, Ordo Malleus collapses after a chain of leaves started by Holders Of LE [HoL] approximately 2 days before."{{cite:community-guild-timeline|Mar 2016 entry}} The alliance thread's last post is dated 10 March 2016, by Ha_Ha_Redstone.{{cite:forums-wynncraft-com-forums-guilds-72-prefix-id-82-order-post-date-direction-asc|complete census of Alliance-prefixed threads, page 1}} A chronology kept to the minute gives the whole sequence and sides with the timeline. Holders of LE left at 5:27 PM EST on 9 March, Death Reapers at 5:31, Libertas and HackForums at 5:55. WynnTheory went the next afternoon at 3:46, and with it, in the chronology's words, "the only few people who could successfully lead the alliance give up, and the alliance is dead". Necronomicon left at 6:50 AM on 11 March, White Wolves at 7:34, Kangronomicon at 7:39 and Sinners at 12:20 PM.{{cite:gdoc-1csqnkuglsisvsvx|entries of 3/9/16 – 3/11/16}} Drew1011 wrote that afterwards "many people began naming me as its destroyer. Did I truly deserve that title? To this day I'm still not sure."{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L457, composed 23 Jan 2018, re-posted 26 Feb 2018}} Both Paladin A'renos and Dar_Krusos left Wynncraft shortly afterwards; A'renos returned about a year later, while Kru "has never returned, except to pass down leadership of Kangronomicon."{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L462–463, composed 23 Jan 2018, re-posted 26 Feb 2018}} Holders of LE and Ha Ha United joined [[Valkyrie]] on 18 March 2016.{{cite:community-guild-timeline|Mar 2016 entry}}{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L472–473, composed 26 Feb 2018}}

## The Shadow Government

The alliance had a tier of leadership above its leadership. Its leader created a chat, named it the Shadow Government, added a handful of guild leaders to it and told them it outranked the ordinary leaders' channel.{{cite:ordo-malleus-informal-power-discord-private|2015}}

What happened when a member guild's co-leader was added to it is the earliest known instance of a question these alliances never resolved. The narrator records that he did not greet the new arrival at all: his first act was to establish whether that guild now held two votes, and he notes his relief at being told it still held one.{{cite:ordo-malleus-informal-power-discord-private|2015}} The same question was still open thirteen years of guild history later — [[the-federation|the Federation]] argued in 2018 over whether co-leaders voted as well, and in September 2019 a [[terra|Terra]] leader proposing one vote per guild was told the duplicates would have to be removed by hand.{{cite:federation-territory-committee-2018-discord-private|September 2018}}

## Membership

Three rosters survive. The opening post of November 2015 gives eight names — Kangronomicon, Holders of LE, Ha Ha United, End of Everything, HackForums, ToastedPandas, Sinners and the Wynn Wide Merchants Organisation.{{cite:thread-93754-p02|p2 #25, Tapu_Fini, 10 Nov 2015, quoting the opening post}} The February 2016 roster above gives twelve.{{cite:thread-109350|post #11, Drew1011, 20 Feb 2016, quoting the opening post}} The opening post as it stood on 9 March 2016, hours before the collapse, lists eleven guilds beneath a stated count of ten, plus the merchants' organisation: Death Reapers under jjaayyddoonn, Wynn Theory under PaladinArenos, Holders Of LE under Drew1011, Kangronomicon under Dar_krusos, Libertas under yosteric5, Necronomicon under LordMuttonChops, White Wolves under Grimmcat, Sinners under Rani, The No Lifes under chownick, UltimateXeons under motoki1, and HackForums under TheDarkSoul — readmitted after its January expulsion.{{cite:thread-93754|post #1, opening post as last edited 9 Mar 2016}} Machine-recorded membership data begins in January 2018, after the alliance's end.{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}

## Culture

The alliance ran a public programme alongside the war. Its thread advertised a Cross-Province Race, a Thanksgiving Ball and a Valentine's Ball, and a demon-hunting and exploration service called the Pandemonic Paragons; it carried banner art credited to Sparklepopz, coralialia and KompriZe, two versions of an alliance forum signature, and a nine-question guild application form.{{cite:thread-93754|post #1, opening post as last edited 9 Mar 2016}} Two alliance poems were printed on it: "The Passage of Kinship" by Paladin A'renos and "The Blacksmiths of Peace", a twenty-line verse by Dar_Krusos ending "Our shields together, under The Hammer / United en masse 'til the final year."{{cite:thread-93754|post #1, opening post as last edited 9 Mar 2016}}

## The letter to the administration

Ordo Malleus's leaders drafted a letter to the Wynncraft administration opposing a proposed system that would have assigned tiers of territory to guilds by level, with free-for-all land beside it, and refunded guilds' liquid emeralds. It was never sent.{{cite:gdoc-1z47dpzydc1doipe|"Our Purpose and Future of Wynn"}} It puts the alliance's own count at "about eight(?) guilds" out of some three thousand on the server, and argues that no distribution scheme could work because "throughout guild history there have always been one or more guilds who keep a stranglehold, and no matter how big or small of an FFA area you propose, there will still be new alliances made to do so."{{cite:gdoc-1z47dpzydc1doipe|"Our Purpose and Future of Wynn", opening}}

Its case is that opportunity matters more than equality — "Equal opportunity, not equal power" — and that a tiered system would stall every guild at the top tier so that none could level, where the existing system let any guild take Troms for a few hours and climb.{{cite:gdoc-1z47dpzydc1doipe|"Our Purpose and Future of Wynn", the scenario}} It argues by analogy from twentieth-century political economy that a single controlling entity cannot be checked once it goes wrong, and predicts the plan would produce "the EXACT SAME RESULT as the current system".{{cite:gdoc-1z47dpzydc1doipe|"Our Purpose and Future of Wynn", the analogy}}

In place of the plan it proposes four changes: let guild leaders withdraw emeralds from guild banks, capped daily or offset by reducing or removing territory income; make territories smaller so there are more of them; and fix the automatic kicking of inactive guilds. The letter also anticipates the objection to its authors — that alliance leaders are "power-hungry dogs that do not care for others" — and concedes it "to some extent".{{cite:gdoc-1z47dpzydc1doipe|"Our Purpose and Future of Wynn", proposals}}

## The alliance from the ranks

A member of [[holders-of-le|Holders of LE]] who joined the guild during the alliance years wrote his own history of the period in April 2018, from below the leadership rather than inside it.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|2 and 7 Apr 2018, 117 messages}} The alliance is Ordo Malleus throughout: already formed when he began playing in August 2015, growing and widely known by the late November when he decided to join it, ruling the guild scene for the whole of his membership, and gone by the time he came back.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|the alliance across both instalments}} He gives no date for its end, and arrives at one anyway by counting his own absences — a month away over the December update, a further two months after it — which places his remark that the alliance had by then ceased to exist in about March 2016.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|the absences and the remark, in message order}} Ordo Malleus collapsed on 9 March 2016.{{cite:holders-of-le-guild-profile-discord-private|the collapse of 9 Mar 2016}} A man reckoning from how long he was away, two years later, landing in the right month is worth more than a date recited correctly would be.

On his description the ranks were kept outside its politics. He and the members around him were largely unaware of the disputes among the senior ranks, and what reached them came as fragments from the chiefs{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|what the ranks knew of the alliance's quarrels}}; some of them did not know which guild a war was against or what it was about, and fought it because it was exciting.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|not knowing the enemy or the reason}} That is one member of one guild reporting what the people near him knew, rather than evidence that the reasons went unstated.

He also described the alliance as unopposed. It ruled the whole guild scene for as long as he played under it, and players divided into those who wanted to join it and those who wanted to bring it down{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|the alliance's dominance}}; several rival alliances were formed against it in those months and none came to anything.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|the rival alliances}} He was in the first camp, joining because he wanted to know what a large and active guild was like{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|his reason for joining}}, and once inside made it his business to clear smaller guilds off the map.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|what he did once inside}} The rest of the account is at [[the-rank-and-file|the rank and file]].

## Legacy

Ordo Malleus became the yardstick veterans reached for whenever a later power looked too large. When Glitchedslayer compared [[hackforums|HackForums]] to it in August 2016 — "both were known as the king of guild territories and stopped everyone from getting and holding land"{{cite:thread-143392|post #10, Glitchedslayer, 9 Aug 2016}} — Drew1011 objected to the comparison itself: "if you're going to try to compare your guild to the greatest alliance to inhabit Wynn, at least spell it right. It's Ordo Malleus. (Order of the Hammer)"{{cite:thread-143392|post #7, Drew1011, 9 Aug 2016}}, adding "I was just trying to defend the memory of the alliance that my friends and I developed."{{cite:thread-143392|post #9, Drew1011, 9 Aug 2016}}

Glitchedslayer wrote that Ordo "collapsed from the inside because of guilds fighting and was much slower because they had the split the land together" — a structural contrast with Hax, a single guild that "gets much more land for itself so it lvls faster and is much harder to die because of inner fighting".{{cite:thread-143392|post #10, Glitchedslayer, 9 Aug 2016}} Drew1011's gloss on the difference was about the era rather than the structure: "people cared a lot more about guilds then and there were a lot more active guilds fighting for territories".{{cite:thread-143392|post #11, Drew1011, 9 Aug 2016}} He also credited Ordo with the first guild ball, the community-event format later alliances copied: "First guild ball was hosted by Ordo. Legio never hosted events."{{cite:thread-188024-p04|post #61, Drew1011, 22 May 2017}} The demon-hunting service went the same way. Ordo founded a boss-killing service called the Demon Hunters on 1 December 2015, the day it expelled one member guild and admitted another;{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L234–247, composed 22 Feb 2018}} the [[emperium-of-wynn|Emperium of Wynn]] established the Blades of the Emperium, styled the Demon Hunters, in the spring of 2017 as paid boss-slayers and guides for the wider community.{{cite:emperium-announcements|4/24/2017 and 5/8/2017}} Reading the two as one institution carried from one alliance to the next is this article's, and no source joins them.

The alliance kept a social afterlife. A reunion Discord server was created in early 2017; Paladin A'renos joined it, the deleted alliance thread was recovered through it, and it was where A'renos began planning the alliance that became the [[emperium-of-wynn|Emperium of Wynn]].{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L691–700, composed 16 Feb 2018, re-posted 26 Feb 2018}} Members still identified with it years later — "Once an Ordo brother always an Ordo brother", written on the 2018 Federation tribute thread.{{cite:thread-237070|post #6, Drew1011, 13 Nov 2018}}

articles.title: Paladins United
articles.summary: Wynncraft guild founded on 2 Jun 2017 by EHTYSCYTHE, with one of the broadest alliance histories on record: the Coalition, Alliance Alliance, the Federation, Terra, co-founder of Artemis, Valkyrie and Hestia member, Goose, Valhalla, Vanir, and smtn elf.

articles.title: PaladinSorcerer
articles.summary: Titans Valor member, known on the forums as "Pally", whose megalist posts of December 2020 and June 2021 are the earliest and fullest written records of the Hestia and Artemis alliances.

infobox.label: Known for
infobox.value: The 2 Dec 2020 [[hestia|Hestia]]/[[artemis|Artemis]] megalist post; the Jun 2021 Hestia roster

articles.body:
PaladinSorcerer posted as "Pally"; his posts carry the forum title "Titans Valor [ANO]/Holders of LE [HoL]"{{cite:thread-278112-wb20210704|author profile block beside posts #8–#10 (badge markup, not post text), capture of 4 Jul 2021}}.

On 2 December 2020 he wrote to [[the-forum-megalist|the megalist]] arguing that [[titans-valor|Titans Valor]] was neither a war guild nor a community guild but "Mixed", citing the guild-run "Spring Fling, Summer Tournament, and Hallowynn Festival which we hosted for the entirety of the wynn community"{{cite:thread-278112|post #8, 2 Dec 2020}}. A second post the same day named both of Titans Valor's alliances: "ANO is apart of the alliances Hestia (a community alliance between ANO, ESI, LXA, and PUN) and Artemis (war alliance) made up of all the current massive land holding guilds on the map"{{cite:thread-278112|post #10, 2 Dec 2020}}. [[iceresistance|IceResistance]] replied within the hour: "umm ANO community guild FIRST / war second"{{cite:thread-278112|post #11, 2 Dec 2020}}.

On 6 June 2021 he posted [[hestia|Hestia]]'s six-guild roster: "you can add Hestia to Titans Valor [ANO], [[emorians|Emorians]] [ERN], Lux Nova [LXA], Empire of Sindria [ESI], [[paladins-united|Paladins United]] [PUN], and [[hackforums|Hackforums]] [Hax]... We're a community alliance and have been together for about a year now."{{cite:thread-278112-p07|p7 #140, 6 Jun 2021}}

His rank inside Titans Valor was never recorded. [[titan-times|Titan Times]] vol. 3 lists PaladinSorcerer among recipients of the guild's Veteran Medal, "granted to distinguished former members of ANO", placing his departure before mid-2022{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol3|vol. 3, 12 Jun 2022}}.

articles.title: PillowPet
articles.summary: PillowPet created Holders of LE on 21 December 2014, in the week guild warfare was introduced, and was still listed among the guild's chiefs in May 2018, nearly three and a half years later.
articles.body:
**PillowPet** created [[holders-of-le|Holders of LE]] [HoL] on 21 December 2014{{cite:community-guild-timeline|Dec 2014}} — one day before guilds and guild warfare were released in [[the-guild-update|the Guild Update]], and among the first guilds in the [[early-guild-era|early guild era]]. The guild's recruitment thread described it as "Founded upon the advent of the official release of guilds"{{cite:thread-217600|post #1, Thundderr, 10 May 2018}}.

In May 2018 "Pillowpet" was among the guild's four chiefs, alongside [[kuroi|Kur0i]], PikaLegend_ and Hawaiian__{{cite:thread-217600|post #1, Thundderr, 10 May 2018}}. Between the two dates lie nearly three and a half years and at least five changes of ownership at the guild{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L19, L67–71, L104–111, L312, L1035}}.

Nothing else about PillowPet is recorded. The name appears nowhere in [[drew1011|Drew1011]]'s account of the guild's 2015 leadership crisis, in any alliance roster, or on any leaderboard. Whether PillowPet led the guild at any point, or in what capacity the 2014 creation was made, was never documented.

articles.title: Pirates of Wynn
articles.summary: Pirates of Wynn [PoW] was a Wynncraft guild of early 2015, reportedly a top-ten guild contesting sixth place with Kangronomicon in January 2015 and dead by late May. Almost nothing else about it was ever recorded.
articles.body:
[[drew1011|Drew1011]] named **Pirates of Wynn** [PoW] as the first guild he joined: "I joined it in early January 2015, when it was a top 10 guild constantly fighting [[kangronomicon|Kangronomicon]] for the #6 rank."{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L13–14, composed 19 Jan 2018, re-posted 22 Feb 2018}} He left Wynncraft within about a week and returned in late May 2015 to find "that the guild had died"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L15, composed 19 Jan 2018}}.

Nothing else about the guild was ever recorded. Its creation date, its owner, its members, its alliances and the circumstances of its end are all unknown{{cite:community-guild-timeline|the timeline names no guild called Pirates of Wynn}}. No guild leaderboard from early 2015 survives, and machine-recorded war data begins in January 2018{{cite:territory-exchanges|earliest row in the table, 3 Jan 2018 20:22:23 UTC; nothing precedes it}}. The guild belongs to the [[early-guild-era|early guild era]]'s large undocumented remainder.

articles.title: Pressure on unaligned guilds
articles.summary: A guild that took a territory and belonged to no alliance was told to pick a side. On 19 July 2018 an officer of Kingdom of Foxes described to the Federation's war channel how the opposing bloc approached any unaligned guild that took ground and told it to join or hold nothing, and gave one case in which the answer was no. The Federation's own member guilds had done something of the kind on a smaller scale.
articles.body:
On 19 July 2018 an officer of [[kingdom-foxes|Kingdom of Foxes]] [Fox] told [[the-federation|the Federation]]'s war channel, while arguing about how wide the alliance's own enemy list should be, what the opposing bloc did with guilds that belonged to nobody: it approached any guild at all that took a territory and was not in the Federation, and told it to join or be prevented from ever holding ground or having a future.{{cite:pressure-on-unaligned-guilds-2018-discord-private|19 Jul 2018, the method described}} Another leader put it more shortly, as threatening small low-level guilds that they would never be allowed to grow.{{cite:pressure-on-unaligned-guilds-2018-discord-private|19 Jul 2018, the shorter form}} The officer added that the practice could not be policed.{{cite:pressure-on-unaligned-guilds-2018-discord-private|19 Jul 2018, guilds could not be policed}} It is one alliance's account of its opponents, and no answer from the other side was ever written down.

## The case with an ending

The approach had been made to Stone Hearts [HEA], which answered that the Federation had helped it and that it liked the Federation.{{cite:pressure-on-unaligned-guilds-2018-discord-private|19 Jul 2018, Stone Hearts' answer}} It was told that in that case it should expect neither territory nor a future.{{cite:pressure-on-unaligned-guilds-2018-discord-private|19 Jul 2018, the reply}} When the approach was made was not said.{{cite:pressure-on-unaligned-guilds-2018-discord-private|19 Jul 2018, the approach undated}} The officer attributed the design of the method to the standing leader of Achte Shadow [ASh] and to the leaders of Mag and Oce{{cite:pressure-on-unaligned-guilds-2018-discord-private|19 Jul 2018, the leaders named}}, and said the rival guild leader most often blamed for pressure of this kind was not a member of that alliance at the time.{{cite:pressure-on-unaligned-guilds-2018-discord-private|19 Jul 2018, the rival not a member}}

Almost everything Stone Hearts did on the map was on open ground. Between 4 June and 1 August 2018 it took part in 232 exchanges, of which 186 stood on territory the Federation had declared free for all and 46 did not.{{cite:territory-exchanges|exchanges involving Stone Hearts, 4 Jun – 1 Aug 2018 UTC, free-for-all list of 4 Jun 2018: 232 raw, 186 on the list, 46 contested}} From 6 to 31 August it took part in 362, every one on the declared list, in trade with [[kingdom-foxes|Kingdom Foxes]], [[emorians|Emorians]], [[ex-nihilo|Ex Nihilo]], [[thenolifes|TheNoLifes]] and [[fantasy|Fantasy]].{{cite:territory-exchanges|exchanges involving Stone Hearts, 6–31 Aug 2018 UTC, free-for-all list of 6 Aug 2018: 362 raw, 362 on the list, 0 contested}} Ground on that list was open to anyone — see [[territory-warfare|territory warfare]]. Its last exchange of the summer fell on 27 August and its next on 24 December, four months with no gap in the record between them.{{cite:territory-exchanges|last and next exchanges involving Stone Hearts, 27 Aug and 24 Dec 2018 UTC; no capture-log gap of three days or more falls between them}} What became of the guild was never recorded, and nothing joins its silence to what it had been told.

## The Federation on the same question

Its own member guilds had done something of the kind on a smaller scale. On 14 March 2018 the alliance's founder told the war channel that a small guild then under attack was the one a captain of Kingdom of Foxes had tried to extort, the demand being a payment in exchange for not being attacked back.{{cite:pressure-on-unaligned-guilds-2018-discord-private|14 Mar 2018, the accusation}} He had found the details out afterwards and thought the episode embarrassing.{{cite:pressure-on-unaligned-guilds-2018-discord-private|14 Mar 2018, found out afterwards}} When the attempt was made was never stated, only that it was some time before that day.{{cite:pressure-on-unaligned-guilds-2018-discord-private|14 Mar 2018, the attempt undated}} The guild he named was the one another member had asked about earlier that day, when it turned up as an unfamiliar attacker on a member guild.{{cite:pressure-on-unaligned-guilds-2018-discord-private|14 Mar 2018, the earlier question}} The captain was not named, the charge was made in his absence, and the guild said to have been asked to pay left no account.

The advice given to a member losing ground to a guild he did not recognise was to destroy it. On 23 February 2018 a member reported in the general channel that an unfamiliar guild had taken territories belonging to [[buildcraftia|BuildCraftia]] [BCr], and asked what he should do.{{cite:pressure-on-unaligned-guilds-2018-discord-private|23 Feb 2018, the report}} He was told to take back whatever was assigned to him and, if he could manage it, to reduce the attacker to nothing and see what it did then{{cite:pressure-on-unaligned-guilds-2018-discord-private|23 Feb 2018, the advice}}; a second member added that this needed a proper build rather than whatever was to hand.{{cite:pressure-on-unaligned-guilds-2018-discord-private|23 Feb 2018, the qualification}} Two members answering in a general channel are not an instruction of the alliance's. BuildCraftia was holding Federation-assigned ground that day, five weeks before the alliance expelled it.{{cite:pressure-on-unaligned-guilds-2018-discord-private|23 Feb 2018, the assignment held}}

The two are not of the same kind, and setting them beside each other is this article's: a practice described as systematic by a witness on the other side of it, against one accusation and one exchange in a general channel.

articles.title: Pretzule
articles.summary: Leader of House of Sentinels from at least April 2017, when the guild turned deliberately toward warring — the pivot that took it into the Coalition's founding circle that October.

articles.title: The private diplomacy era
articles.summary: 2023 to 2026: alliance-making disappeared into private Discords, and the era's alliances — behind the largest wars ever fought — were never named or published. The in-game ally registrations that appeared from June 2026 record a game mechanic used chiefly to permit joint guild raids, not the era's politics.

infobox.label: Named alliances
infobox.value: [[Avocado Aquarium]] (the era's only named war pact)

infobox.label: Major wars
infobox.value: [[the-avocado-split|The Avocado split]], [[avicia-sequoia-war|Avicia–Sequoia war]], [[idiot-co-aquarium-war|Idiot Co–Aquarium war]], [[aequitas-avicia-war|Aequitas–Avicia war]], [[aequitas-sequoia-war|Aequitas–Sequoia war]]

infobox.label: Defining shift
infobox.value: Diplomacy moved to private Discords and never re-emerged in public

articles.body:
{{map:2024-06-01|The map during the Idiot Co–Aquarium war}}

After [[smtn elf]] faded in mid-2023, public diplomacy stopped. No alliance roster was published anywhere after June 2022{{cite:thread-278112-p09|p9 #161, Sg_Voltage, 7 Jul 2022}}, and from 2023 onward alliance-making happened in private guild Discords. [[Titans Valor]]'s founder IceResistance later described the older practice: guilds "had their own channels, their own Discords, their own backrooms where actual conversations happened. Alliances were formed, enemies were negotiated with, all behind closed doors. And it worked." In October 2025 the official Discord's #guild-politics channel was renamed #guild-community{{cite:thread-322643|post #1, IceResistance, 2 Oct 2025}}. The wars of this era were the largest yet fought, but the alliances behind them were never named or published.

## The Avocado Aquarium

The era's one named pact was [[Avocado Aquarium]], the two-guild alliance of [[Avicia]] and [[The Aquarium]] after [[the-avocado-split|they quit smtn elf]] in June 2023. The pair waged a sniping and claim-taking campaign against their former allies into early 2024 and ran shared infrastructure, including the joint subguild Avoquarium [HQs] (created 9 August 2023){{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. By August 2023 they were each other's 'unwavering ally'{{cite:thread-310286|Avicia guild thread, season post of 19 Aug 2023}}. The era's only other named relationship came in September 2023: 'TNL and AEQ were allied and warring together.'{{cite:thread-280525-p22|p22 #427, kwiebs, 1 Sep 2023}}

## Wars known only from the map

None of the era's major wars was publicly declared:

- [[avicia-sequoia-war|Avicia–Sequoia war]] (Oct–Nov 2023, second round Jan 2024) — Avicia against the young [[Sequoia]] (founded 14 Oct 2022){{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-sequoia|creation date 14 Oct 2022, retrieved 2 Sep 2026}}, whose rise continued regardless: it won seven consecutive guild seasons from mid-2024{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|season table, Seasons 19-25}}.
- [[idiot-co-aquarium-war|Idiot Co–Aquarium war]] (Apr 2024 – Jan 2025) — the biggest war since 2021, peaking at 5,045 territory exchanges in a week{{cite:territory-exchanges|Idiot Co-Aquarium war, Apr 2024 - Jan 2025: weekly peak 5,045}} and spanning the 'Rekindled World' map rework of 10 August 2024{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}.
- [[the-long-raid|The Long Raid]] (late Jul – early Aug 2024) — a week-long siege of [[Aequitas]]'s Sky-province claim, the era's only battle retold first-hand{{cite:thread-318070|post #1, Defervesco, 9 Aug 2024}}{{cite:youtube-com-watch-v-rlrh14ns6ok|'Wynncraft Warring - The Long Raid', Frank Wynncraft, premiered 4 Aug 2024}}; the attackers were never named.
- [[aequitas-avicia-war|Aequitas–Avicia war]] (3 Nov – 21 Dec 2025) — the largest war ever fought: 15,710 territory exchanges, weekly peak 4,736{{cite:territory-exchanges|Aequitas-Avicia war, 3 Nov - 21 Dec 2025}}.
- On 25 May 2026 KongoBoys began a sustained campaign against [[Profession Heaven]], ending the neutrality it had held since January 2021{{cite:territory-exchanges|KongoBoys-Profession Heaven campaign from 25 May 2026}}.
- [[aequitas-sequoia-war|Aequitas–Sequoia war]] (from Aug 2026, ongoing) — 7,488 territory exchanges in its first week, with Aequitas driven to zero territories{{cite:territory-exchanges|Aequitas-Sequoia war, first week, Aug 2026}}.

## The public critique

With alliance politics gone, the era's public writing about guilds turned to the system itself. On 9 December 2023 TheNelston, then the owner of [[idiot-co|Idiot Co]], published "Wynncraft's Guilds are Bad... Here's Why", a twenty-minute critique of "the messy state of guild wars, the lack of content for lower level players and non-warrers in general, and the absence of many quality of life features"{{cite:youtube-com-watch-v-m2g6zqx2dko|video description, 9 Dec 2023}}, and opened a companion forum thread asking what the community wanted, where he named guild raids as the change he would ask for first.{{cite:thread-313565|post #1, TheNelston, 9 Dec 2023}} He followed it in February and May 2024 with a guild-war guide and a war-economics guide, written, he said, because many players had told him they did not understand wars and because he wanted the guild scene to be more active.{{cite:youtube-com-feeds-videos-xml-channel-id-ucjooggtimerj6rxphwebgxg|channel feed: uploads of 18 Feb and 10 May 2024}}

Nothing replaced the alliance rosters, but guides to the system kept appearing. A December 2024 guide lists what guilds were then for — community, warring, events, the guild bank, guild raids and tomes — and describes the recruitment route of the era: "Most guilds require an application, which can usually be found on their private Discord."{{cite:thread-320194|post #1, Mocomochi, 23 Dec 2024}} Even the mechanics of cross-guild talk were still absent from the game: a July 2023 suggestion asked for an in-game alliance chat on the grounds that community building between guilds was "currently very restricted to discord".{{cite:thread-309201|post #1, TheNelston, 6 Jul 2023}}

Below the warring guilds the forums filled with small dead ones. A 2025 thread collected owners of guilds that had emptied out and whose statistics pages had corrupted, one of them writing that the system "doesn't really understand how to process a guild with no active updates".{{cite:thread-321698|posts #1–4, May–Oct 2025}}

## The in-game ally record (2026)

In June 2026 a machine-made record of guild relationships appeared, but not a record of the era's politics. Wynncraft's in-game ally system — present since 2021 — acquired its main practical use when allied guilds gained the ability to run guild raids together{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-version-2-2-1|Official Wynncraft Wiki, 'Version 2.2.1' (12 Jun 2026)}}, and [[Sequoia]]'s open-source mod began capturing the game's 'formed/revoked an alliance with' broadcasts{{cite:github-com-sequoiawynncraft-sequoia-mod|commit 69fb472, 12 Jun 2026}}, producing the first machine-made records of [[first-machine-recorded-alliances|in-game ally registrations]]{{cite:raw-githubusercontent-com-sequoiawynncraft-sequoia-mod-main-src-test-java-com-seqwawa-|ChatManagerTest alliance-message fixtures}}. They record which guilds were registered as allies and nothing about the politics of the era. From 30 July 2026 the mod auto-snapshots the in-game Diplomacy menu to a private archive{{cite:github-com-sequoiawynncraft-sequoia-mod|commit 8b27368 and Modrinth 1.8.0 changelog, 30 Jul 2026}} (see [[the-diplomacy-update|The Diplomacy update]]).

What became visible is a game-mechanical relationship, used chiefly to permit joint guild raids; it does not indicate political alliance, and guilds registered as in-game allies may be rivals or recent belligerents. The alliances behind the era's wars therefore remain unnamed. Nothing has succeeded [[the-forum-megalist|the megalist]], whose last roster dates from June 2022{{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #160, TherapueticLiz, 26 Jun 2022}}.

articles.title: Profession Heaven
articles.summary: A public profession-XP guild founded by Crokee in January 2021 and granted neutral status that same month under the joint protection of Goose and Artemis. Its neutrality outlived both protectors and every successor alliance, ending only in May 2026 when KongoBoys began a sustained campaign against it.

articles.title: Profession Heaven neutrality
articles.summary: On 25 Jan 2021 Profession Heaven was granted neutral status, protected by both Goose and Artemis, and given Silent Expanse territory as a public profession-XP guild — an arrangement that held for over five years.
articles.body:
The grant was made in the middle of the [[Goose-Artemis war]], with both warring alliances protecting [[Profession Heaven]] at once{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. Its first territory exchange fell on the same day{{cite:territory-exchanges|first Profession Heaven territory exchange, 25 Jan 2021}}.

The arrangement was unique: a guild holding land on a contested map by the joint consent of both sides of a map-wide war.

## A five-year peace

The neutrality outlived its guarantors. When Goose and Artemis collapsed together on 11 May 2021 ([[The Great Collapse]]), protection carried over to their successors. Profession Heaven eventually joined the blocs outright, appearing on [[Cucumber Company]]'s final public roster of 26 Jun 2022{{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #160, TherapueticLiz, 26 Jun 2022}} and remaining through the rename into [[smtn-elf|smtn elf]]{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol6|vol. 6, 12 Oct 2022}} until that alliance's end in mid-2023 — while its protected, neutral character as a public XP guild persisted.

The arrangement held until 25 May 2026, when KongoBoys — itself a former Cucumber Company ally — began the sustained campaign that [[fall-of-profession-heaven-s-neutrality|ended the neutrality]] after more than five years{{cite:territory-exchanges|KongoBoys-Profession Heaven campaign from 25 May 2026}}.

articles.title: Sequoia
articles.summary: Wynncraft guild founded on 14 Oct 2022 that rose to win seven consecutive guild seasons from mid-2024. Its open-source mod produced the first machine-captured records of the game's in-game ally system in June 2026. Fought Avicia in 2023-24 and has been at war with Aequitas since August 2026.

articles.title: Seraphim
articles.summary: Seraphim was a self-consciously unserious community alliance opened on 8 August 2016 by Dacleos, declaring itself "100% community based" with "no intention of actively providing support for guild wars". Its four recorded members included Libertas, then the second-largest territory holder on the map.
articles.leadImageCaption: The Seraphim Alliance emblem: a gold eight-pointed star within a crescent.

articles.title: Serpentem Empire
articles.summary: A Wynncraft guild founded in November 2017 by members who left or were removed from KingdomPhoenixes in the split over Drew1011’s appointment as viceroy. It fought on the Coalition’s side in the Gavel Invasion that December and was still a Federation member a year later.

infobox.value: Early November 2017, from the KingdomPhoenixes split

articles.title: Sg_Voltage
articles.summary: Creator and maintainer of the forum megalist, Wynncraft’s community register of guilds and alliances from November 2020, and the player who deleted its alliance section in July 2022.
articles.body:
Sg_Voltage created Wynncraft forums thread 278112, "Read Before Applying To A Guild - All Currently Recruiting Guilds Megalist", on 29 November 2020, and maintained it for the next two years{{cite:thread-278112|thread opened 29 Nov 2020; first replies of 30 Nov 2020}}. The opening post set out the purpose: "I've assembled a list of every* guild which is currently recruiting along with some important stats... My goal is to be able to make sure every guild gets the chance to shine and every player can get the chance to find the guild that's right for them."{{cite:thread-278112|post #1 (OP)}}

The list lived in a Google Sheet edited by the guilds themselves — "send me a message with your Gmail and I'll give you editing permission" — which is why its rosters were lost when the sheet went down{{cite:thread-278112-wb20210704|post #1 (OP), capture of 4 Jul 2021}}. Forum administrator colin350 pinned the thread on 17 January 2021 after Sg_Voltage committed to weekly updates{{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #65 and #67, 14–17 Jan 2021}}.

One column of that sheet recorded alliances, and it became the era's register of record: nearly every dated alliance roster of 2020–22 traces to a post asking Sg_Voltage to update it. On 7 July 2022 he ended it, replying to a correction with "For alliance information, it's supposed to be updated by the guilds themselves... I don't care to follow guild drama", then: "You know what, on second thought I'm just going to delete that section. If it's not updated regularly it's not really useful anyways."{{cite:thread-278112-p09|p9 #161, 7 Jul 2022}} No public alliance roster has been published since.

No guild is recorded for Sg_Voltage. In July 2021 his forum profile showed a CHAMPION rank, the custom title "1.18 was the best update, don't @me", and no guild field at all{{cite:thread-278112-wb20210704|author profile block (badge markup, not post text), capture of 4 Jul 2021}} — fitting for the community's neutral registrar, though whether the omission was deliberate is unknown.

articles.title: ShadowFall
articles.summary: Wynncraft guild founded in 2017 that held a leadership seat in Artemis by early 2020, switched sides to Goose in February 2021, and served in Niflheim, Valhalla and Vanir. By 2023 it was a subguild of The Aquarium.
