articles.title: The betrayal of Valhalla
articles.summary: The Mage Legacy and TheNoLifes turned on their Valhalla allies — friction visible from August 2021, erupting into open war in December with 5,359 territory exchanges that month. Both were excluded when Vanir formed on 28 Nov 2021.

infobox.label: Belligerents
infobox.value: The Mage Legacy, TheNoLifes vs the [[Valhalla]]/[[Vanir]] guilds

articles.body:
## Background

The Mage Legacy and TheNoLifes were both [[Valhalla]] members from its founding on 11 May 2021, part of the thirteen-guild bloc that took the map after [[The Great Collapse]]{{cite:community-guild-timeline|11 May 2021 Valhalla roster}}. Friction between the two and their allies appears from August 2021, months before any open break{{cite:territory-exchanges|Mage Legacy and TheNoLifes friction from August 2021}}.

## The betrayal

When Valhalla's guilds reorganized as [[Vanir]] on 28 Nov 2021, both were excluded{{cite:community-guild-timeline|28 Nov 2021 Vanir roster}}. Open war followed in December: 5,359 territory exchanges that month between the two betrayers and their former allies — one of the most violent single months of territory warfare on record{{cite:territory-exchanges|5,359 territory exchanges, December 2021}}.

TheNoLifes went on to help lead [[Khaos]]{{cite:cameron-oral-history|Cameron oral history (TAq veteran testimony)}}, which it joined around 1 December 2021{{cite:chronicle-records|Khaos membership: TheNoLifes from ~1 Dec 2021}}.

{{map:2021-11-28|The map when Vanir formed without the betrayers}}

## Aftermath

By early 2022 the fighting had folded into [[khaos-s-last-war|Khaos's last war]], the winter-long struggle between Khaos and the ex-Valhalla guilds. TheNoLifes stayed hostile to its former allies into 2023, long after the blocs themselves had dissolved{{cite:territory-exchanges|TheNoLifes' hostility to the ex-Valhalla guilds persisting into 2023}}.

articles.title: The Canyon concession
articles.summary: On 31 December 2018 the Aesir Pact released part of the Canyon of the Lost — the region it had been formed to hold — to Blacklisted, in exchange for a ceasefire with the Olympus alliance. The deal was put, approved and announced within three hours and eleven minutes, in the alliance's warriors' channel rather than its council. Within two days the ground had passed to a guild that was no party to it, and on 18 January 2019 the alliance struck the Canyon off its own claims map.

articles.title: The Coalition Discord Deletion
articles.summary: The Coalition's first Discord server was destroyed on the evening of 11 January 2018 by the former monarch of KingdomPhoenixes, one of the alliance's two founding guilds, who said so in her own guild's channel a minute later and told another guild it was a good moment to attack. A replacement server was created forty seconds after the deletion, and the members she had removed from the guild were reinstated within the hour.

infobox.label: Date
infobox.value: 11 Jan 2018 on the guild channel's clock; 12 Jan 2018, 04:19 UTC

articles.title: The Consortium
articles.summary: The Consortium was a Wynncraft war alliance of spring 2019, organised in March against the Valkyrie bloc and arguing over its own dissolution by 2 April. It took in a dozen member guilds in three weeks, published a roster of seven enemies and eleven allies, opened one offensive, and passed through three leaders before it ended.

articles.title: The Diplomacy update
articles.summary: Wynncraft's in-game guild ally system, introduced in version 1.20 (2021). Allying is a game-mechanical relationship — an ally tax rate, and from 2026 the ability for allied guilds to run Guild Raids together — rather than a political alliance, though from June 2026 its events became the first machine-readable record of guild relationships.

infobox.label: What allying does
infobox.value: Applies the ally tax rate; from 2026, permits joint Guild Raids

infobox.label: API status
infobox.value: No alliance field in the official API (as of Sep 2026)

articles.body:
Wynncraft has had an in-game guild ally system since version 1.20 'Gavel Reborn' (20 January 2021){{cite:thread-281822|post #1, 20 Jan 2021}}{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, 'Guilds & Wars' sections, 23 Nov 2020}}. Allying is a game-mechanical status rather than a declaration: it interacts with the [[territory-warfare|territory system]] through the ally tax rate charged on an allied guild's territories{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-war|attack-cost formula: allied guilds are charged the ally tax}}, and a Diplomacy menu in the guild UI lists a guild's allies (up to 16, per the Sequoia mod's snapshot feature){{cite:github-com-sequoiawynncraft-sequoia-mod-blob-main-src-test-java-com-seq|GuildAllianceSnapshotManagerTest}}. Setting a guild as an ally does not indicate a political alliance — allied guilds may be rivals or recent belligerents — and the in-game menu played no recorded part in the [[the-realignment-era|realignment-era]] or [[private-diplomacy-era|private-diplomacy-era]] blocs.

What the system is chiefly for became explicit in 2026. Version 2.2.1 (12 June 2026) added the change 'Guild Allies can now do Guild Raids together'{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-version-2-2-1|Official Wynncraft Wiki, 'Version 2.2.1' (12 Jun 2026)}}, which is the point of the feature as it is used: two guilds register as allies so that their members can run guild raids as one group. The feature is also dated to version 2.2.2 of 10 July 2026{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}; the wiki's changelogs attribute it to 2.2.1{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-version-2-2-2|Official Wynncraft Wiki, 'Version 2.2.2' (10 Jul 2026)}}.

The same month, [[Sequoia]]'s open-source client mod began parsing the in-game 'formed/revoked an alliance with' chat broadcasts (commit of 12 June 2026){{cite:github-com-sequoiawynncraft-sequoia-mod|commit 69fb472, 12 Jun 2026}}, the first such records made by software rather than written down by a person{{cite:raw-githubusercontent-com-sequoiawynncraft-sequoia-mod-main-src-test-java-com-seqwawa-|ChatManagerTest alliance-message fixtures}}. From 30 July 2026 the mod auto-snapshots the Diplomacy menu to Sequoia's private backend, a growing machine-readable archive that is not publicly accessible{{cite:github-com-sequoiawynncraft-sequoia-mod|commit 8b27368 and Modrinth 1.8.0 changelog, 30 Jul 2026}}. The official API exposed no alliance field as of 2 September 2026{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-sequoia|v3/guild response, retrieved 2 Sep 2026}}, so the in-game record remains readable only through such tooling.
articles.leadImageCaption: In-game 'View Diplomacy' tooltip shown in the 1.20 'Gavel Reborn' changelog: a guild's alliance list naming two allied guilds.

articles.title: The Divine Swords
articles.summary: The Divine Swords [DsQ] was a Wynncraft guild of 2017–2018 that began as a subguild and never settled who led it. Its council chose a leader over the members doing its fighting, it passed through around six leaders in a year, and the Federation expelled it in October 2018 on discovering it was being run through the alt account of someone who had left the alliance.

infobox.label: Status
infobox.value: No disbandment recorded; nothing after October 2018

articles.title: The Economy Update
articles.summary: Wynncraft version 1.18, the Economy Update, released 18 January 2019: professions, crafting and an in-game trade market. It reshaped the economy that funded guilds but left war mechanics essentially untouched.

infobox.label: Focus
infobox.value: Professions (gathering and crafting), trade market, guild banners

articles.body:
Version 1.18, officially titled 'The Economy Update', was released on 18 January 2019{{cite:thread-238340|Wynncraft forums thread 238340, '1.18 The Economy Update - Changelog'}}{{cite:https://wynncraft.fandom.com/wiki/Version_1.18|Wynncraft Wiki (Fandom), 'Version 1.18'}} — between the [[the-federation-dies|Federation's fall]] and the founding of [[Luna]], in the middle of [[the-alliance-wars-of-2019|the alliance wars of 2019]].

Its focus was the player economy rather than warfare: it introduced the professions system (gathering and crafting){{cite:thread-238340|Wynncraft forums thread 238340, '1.18 The Economy Update - Changelog'}}, and it added the in-game Trade Market{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-version-1-18|Trade Market listed under the 1.18 additions}}. The feature was trailed in January 2019 on the official Twitter account; the announcement itself does not survive{{cite:x-com-wynncraft-status-1084983171920351232-wb20251203|the status URL captured 3 Dec 2025 returns an empty page}}. On the guild side its contribution was cosmetic: 1.18 introduced guild banners, replacing 'the Mysterious Potatoes riddle'{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guilds|Official Wynncraft Wiki, 'Guilds' (trivia)}}.

No changes to the guild war system itself were recorded in 1.18. The economy-and-war rework that transformed [[territory-warfare|territory warfare]] — war towers, guild resource production, trade routes and taxation — came two years later, in version 1.20 'Gavel Reborn' (20 January 2021){{cite:thread-281822|post #1, 20 Jan 2021}}{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, 'Guilds & Wars' sections, 23 Nov 2020}}, which also laid the groundwork for [[guild-seasons|Guild seasons]] and the in-game ally system (see [[the-diplomacy-update|The Diplomacy update]]).
articles.leadImageCaption: Official logo for Wynncraft version 1.18, the Economy Update, released 18 January 2019.

articles.title: The Federation
articles.summary: The Federation was the dominant Wynncraft war alliance of 2018, founded around 16 Feb 2018 out of the Coalition remnant and the War Syndicate remains, and led by Drew1011. It took the entire territory map on 21 Feb 2018 and held it for 8 months and 25 days, grew to 37-40 member guilds, and died by internal collapse in a single day on 10 Nov 2018.

infobox.label: Map control from
infobox.value: 21 Feb 2018 (356 of 383 territories); the opposing bloc was eliminated on 19–20 Mar 2018

articles.title: The Federation in April 2018
articles.summary: In April 2018 the Federation made attacking its listed enemies compulsory and then voted to expel four member guilds that had not claimed the territory assigned to them — the first activity test it ever wrote down. One guild was taken off the list while the vote was running, after two leaders said they would vote yes if it were, and dissolved itself four days later.

infobox.label: Test applied
infobox.value: Assigned territory not claimed or attempted

articles.title: The Federation dies
articles.summary: The internal collapse of the Federation on 10 November 2018: one guild left at around 3 AM EST, and the alliance that had held the entire map for 8 months and 25 days cascaded apart within a day.

infobox.label: Alliance
infobox.value: [[the-federation|Federation]] (and the [[Aesir Pact]], which died with it)

infobox.label: Cause
infobox.value: Internal collapse — 'what killed Federation was... internal affairs' (Drew1011)

articles.title: The Federation's Founding Night
articles.summary: The Federation's Discord server was created at five past eight on the evening of 16 February 2018, fifty-two minutes after the first guild announced it was leaving the Coalition. The merger was announced inside it as a completed fact within its first minute, nothing was put to a vote, and the alliance was named the next morning while its permanent channels were being made.

infobox.label: Decided by
infobox.value: Two guild leaders; no vote recorded

articles.title: The Federation in July 2018
articles.summary: In July 2018 the Federation held the whole territory map and lost four member guilds. Its largest contributor measured its own share of the alliance's fighting at a quarter, announced that it would stop defending its allies, and was besieged for fourteen hours at the end of the month.

articles.title: The Federation's June crisis
articles.summary: On the morning of 25 June 2018 the Federation's Discord administrator, herself the leader of a member guild, deleted every role on the alliance's own server. By that afternoon her guild faced an expulsion vote and she had left, Paladins United had announced its departure on unrelated grounds, a third leader had gone, and a replacement guild had been voted in.

articles.title: The feeding accusation
articles.summary: In May 2018 the Federation was accused on Wynncraft's public forums of feeding — arranging for territory to fall to a guild rather than fighting for it. Its public answer denied that any of its guilds were alternate or subguilds, its own advisory channel produced two incompatible definitions of the word the next day, and a Wynncraft administrator closed the argument on 30 May by declining to regulate the practice at all.

articles.title: The forum megalist
articles.summary: Wynncraft forums thread 278112, created and maintained by Sg_Voltage from 29 November 2020: the community-maintained list of guilds and alliances. Its posts of December 2020 - June 2022 preserve most of the era's known alliance rosters; its alliance section was deleted on 7 July 2022, ending public alliance rosters.
articles.body:
Between December 2020 and June 2022 it was the only public, dated record of who was allied with whom - and nearly every known alliance roster of the [[artemis-goose-era|Artemis-Goose]] and [[the-realignment-era|realignment]] eras traces to one of its posts.

## Authorship

The thread was created on 29 November 2020 by [[sg-voltage|Sg_Voltage]], who maintained it for years afterwards{{cite:thread-278112|thread opened 29 Nov 2020; Sg_Voltage replies through p1}}. Pally - [[paladinsorcerer|PaladinSorcerer]] of [[Titans Valor]] - was a reader, and the author of the thread's 2 December 2020 alliance post{{cite:thread-278112|p1 #10, Pally, 2 Dec 2020}}, but never its maintainer. Sg_Voltage's own guild affiliation is unknown; his forum profile displayed a CHAMPION rank and no guild{{cite:thread-278112-wb20210704|post #1, capture of 4 Jul 2021}}.

The opening post set out the project - 'I've assembled a list of every* guild which is currently recruiting along with some important stats for each ... My goal is to be able to make sure every guild gets the chance to shine' - and the listing itself lived in a Google Sheet edited by the guilds themselves: 'If you're a high ranking member of a guild and want to see your guild added or want to make changes, send me a message with your Gmail and I'll give you editing permission.' One of the sheet's columns was Alliances - 'Some guilds are in alliances for warring, this is where they're listed' - and that column is why the thread matters to guild history{{cite:thread-278112-wb20210704|post #1, capture of 4 Jul 2021}}. After Sg_Voltage was asked whether he intended to update it weekly, forum administrator colin350 pinned the thread on 17 January 2021{{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #65 and #67, colin350, 14-17 Jan 2021}}.

## Landmark posts

Its landmark entries include: the 2 December 2020 post by Pally (post #10) recording that 'ANO is apart of the alliances Hestia (a community alliance between ANO, ESI, LXA, and PUN) and Artemis (war alliance) made up of all the current massive land holding guilds on the map'{{cite:thread-278112|p1 #10, Pally, 2 Dec 2020}} - the first record of both [[Hestia]] and [[Artemis]]; two posts on the morning of 19 January 2021, 99loulou999's 'TNR (TNI and TNA) are part of Goose' and Lev98bug's 'Eden is in Goose if you could add that', the earliest recorded uses of the name [[Goose]], to which Sg_Voltage replied 'Just want to drop in and say that I'm a huge fan of the name'{{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #71-73, 19 Jan 2021}}; the 1 February 2021 side-switch report by urbymine ('BNU(IBT), SHY and TNL are all goose now'){{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #76, urbymine, 1 Feb 2021}}; the 25 May 2021 post recording the [[Valhalla]]/[[Khaos]] renames after [[the-great-collapse|the Great Collapse]]{{cite:thread-278112-p07|p7 #134-137, 25 May 2021}}; Pally's six-guild Hestia roster of 6 June 2021{{cite:thread-278112-p07|p7 #140, Pally, 6 Jun 2021}}; the 7 July 2021 [[Niflheim]] roster{{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #146, HungHung, 7 Jul 2021}}; and the 26 June 2022 post giving [[Cucumber Company]]'s full 14-guild roster{{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #160, TherapueticLiz, 26 Jun 2022}} - the last public alliance roster ever posted anywhere.

## The deletion

Twelve days later, on 7 July 2022, the thread's alliance section was deleted. Replying to the Cucumber Company roster in post #161, Sg_Voltage first explained that 'for alliance information, it's supposed to be updated by the guilds themselves, I noticed it was out of date so I just moved it to the side. I don't care to follow guild drama', then added: 'You know what, on second thought I'm just going to delete that section. If it's not updated regularly it's not really useful anyways.'{{cite:thread-278112-p09|p9 #161, Sg_Voltage, 7 Jul 2022}} The deletion marks the boundary between the public record and [[private-diplomacy-era|the private diplomacy era]]: no alliance roster has been published since{{cite:thread-278112-wb20220517|capture of 17 May 2022, alliance column still described in the opening post}}{{cite:thread-278112-wb20220915|capture of 15 Sep 2022, alliance column gone}}.

The thread itself outlived its alliance column. Sg_Voltage reported the sheet being flagged by Google in January 2023 and was still fielding update requests that March, and readers were still posting to it in 2025{{cite:thread-278112-p09|p9 #168 and #170, Jan-Mar 2023; #172-174, 2025}}. The underlying Google Sheet was never captured by any web archive, so the Valhalla- and Khaos-era rosters it once held are gone from the public web{{cite:chronicle-records|the lost Google Sheet; megalist authorship correction}}; the thread's posts survive partly through Wayback Machine snapshots{{cite:thread-278112-wb20210704|post #1, capture of 4 Jul 2021}}.

articles.title: The Great Collapse
articles.summary: On 11 May 2021, Goose and Artemis — the two blocs that had fought the war for the map — both collapsed on the same day. Thirteen guilds formed Valhalla and nine formed Khaos, and the new blocs went straight to war.
articles.body:
{{map:2021-05-12|The map the day after the collapse}}

## Background

The [[goose-artemis-war|Goose-Artemis war]] had run since December 2020{{cite:thread-279337|post #1, Sheepn, 18 Dec 2020}}: [[Artemis]] the map-holder, [[Goose]] the coalition that rose against it and eventually took map control. By May 2021 Goose had absorbed much of the old Artemis world along with the guilds that would become Khaos's core.

## They were negotiating a merger until the morning it happened

Two days before both blocs dissolved, one of the men running the Artemis side built a Discord server to negotiate a merger with the other. It went up at 18:06 on 9 May, replaced a ten-person group chat that could not hold an eleventh negotiator, capped its invite at ten uses, and the first thing decided in it was to keep it off the other bloc's leadership channel.{{cite:artemis-elysium-negotiation-may-2021-discord-private|9 May 2021}} It carried 704 messages that day and 728 on the 10th.{{cite:artemis-elysium-negotiation-may-2021-discord-private|9–10 May 2021}}

A constitution was tabled, a map was tabled, each guild's demands were written out, the draft was revised, and one guild's acceptance was recorded.{{cite:artemis-elysium-negotiation-may-2021-discord-private|9–10 May 2021}} The period is usually described as the one where alliance politics moved into private rooms and stopped being written down; this was written down, in a room built for it.

**The two blocs were attacking each other throughout, and neither side treated that as a difficulty.** Asked about it, [[kingdom-foxes|Kingdom Foxes]]' leader said the attacks were the only answer to a charge that his guild had shown no activity, and asked how Artemis was supposed to justify a decent claim if it was not to war. The other side granted that the charge had been fair and moved on.{{cite:artemis-elysium-negotiation-may-2021-discord-private|10 May 2021}} Warring was the credential, not the obstacle.

The longest argument was about who would moderate the merged server. Both sides agreed the manager role should be moderation only; [[eden|Eden]]'s leader said that in practice managers always outweigh guild leaders; another proposed abolishing their private channel as a check; the Artemis side answered that the check on managers is each other.{{cite:artemis-elysium-negotiation-may-2021-discord-private|10 May 2021}} It was settled only that the split would be even.

On 11 May the server carried 57 messages and stopped.{{cite:artemis-elysium-negotiation-may-2021-discord-private|11 May 2021}} No outcome was ever written in it, and part of the record was never text at all — the negotiators moved into a voice channel expressly to avoid typing, and one of them reports a map approved there that appears nowhere else.{{cite:artemis-elysium-negotiation-may-2021-discord-private|10 May 2021}}

That the talks stopped on the day the two blocs collapsed is a join between two records rather than a claim in either: the messages and their ending are from the negotiators' own server, the collapse and the alliances that followed are from the community's account of the day, and nothing in either says which way any causation ran.

## The collapse

On 11 May 2021 both alliances dissolved on the same day. Thirteen guilds — including [[The Aquarium]] — formed [[Valhalla]], while nine, largely the Goose bloc's core (Aequitas, Wheres The Finish, Nerfuria, Ultra Violet, Fuzzy Spiders, ChinaNumberOne, Cyphrus Code, Eden, with Tartarus Wrath joining days later), formed [[Khaos]]{{cite:community-guild-timeline|11 May 2021 rosters}}. Valhalla took map control from Goose's remnants within days{{cite:community-guild-timeline|the May 2021 entry: Valhalla takes map control from Goose}}.

A megalist post of 25 May 2021 recorded that 'the two major alliances both disbanded and got new names... Valhalla and Kaos', while noting that [[Valkyrie]] 'stayed the same'{{cite:thread-278112-p07|post #134, Dream, 25 May 2021}}{{cite:thread-278112-p07|post #136, Dream, 25 May 2021}}. No public rosters of the new blocs were ever posted{{cite:community-guild-timeline|11 May 2021 rosters}}. Why both alliances fell on the same day is not recorded.

## Aftermath

The day ended the [[artemis-goose-era|Artemis-Goose era]] and began the Valhalla one{{cite:community-guild-timeline|11 May 2021 entry}}. The [[valhalla-khaos-war|Valhalla-Khaos war]] began the day both blocs formed and outlived them both in their original shapes. The collapse also fixed the shape of guild politics for the following year: Valhalla's line ran through [[Vanir]] to the great 2022 realignment{{cite:chronicle-records|Goose, Artemis, Valhalla and Khaos}}, and Khaos's guilds were eventually absorbed into [[Cucumber Company]]{{cite:thread-278112-p08|post #160, TherapueticLiz, 26 Jun 2022}}.

articles.title: The Guild Update
articles.summary: Guilds and guild wars were introduced to Wynncraft in version 1.13, the Wynnter Update, released on 22 December 2014 — the starting point of all guild warfare history.
articles.body:
Guilds were introduced to Wynncraft in version 1.13 — the 'Wynnter Update' — released on 22 December 2014{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guilds|Official Wynncraft Wiki, 'Guilds'}}{{cite:https://wynncraft.fandom.com/wiki/Version_1.13|Wynncraft Wiki (Fandom), 'Version 1.13'}}, and guild wars have existed since the same update{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-war|Official Wynncraft Wiki, 'Guild War'}}. Per the official wiki, guilds 'were originally going to just be permanent parties'{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guilds|Official Wynncraft Wiki, 'Guilds'}}; instead they became territorial powers, and the war system introduced here is the one under which the entire [[early-guild-era|early guild era]] and [[federation-era|Federation era]] were fought.

In the original system, players accessed the Guild Master through a teleporter in Troms (moved to the Guild Hall in the 1.14 Gavel expansion of 2015){{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guilds|Official Wynncraft Wiki, 'Guilds'}}. The 1.13-era war mechanics — including mob-wave wars fought on dedicated war servers, with territories generating XP — survived with incremental changes for six years, until the ground-up rework in version 1.20 'Gavel Reborn' (20 January 2021{{cite:thread-281822|post #1, 20 Jan 2021}}{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, 'Guilds & Wars' sections, 23 Nov 2020}}; see [[territory-warfare|Territory warfare]] and [[guild-seasons|Guild seasons]]).

Every era article on this wiki descends from this update: the first territorial powers of 2015–2016, the [[HackForums]] dominance, and everything after (see [[history-of-wynncraft-guild-warfare|History of Wynncraft guild warfare]]).
articles.leadImageCaption: A tier 1 guild banner, the customisable emblem each guild carries.

articles.title: The Hive
articles.summary: The Hive [THI] was a Wynncraft guild of 2018 named after a territory, which it took 621 times — more than any other guild. It belonged to the Federation and to Valkyrie at once, argued the small guilds' case inside the first, and left on 27 October 2018 without giving a reason, leaving its own leaders unable to say which alliance it had left.
articles.body:
## The guild and the territory

The guild was named after a piece of ground it could not be given. Hive was the fourth most fought-over territory on the map between 30 March and 8 October 2018, changing hands 3,233 times{{cite:territory-exchanges|Hive captures, 30 Mar – 8 Oct 2018}} — but the three above it and the one below were Lava Lake, Detlas, Temple of Legends and the Emerald Trail, and all five sat on the alliance's published free-for-all list, open to anyone.{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|FFA declarations, 2018}} Ground at the top of that table turned over because nobody was permitted to keep it.

What is particular to this guild is the share. The Hive took its namesake 626 times, more than any other guild, ahead of [[fantasy|Fantasy]] at 507 and Lunatic at 412.{{cite:territory-exchanges|Hive captures by attacker, 30 Mar – 8 Oct 2018}} Roughly one Hive in five was taken by the guild named after it, on ground the alliance had declared nobody could hold.

Its own war activity rose sharply through the same period: 44 recorded transitions in March 2018, 787 in April, 856 in May, 3,340 in June and 2,589 in July.{{cite:the-hive-guild-profile-discord-private|war transitions by month, Mar–Jul 2018: 44, 787, 856, 3,340, 2,589}} The fourfold rise in June is the month at least four guilds attacked it at once.{{cite:the-hive-guild-profile-discord-private|June 2018}}

## In two alliances at once

It was admitted to the Federation on 20 February 2018, after a period of helping the alliance's war effort without being a member, and the vote to admit it passed comfortably.{{cite:the-hive-guild-profile-discord-private|20 Feb 2018}} It joined [[valkyrie|Valkyrie]] around March 2018 while sitting inside [[the-federation|the Federation]], one of several guilds in both at the same time.{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}} By May a member of the alliance's largest guild was remarking that this relatively new guild had nearly caught the scores of guilds that had existed for years.{{cite:the-hive-guild-profile-discord-private|May 2018}}

Its own members traced the campaign against it to a split on the other side, recording that the opposing alliance's leader turned on the guild after one of his own allies broke away from him and aligned with it.{{cite:the-hive-guild-profile-discord-private|2018}} That is the Federation side's explanation of an enemy's motive, and it is the kind of account that tidies a war into a personal grievance; nothing from the other bloc stands beside it. For most of its membership it argued the small guilds' case: in March 2018 its leader raised that the larger allies were taking territory assigned to weaker guilds and defending it as their own{{cite:the-hive-guild-profile-discord-private|March 2018}} — the complaint that runs through the whole of the alliance's second half.

In September 2018, when a map revision moved several high-value territories away from the guild, its representative confronted the alliance's map-maker, and in the same discussion its leader offered to hand her position to someone else.{{cite:the-hive-guild-profile-discord-private|September 2018}} Whether anyone took up the offer was never recorded.

## Asking to be stripped

On 26 July 2018 the guild asked [[the-federation|the Federation]] to take almost all of its territory away.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-july-2018-discord-private|26 Jul 2018, the motion}} It put to the voting channel that the next map should assign it three named territories and nothing else.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-july-2018-discord-private|26 Jul 2018, the three territories}} It was consistently a priority target for the opposition, it said, and the change would take the pressure off it, free ground for the other member guilds and for the free-for-all pool, and let it defend less and help its allies more — while conceding that its enemies might follow it onto whatever it kept.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-july-2018-discord-private|26 Jul 2018, the case made}} It asked the alliance's view before putting the change forward, and nine accounts approved, four objected and two recorded themselves indifferent.{{cite:federation-ballot-record-july-2018-discord-private|26 Jul 2018, the reactions}} The map ratified on 1 August was the next one the alliance passed.{{cite:federation-map-votes-july-august-2018-discord-private|poll results, 13 Jul – 16 Aug 2018}} Three months later the guild left the alliance without giving a reason. The rest of the month's motions are at [[federation-ballots-july-2018|the Federation's ballots in July 2018]].

## The departure nobody could define

The Hive left the Federation on 27 October 2018 without giving a public reason, announcing that it would go independent and fight no more wars.{{cite:the-hive-guild-profile-discord-private|27 Oct 2018}}{{cite:federation-collapse-2018-discord-private|Federation leadership channels, 27 Oct 2018}} A leader then asked in the channel whether it had left Valkyrie as well or only the Federation, and nothing in the record answers him.{{cite:the-hive-guild-profile-discord-private|October 2018}} That is a fact about the alliances rather than about the guild: two overlapping memberships, one guild holding both, and no mechanism anywhere for saying which of them a departure ended.

Its neutrality lasted about a fortnight. It began retaliating against whoever had taken its old ground; two days after the announcement a player from a Federation member guild attacked it on his own initiative, which members recorded as pushing a guild that had been inclined to help them into hostility instead; and a further row over a member taking a toll territory for the experience finished it.{{cite:the-hive-guild-profile-discord-private|late October 2018}}{{cite:federation-collapse-2018-discord-private|Federation war channel, late October 2018}} The alliance was left arguing whether an unwritten understanding not to attack the guild still applied, one member observing that sparing it while fighting its allies made no sense.{{cite:the-hive-guild-profile-discord-private|November 2018}} Its leadership had put the case publicly two days after the guild left: it was advisable not to attack The Hive, because it was attempting to help the Federation but would target any guild that attacked Hive, and Federation guilds attacking it were working against their own alliance.{{cite:federation-alliance-announcements|Drew1011, 10/29/2018}}

## Afterwards

The guild reappeared the following year. In September 2019 members of a later alliance recorded a long-dormant guild of that name holding territory again, and remembered it as a guild of the Valkyrie era.{{cite:the-hive-guild-profile-discord-private|September 2019}}

Its departure was the first of the five that emptied the Federation in the fortnight before [[the-federation-dies|it dissolved]] on 10 November 2018.{{cite:federation-collapse-2018-discord-private|Federation leadership channels, 27–30 Oct 2018}} Nothing connects the September argument to the October silence, and no reason for the departure was ever given.

articles.title: The Long Raid
articles.summary: A roughly week-long siege of Aequitas's claim in the Sky province, late July to early August 2024 - the only battle of its era with a first-person retelling, the video 'Wynncraft Warring - The Long Raid' by Frank Wynncraft. The attackers were never named, and the outcome is not known.

infobox.label: Dates
infobox.value: late Jul - early Aug 2024 (~28 Jul - 4 Aug)

articles.body:
The retelling that makes it the only documented battle of [[private-diplomacy-era|its era]] is the video 'Wynncraft Warring - The Long Raid' by Frank Wynncraft, which premiered on 4 August 2024{{cite:youtube-com-watch-v-rlrh14ns6ok|premiered 4 Aug 2024}}, followed by a forum post of 9 August 2024 in which Defervesco linked it - '[[Aequitas]]'s claim in sky was under siege for some time last week. Enjoy this retelling of the war!'{{cite:thread-318070|post #1, Defervesco, 9 Aug 2024}}

{{map:2024-07-28|The map during the siege}}

## Background

The raid falls inside the window of the [[idiot-co-aquarium-war|Idiot Co-Aquarium war]], the era's dominant conflict{{cite:territory-exchanges|Idiot Co-Aquarium war window, Apr–Jul 2024}}, but is described in the retelling as small-guild warfare rather than part of that war's main front{{cite:youtube-com-watch-v-rlrh14ns6ok|premiered 4 Aug 2024}}.

## Course of the war

The attackers besieged Aequitas's Sky-province claim for about a week{{cite:territory-exchanges|siege window, ~28 Jul – 4 Aug 2024}}. The attackers were never named, and the outcome was not recorded.

## Aftermath

Nothing further is recorded. The video is a rare first-person account from a period when almost all guild diplomacy and war reporting had moved to private channels.

'Wynncraft Warring' is not a series: of the thirteen videos on Frank Wynncraft's channel, only this one carries the title{{cite:chronicle-records|section 6: Frank Wynncraft channel enumeration from the Wayback capture of 8 May 2026}}. The rest are build, market, raid and update videos.
articles.leadImageCaption: Thumbnail of Frank Wynncraft's video 'Wynncraft Warring - The Long Raid', premiered 4 August 2024.

articles.title: The Mage Legacy
articles.summary: Wynncraft guild created in October 2016 and led by CalAnders ever since — one of the longest unbroken guild ownerships on record. It joined Goose in March 2021, was a founding member of Valhalla, and was one of the two guilds excluded when Valhalla reorganized as Vanir.
articles.body:
The Mage Legacy's owner, CalAnders, joined at the moment of the guild's creation and was still its owner in September 2026 — an unbroken tenure of nearly ten years, and one of the longest on record{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-the-20mage-20legacy|v3/guild response, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}.

## History

### The Emperium of Wynn (2017)

The Mage Legacy first appears as an alliance member in the [[emperium-of-wynn|Emperium of Wynn]], listed as 'The Mage Legacy (Mag) - Owner: CalAnders' among the alliance's current guilds in May 2017{{cite:thread-188024|post #4 (quoting the OP as it then stood), 7 May 2017}}; by August 2017 the guild had been moved to the alliance's 'Honored Retired Guilds' list{{cite:thread-188024|post #1 (OP), 'Honored Retired Guilds', as of 8 Aug 2017}}. CalAnders himself posted in the thread on the day it opened{{cite:thread-188024|post #5, 7 May 2017}}. Nothing more was recorded of the guild for almost four years.

### Goose and Valhalla (2021)

The Mage Legacy joined [[Goose]] on 30 March 2021, during the [[goose-artemis-war|Goose-Artemis war]]{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. That same day [[drasalia|Drasalia]] of ChinaNumberOne posted an illustrated roster of six Goose guilds headed 'MAG - The Mage Legacy' — 'just my doodles of what I think the Guilds would look like if they were people'{{cite:thread-289196|post #1, 30 Mar 2021}}.

When Goose and [[Artemis]] fell together on 11 May 2021 ([[the-great-collapse|the Great Collapse]]), The Mage Legacy was one of the thirteen founding guilds of [[Valhalla]], the bloc that took the map from Goose's remnants{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}.

### Excluded from Vanir

Friction between The Mage Legacy, [[thenolifes|TheNoLifes]] and their Valhalla allies appears from August 2021, months before any open break{{cite:territory-exchanges|Mage Legacy and TheNoLifes friction from August 2021}}. Both guilds were left out when Valhalla's remaining members reorganized as [[Vanir]] on 28 November 2021, and open war followed that December ([[the-betrayal-of-valhalla|the betrayal of Valhalla]]){{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. Where The Mage Legacy went afterwards was never recorded; unlike TheNoLifes, which passed into [[Khaos]], it appears in no later alliance roster.

As of September 2026 the guild remains active at level 90 with 87 members and 13,368 recorded wars, holding no territories{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-the-20mage-20legacy|v3/guild response, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}.

## Alliances

- [[emperium-of-wynn|Emperium of Wynn]] — by 7 May 2017; a retired guild by August 2017{{cite:thread-188024|post #4 and post #1 (OP), 2017}}
- [[Goose]] — 30 Mar – 11 May 2021
- [[Valhalla]] — 11 May – 28 Nov 2021 (founding member)

articles.title: The map refilled
articles.summary: What occupied the ground taken on the night of 7 September 2019. Over the three months that followed, Terra's war channel repeatedly could not say who held the territory beside it — guilds reformed under new names, tags out of the Valkyrie era, and one subguild that had become a single hostile player. Terra dissolved on 30 December with Imperial, the guild it was founded to drive off the map, holding more of it than anyone.

articles.title: The Nameless Samurai
articles.summary: A Wynncraft guild created in September 2023 that held 59 of the map's 437 territories in the census of 3 September 2026 - level with Avicia and behind only Sequoia. No forum thread, newsletter, video or narrative account of it was ever written; two API captures are the whole of its record.
articles.body:
## What the record contains

The Nameless Samurai [TNSR] was created on 28 September 2023{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-the-20nameless-20samurai|guild record, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}. The guild's API record of 3 September 2026 lists makugon as owner and ten chiefs - _Snowy_, pozicoco, yayo_dayo, sutiru_, DOBUMASUO, nasinasi820, suraimu1233301, aoiei, tamago_256 and xX_ThinkiFace_Xx - across 84 members at guild level 77, with 12,345 lifetime wars and 1,979 raids{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-the-20nameless-20samurai|owner, chiefs, member total, level and lifetime counts, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}. On the same day it held 59 of the map's 437 territories - level with [[Avicia]] and behind only [[Sequoia]]'s 62{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-list-territory|full territory ownership snapshot, 3 Sep 2026}}.

Those figures sit oddly beside its holdings. Of the six largest holders in the census it has the fewest members, the lowest guild level, and by an order of magnitude the fewest lifetime wars. [[Avicia]], on the same 59 territories, records 227,706 wars{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-avicia|lifetime war count, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}; [[Sequoia]] records 161,494{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-sequoia|lifetime war count, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}; [[KongoBoys]], on roughly half the territory, records 98,864{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-kongoboys|lifetime war count, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}. How a guild with a five-figure war count came to hold as much land as one with a six-figure war count was never documented.

The season record says the same thing from the other side. The guild's season ratings run from Season 14 (1,300) through Season 32 (590,577), peaking at 2,416,820 in Season 24{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-the-20nameless-20samurai|seasonRanks, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}} - roughly a fifth of the totals that won seasons over the same years, which ran between 10 and 14.6 million{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|season winners table, Seasons 19-25}}. By season rating the guild was never a contender for a crown; by territory count it was second on the map.

## The claim

The 59 territories formed a single regional bloc in central Gavel rather than a scattered holding: the guild's headquarters was Cinfras Outskirts, and the claim ran through Cinfras and its approaches, the Aldorei valley, Gelibord, Lexdale, Thanos, Kander, Efilim and the Forgery{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-list-territory|TNSR territory list and HQ, 3 Sep 2026}}. No written source describes the guild's holdings.

## An undocumented power

No other record of the period mentions the guild. It has no recruitment or guild thread on the Wynncraft forums: of the eleven guild threads of substance posted between 2023 and 2026, none is TNSR's{{cite:chronicle-records|section 9, forum tag sweeps recorded as complete}}. It is named in none of the twenty-one volumes of [[titan-times|Titan Times]], the era's only regularly published newsletter{{cite:chronicle-records|section 8, Titan Times vols. 14-21 name no outside guild}}, and in none of the in-game chat records captured by [[Sequoia]]'s client mod in 2026{{cite:raw-githubusercontent-com-sequoiawynncraft-sequoia-mod-main-src-test-java-com-seqwawa-|ChatManagerTest fixtures}}. No war involving it is recorded, no alliance, no leadership change, no founding account and no disband notice. Nobody wrote it down.

That absence is the ordinary condition of [[private-diplomacy-era|the private-diplomacy era]], in which the last alliance thread on the forums is dated 21 November 2022 and guild politics moved into private Discords{{cite:thread-322643|post #1, IceResistance, 2 Oct 2025}}. The Nameless Samurai is the sharpest single case of it: a guild founded ten months after that last thread, which reached the top of the map entirely inside the silence.

Its nearest parallel is ten years earlier. [[Libertas]] held 60 of roughly 332 territories on 23 September 2016, second only to [[HackForums]], and its scale was likewise recorded only once{{cite:pre2018-territory-snapshots|pre2018-territory-snapshots.json — Wayback Machine capture of the Wynncraft v1 API guild leaderboard, 23 Sep 2016}}; not one of its wars was ever written down. The two cases bracket the record: at its start and at its present end, a first-rank territorial power exists as a number and almost nothing else.

## Alliances

None recorded. The Nameless Samurai appears in no recorded war or community alliance, and its founding postdates the last public alliance roster by more than a year{{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #160, TherapueticLiz, 26 Jun 2022}}. Nor does it appear in the in-game ally records captured from June 2026 - a game-mechanical registration used chiefly to permit allied guilds to run guild raids together{{cite:raw-githubusercontent-com-sequoiawynncraft-sequoia-mod-main-src-test-java-com-seqwawa-|ChatManagerTest alliance-message fixtures}}.

articles.title: The rank and file
articles.summary: Almost all of the written history of the 2015-16 guild alliances came from the people running them. One account was written from inside the ranks instead — by a Holders of LE member who had lost three small guilds in four months, applied to a large one through the game's forums, and then fought a war nobody had explained to him.

infobox.label: Guilds described
infobox.value: Team United [TUN] and two others; [[holders-of-le|Holders of LE]]

articles.body:
The alliances of 2015 and 2016 were written up almost entirely by the people conducting them. One account came from underneath: over two evenings in April 2018 a member of [[holders-of-le|Holders of LE]] posted 117 messages on how the era had looked to a low-level player who arrived late, held no office and was told very little.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|2 and 7 Apr 2018, 117 messages}}

## The record

Its author gave his method at the outset and returned to it later: he was working back through his own old game logs rather than through any document kept at the time.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|2 Apr 2018, the stated method}}{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|7 Apr 2018, the method described again}} The logs were private and were never published, which cuts both ways. A log keeps the wording of exchanges memory alone would lose; it also means that where the account gives a date, there is no telling whether the date came off a log or out of the author's head.

He wrote it against another account. He opened by setting himself beside the author of the [[guild-histories|longer serialised history]] of the same years, who had kept organised records of the major guild events where he himself had only old logs to search{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|2 Apr 2018, the opening comparison}}, and he began his second instalment by comparing his own version of the first great alliance with that author's.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|7 Apr 2018, the two versions compared}} He had read the other history before writing his own. Where the two agree about alliance politics he did not see for himself, one of them is a reader of the other rather than a second witness; where he describes his own guild, nobody else wrote it down.

The account also dates the central event of its own story two ways. In the first instalment he emptied his guild of its members on 28 November 2015 and took a further eight days to disband it{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|first instalment, 2 Apr 2018, the disbanding}}; in the second he gave the disbandment as 3 December 2016 and his admission to Holders of LE three days after that.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|second instalment, 7 Apr 2018, the disbanding}} The narrative between the two statements is one continuous sequence, so both cannot stand, and nothing in the two evenings decides between them. The year matters more than the day, because a year moves him between alliances: Holders of LE was a founding member of [[ordo-malleus|Ordo Malleus]] from 6 November 2015{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L169–178, composed 22 Feb 2018}} and had gone into hibernation on 1 December 2016, two days before the later date.{{cite:gdoc-1bbnalbfij8cjnog|Dec 2016}} Setting the two datings against the guild's own timeline is this article's reading, and it settles neither. Elsewhere the same account is chronologically careful in a way that tells against reading it as careless: he fixes the end of the alliance not by naming a date but by counting the months he was away from the game, and lands in the month the alliance did in fact collapse.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|the absences and the remark, in message order}}{{cite:holders-of-le-guild-profile-discord-private|the collapse of 9 Mar 2016}} An account can be exact about elapsed time and wrong about a calendar year, and this one is both.

## Three guilds in four months

He joined his first guild at a low level in August 2015 and left it, or was put out of it, shortly afterwards.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|the first guild, August 2015}} A second recruited him in early September and promoted him before its founder stopped playing and it decayed around him.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|the second guild, September 2015}} He then founded his own, Team United [TUN], which reached about eighteen members and roughly the guild level of the one before it, and emptied in its turn.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|Team United, autumn 2015}} Nothing else was ever written down about any of the three.

The reason he gave for his own guild's failure was a recruiting reason rather than a military one: he had taken members only from players he already met in the game instead of advertising for them{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|the stated reason for the guild's failure}}, and a player who plays at one time of day runs out of people to meet.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|playing hours and the pool of recruits}} Small guilds of the period, on his description, spent their effort trying to bring down the largest guilds on the map.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|small guilds against the largest guilds of the period}}

## Applying through the forums

Getting into a large guild meant going through the game's public forums. He had never used them; he made an account for the sole purpose of submitting his application to [[holders-of-le|Holders of LE]], and the application was his first post there.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|the forum application}} He had narrowed the choice to three guilds of the same alliance and took the smaller one, which still had room to grow and which he put at about level forty at the time.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|choosing among three guilds of the alliance}} He did not disband his own guild until he knew the application had been accepted, keeping it alive eight days as somewhere to go back to if it was refused.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|the eight-day fallback}}

## A war nobody had explained

The members of his guild were not told why their alliance was fighting. He wrote that he and the people around him were largely unaware of the disputes among the senior ranks, and that what reached them came as fragments from the chiefs.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|what the ranks knew of the alliance's quarrels}} Some of them did not know which guild a war was against or what it was about, and they fought it because it was exciting.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|not knowing the enemy or the reason}} He kept friendships with members of two of the enemy guilds throughout.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|friendships across the war}}

That is one member of one guild describing what he and the people near him knew, and a recruit not being given a war's reason is not the same as no reason having been given: [[ordo-malleus|Ordo Malleus]] sets out what the leaders of the period argued about.

## An alliance with no opposition

The alliance ruled the whole guild scene for as long as he played under it, and in his description players divided into those who wanted to join it and those who wanted to bring it down.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|the alliance's dominance}} Several rival alliances were formed against it in those months and none of them came to anything.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|the rival alliances}} He put himself in the first camp, joining because he wanted to know what belonging to a large and active guild was like{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|his reason for joining}}; once inside it he made it his business to clear smaller guilds off the map.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|what he did once inside}}

Two rival alliances are dated to the months he describes. Vesta was opened on a forum thread on 10 December 2015{{cite:forums-wynncraft-com-forums-guilds-72-prefix-id-82-order-post-date-direction-asc|census of Alliance-prefixed threads, page 1: Vesta, 3zPz, Dec 10, 2015}} and declared dead a month later, having barely fought at all{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L289–311, composed 19 Jan 2018}}; the Astrafteri Affinity was founded around January 2016 against [[ordo-malleus|Ordo Malleus]]{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L352–358, composed 19 Jan 2018}} and outlived it by months without ever displacing it.{{cite:gdoc-1bbnalbfij8cjnog|Jan 2016 and Mar 2016}} Setting the two beside his description is this article's reading.

## The Gavel update

He dated the release of the Gavel province to 21 December 2015 and described the guild system failing around it, with guild wars not working at all for the first week and the guild chat broken with them.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|the Gavel release and the week after it}} He listed faults he said had predated the update and been made worse by it: players not teleported into the wars they had started, war mobs failing to spawn, and whole servers stalling when a territory was defended.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|the faults he described}} His judgement was that the update brought the wider player community back and killed the guild community with it.{{cite:holders-of-le-storytime-2018-discord-private|his judgement on the update}} The date is the one [[early-guild-era|the older account also gives]]{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L315–325, composed 26 Feb 2018}}, and the two are not independent of each other.

articles.title: The realignment era
articles.summary: May 2021 to mid-2023: Valhalla and Khaos rose from the Great Collapse and fought for a year, Vanir lived twenty days, and the 2022 realignment merged both worlds into Cucumber Company - later smtn elf - until The Aquarium and Avicia walked out in June 2023.
articles.body:
{{map:2022-06-26|The map on the day of the last public alliance roster}}

The realignment era began with two blocs at war, the survivors of [[the-great-collapse|the Great Collapse]], and ended with nearly all of them inside [[smtn elf]] — the last era with a public alliance record. It is also the first era with a published scoreboard: [[guild-seasons|guild seasons]] launched on 5 July 2021{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|Season 0, 5-7 Jul 2021}}, eight weeks into it, and from then on the map's politics can be read against a table of winners.

## Valhalla and Khaos

On 11 May 2021 thirteen guilds including [[The Aquarium]] formed [[Valhalla]] while nine ex-[[Goose]] guilds formed [[Khaos]]{{cite:thread-278112-p07|p7 #134-137, 25 May 2021}}, and the [[valhalla-khaos-war|Valhalla-Khaos war]] began the same day{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. Valhalla took map control within days and dominated the year - 'the meta of being top 10 on the guild sr leaderboard is to join valhalla', a September 2021 forum post complained{{cite:thread-295680|post #1, IamFye, 25 Sep 2021}}. Fighting was sustained at roughly a thousand exchanges a week at its peaks, continuing into spring 2022{{cite:territory-exchanges|Valhalla-Khaos weekly exchange volumes, 2021-22}}.

The season table bears the complaint out only partly. Season 1 (9 Jul - 20 Sep 2021) went to [[ShadowFall]], Season 2 to [[Emorians]], Season 3 to The Aquarium, Season 4 to Nefarious Ravens{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|season table, Seasons 1-4}} - four different winners in a year, three of them Valhalla-line guilds and the first of them a guild that had defected from [[Artemis]] to Goose eight months earlier.

## Betrayal and the twenty days of Vanir

In late 2021 The Mage Legacy and TheNoLifes turned on their Valhalla allies - friction visible from August, erupting into open war in December (5,359 territory exchanges that month){{cite:territory-exchanges|December 2021 territory exchanges}}. Both were excluded when ten Valhalla guilds reorganized as [[Vanir]] on 28 November 2021{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. Vanir lasted twenty days: on 18 December [[Emorians]], Nefarious Ravens, IceBlue Team and [[Avicia]] left and it collapsed; [[Niflheim]] officially dissolved the same day{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. Khaos's war against the ex-Valhalla guilds - its opponents known as the Pineapple Pact, a name never written down at the time{{cite:cameron-oral-history|Cameron (TAq veteran) oral testimony, fact-checked against map data}} - peaked in January 2022 at 500-800 territory exchanges per week and faded to nothing by mid-July{{cite:territory-exchanges|Khaos war volumes, Jan-Jul 2022}}.

## Cucumber Company and smtn elf

The 2022 realignment merged the ex-Valhalla and ex-Khaos worlds into [[Cucumber Company]], formed for guild Season 5 - 'our first season being a part of the new Cucumber Company war alliance', wrote [[titan-times|Titan Times]]{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol1|vol. 1, 8 May 2022}}. Season 5 ran from 3 March to 2 May 2022{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|season table, Season 5}}. Its 14-guild roster, posted to [[the-forum-megalist|the forum megalist]] on 26 June 2022{{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #160, TherapueticLiz, 26 Jun 2022}}, was the last public alliance roster ever; the megalist's alliance section was deleted twelve days later{{cite:thread-278112-p09|p9 #161, Sg_Voltage, 7 Jul 2022}}. At the start of Season 8, which began on 12 September 2022{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|season table, Season 8}}, 'Cucumber was archived. The new alliance name is called Smtn else' - the same newsletter recording Gang of Fools having 'left and betrayed the alliance' and welcoming [[Paladins United]], [[The Simple Ones]] and TerraLune{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol6|vol. 6, 12 Oct 2022}}. Renamed 'smtn elf' for Christmas 2022 and never changed back{{cite:cameron-oral-history|Cameron (TAq veteran) oral testimony, fact-checked against map data}}, the super-alliance was crowned - satirically - 'unquestionably the greatest super-alliance of 2023' that February{{cite:thread-306790|Wynncraft forums thread 306790, 17 Feb 2023}}. In spring 2023 busted moments and [[Idiot Co]] joined{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol9|vol. 9, 25 Mar 2023}}. Meanwhile the community layer turned over: as [[Hestia]] declined, the leaders of [[Titans Valor]] and Empire of Sindria founded [[Adonis]] around May 2022 as its effective successor{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol1|vol. 1, 8 May 2022}}.

Under the super-alliance the crown circulated among its own members - The Aquarium in Season 5, KongoBoys in Season 6, [[Avicia]] in Season 7, The Aquarium again in Season 8 - and then stopped circulating. Avicia won Seasons 9 through 13 without a break, from October 2022 to August 2023{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|season table, Seasons 5-13}}, a run that begins inside smtn elf and ends after it.

## The Eden coup

Somewhere in this period [[Eden]], a founding guild of Khaos, was overthrown from within. A player called xK6TA, applying to [[Titans Valor]] in April 2023, wrote: 'I was a part of Eden when it was #1 and slightly after it got couped.'{{cite:thread-206094-p97|p97 #1922, 16 Apr 2023}} The coup's actors and date were never recorded, beyond that it happened by April 2023, and what '#1' meant is not known - Eden never won a guild season{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|season table, Seasons 0-26}}.

## The view from outside

The super-alliance drew public mockery. In November 2022 a thread announced the "Anti Alliance Alliance", whose stated purpose was "to spread chaos between guilds in the Generic Mega Alliance #472856 by taking random territories on the map and putting there max tax", and which advertised that "our members have achieved literally nothing"; three players joined over the following month.{{cite:thread-305152|posts #1–4, Nov–Dec 2022}} Its name was a joke on [[alliance-alliance|Alliance Alliance]] of 2018 and it had no connection to it.

## The end

In June 2023 The Aquarium and Avicia quit smtn elf, rejecting pressure to shrink their claims{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}, and opened [[the-avocado-split|the Avocado split]] against their former allies. smtn elf was last mentioned in Avicia's season post of 10 June 2023{{cite:thread-308780|Avicia guild thread, season post of 10 Jun 2023}}, in the closing days of the Season 12 it had won; its end was never announced. With it ended the era of publicly named alliances, and [[private-diplomacy-era|the private diplomacy era]] began.

articles.title: The wipe of HackForums
articles.summary: Over 19-20 February 2018, days after forming, the Federation took every territory HackForums held; by 22 February 2018 it held none, ending Hax as a territorial power a year after its peak of roughly 350 territories. It is the event behind the community memory of "the fall of Hax", which is usually misdated to 2017.

infobox.label: Date
infobox.value: 19 Feb 2018; zero territories by 22 Feb 2018{{cite:thread-219744|post #1, 22 Feb 2018}}

infobox.label: Outcome
infobox.value: HackForums reduced from 111 territories to zero; no guild then held more than 43{{cite:thread-219744|post #1, 22 Feb 2018}}

articles.body:
The capture log has Hax at 96 territories at the start of 19 February 2018 and 108 by midday, then falling through the 20th — 98 at midnight, 79 at 06:00, 25 at noon and none by 18:00 UTC{{cite:territory-exchanges|holdings reconstructed from the capture log, 19-22 Feb 2018 UTC}}; it held zero on 22 February 2018{{cite:thread-219744|post #1, 22 Feb 2018}}. It ended Hax's years as a territorial power.

{{map:2018-02-19|The map on the day of the wipe}}

## Background

HackForums was the dominant territorial guild of the mid-2010s. In September 2016 Hax held 146 of roughly 332 held territories — more than double the next guild, [[Libertas]] (60), with UltimateXeons third (53){{cite:pre2018-territory-snapshots|pre2018-territory-snapshots.json — Wayback Machine capture of the Wynncraft v1 API guild leaderboard, 23 Sep 2016}}. Its 2017 peak approached 350 territories{{cite:thread-265297|post #18, 4 Apr 2020}}. It held that map at the head of a bloc, not alone: [[HackForums]], Libertas [Lir] and Blacklisted [BLA], with UltimateXeons [UXs] a party to the pact in mid-2016{{cite:thread-133666|post #13, 27 Jun 2016}}{{cite:thread-143392|post #12, 9 Aug 2016}}{{cite:thread-131893|post #1, as revised 15 Sep 2017}}. Contemporaries had no name for the arrangement, calling it "a mutual land agreement"{{cite:thread-133666|post #16, 28 Jun 2016}}; the label "Hax & Co" was a later community coinage, first recorded in July 2019{{cite:thread-252647|post #5, 21 Jul 2019}}. No exchange-level war data from before 2018 was ever published{{cite:territory-exchanges|earliest row in the table, 3 Jan 2018 20:22:23 UTC; nothing precedes it}}.

By early 2018 Hax was a member of the [[Coalition]], and on 16–17 February 2018 it left with the breakaway [[Alliance Alliance]] bloc, starting the [[coalition-civil-war|Coalition Civil War]]{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. [[the-federation|The Federation]] — formed on 16 February 2018 from the Coalition remnant and War Syndicate's remains — was three days old when it struck{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}.

## Course of the war

Both surviving accounts put the guild higher and the attack a day earlier than the log does, and they agree with each other. The community timeline image reads "Feb 19 2018 Fed attacks Hax's 111 territories and wipes them to 0 in under 12 hours"{{cite:thread-265297|post #1, DerpyEmerald24's guild-history timeline image (i.imgur.com/seklYAQ.png), 28 Jul 2020}}, and Drew1011 has Hall of Fame's Snowythewolf calling the attack "at the very latest hours of the 19th", with Hax on "111 territoires" and none "less than 10 hours later"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|part 17, composed 30 Aug 2018}}. The two reconcile with the log once the clocks are lined up: the latest hours of the 19th in Eastern time are the early hours of the 20th in UTC, which is where the log puts the collapse, and both durations match its run from 79 territories at 06:00 to none at 18:00. The guilds that took them were [[kingdom-foxes|Kingdom Foxes]] (92 territories), [[Fantasy]] (56), [[Imperial]] (41), [[holders-of-le|Holders Of LE]] (38), The Divine Swords (37) and The Hive (32){{cite:territory-exchanges|holdings reconstructed from the capture log, 19-22 Feb 2018 UTC}}. A thread of 22 February 2018, "Haxforums Has Fallen At Last.", announced: "After years of being number 1, HaxForums has lost all its territories. Now its much easier to be on the leaderboard, since the guilds with the most territories have only 43. Everyone celebrate!"{{cite:thread-219744|post #1, 22 Feb 2018}} A moderator closed the thread four minutes and two replies later{{cite:thread-219744|post #3, 22 Feb 2018}}. No fuller account of the fighting survives: the attacking guilds, the order of the territories, and how the 19 February attack relates to the 22 February result were never recorded.

## Aftermath

Hax's land was dispersed rather than inherited: no guild held more than 43 territories immediately afterwards{{cite:thread-219744|post #1, 22 Feb 2018}}. In community memory the event is usually placed a year earlier — one participant called the fall of Hax "probably the biggest event that happened in 2017"{{cite:thread-265297|post #16, 4 Apr 2020}} — but the recollection is about two months out: 2017 was the decline, and the fall itself belongs to February 2018 and to the Federation rather than to the [[Coalition]]{{cite:thread-219744|post #1, 22 Feb 2018}}.

The guild itself survived: it held 33 territories in March 2019{{cite:pre2018-territory-snapshots|pre2018-territory-snapshots.json — Wayback Machine capture of the Wynncraft v1 API guild leaderboard, 3 Mar 2019}}, and it was later a member of [[Valhalla]] (2021){{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}} and the [[Hestia]] community alliance (June 2021){{cite:thread-278112-p07-wb20211128|post #140, 6 Jun 2021}} — but it never again approached its 2016–17 scale.

articles.title: TheDarkSoul
articles.summary: Owner of the war guild HackForums from its creation on 24 December 2014, presiding over its 2016-17 territorial hegemony of up to roughly 350 territories.
articles.body:
TheDarkSoul owned the guild [[HackForums]] [Hax]. The guild's recruitment thread named him in every recovered revision, its header reading "HackForums [Hax] Lvl. 92 - Created 12/24/2014 / Guild Owner: TheDarkSoul"{{cite:thread-109319|post #1 (OP)}}. By the 2019 revision the thread no longer described a war guild at all: "This is a community guild, we do not war."{{cite:thread-109319-wb20190723|post #1 (OP), Wayback Machine capture 23 Jul 2019}} Day-to-day forum-keeping fell to officers such as Mrussell75 and Christinel8{{cite:thread-109319|thread bumps and replies by Mrussell75 and Christinel8}}; TheDarkSoul himself wrote almost nothing in public.

Under his ownership HackForums became the dominant territorial power of the pre-[[Coalition]] era. On 23 September 2016 Hax held 146 of roughly 332 territories, far ahead of any rival{{cite:pre2018-territory-snapshots|pre-2018 territory snapshots: Wynncraft v1 API guild leaderboard, Wayback capture of 23 Sep 2016}}; a March 2017 complaint thread put its holdings at "100+ territories"{{cite:thread-179383|post #6 (Drew1011), 1 Mar 2017; thread opened by Tntdestroyd the same day}}; by May 2017 it held more than 300{{cite:thread-189768|post #1, Hide007, 22 May 2017}}; and in 2020 Lego_DW placed the peak "closer to 350"{{cite:thread-265297|post #18 (Lego_DW), 4 Apr 2020}}. The hegemony ended in the Coalition-era wars of late 2017 and [[the-wipe-of-hackforums|the wipe of HackForums]] in February 2018.

When, or whether, his ownership ended was never recorded.

articles.title: TheNoLifes
articles.summary: One of the oldest guilds on Wynncraft, founded by Chownick in December 2014, days after guilds were introduced. It served in Ordo Malleus, the Emperium of Wynn, the Federation, Terra, the Council of Canyon Kingdoms, Goose, Niflheim and Valhalla — then turned on Valhalla in late 2021 and helped lead Khaos.

infobox.label: Status
infobox.value: Exists but near-dormant (7 members, no territories, Sep 2026)

articles.body:
TheNoLifes [TNL], also styled Del Morto, was founded on 27 December 2014 by [[chownick|Chownick]] — five days after guilds were added to Wynncraft in [[the-guild-update|the Guild Update]] — 'placing it as one of the oldest guilds in existence since the introduction of the guild system in Wynn'{{cite:thread-306694|post #1 (OP), 11 Feb 2023}}. The official API dates its creation to 28 December 2014{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-thenolifes|v3/guild response, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}; the one-day gap is unexplained.

## History

### Early alliances (2015-2018)

TheNoLifes was among the guilds of [[ordo-malleus|Ordo Malleus]] listed in 2017{{cite:thread-109350|post #1, 'Guilds in Ordo Malleus' list}}, and in the roster of the [[emperium-of-wynn|Emperium of Wynn]] as 'The No Lifes (TNL) - Owner: chownick'{{cite:thread-188024|post #1, member-guild roster}}. It joined [[the-federation|the Federation]] on 5 May 2018{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}, one of the 37 guilds of [[drew1011|Drew1011]]'s Federation Tribute roster{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, member-guild list, 13 Nov 2018}}. When the Federation broke up, a forum post that day named TNL among the core guilds left exposed by the departures: 'leaving Fox, Hax, Imp, TNL, Ern, and a bunch of minor guilds weak'{{cite:thread-236914|post #1 (Glial), 10 Nov 2018}}.

### The 2019 churn

In [[the-alliance-wars-of-2019|the alliance wars of 2019]] it joined [[Terra]] on 30 August, followed the Terra core into the [[council-of-canyon-kingdoms|Council of Canyon Kingdoms]] on 29 September, and stayed until that alliance collapsed on 23 November{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}.

TheNoLifes joined the [[aesir-pact|Aesir Pact]] on 17 November 2018, a week after that bloc left [[the-federation|the Federation]], under written ground rules covering leaking, respect for the alliance's existing pacts with a third alliance, and an obligation to defend the Canyon on request.{{cite:aesir-pact-2018-discord-private|admission, 17 Nov 2018}}

### Goose, Niflheim and Valhalla (2021)

TNL switched sides during the [[goose-artemis-war|Goose-Artemis war]]: on 1 February 2021 [[the-forum-megalist|the forum megalist]] recorded that 'BNU(IBT), SHY and TNL are all goose now'{{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #76, 1 Feb 2021}}. Its membership was still current on 30 March, when [[drasalia|Drasalia]] of ChinaNumberOne drew TNL as one of six Goose guilds and noted its reputation: 'From what my Guild Leader told me, they are the ones that know more about guild politics and all that cool stuff.'{{cite:thread-289196|post #1, 30 Mar 2021}} It joined the community alliance [[Niflheim]] by 7 July 2021{{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #146, 7 Jul 2021}} and was a founding member of [[Valhalla]] on 11 May 2021{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}.

### The break with Valhalla

When Valhalla's guilds reorganized as [[Vanir]] on 28 November 2021, TheNoLifes and [[the-mage-legacy|The Mage Legacy]] were excluded, and open war followed in December ([[the-betrayal-of-valhalla|the betrayal of Valhalla]]){{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. TNL fought in [[Khaos]] from about 1 December 2021 until Khaos was absorbed into [[cucumber-company|Cucumber Company]] in June 2022, and helped lead the alliance{{cite:cameron-oral-history|Cameron oral history (TAq veteran testimony)}}.

### Later years

A recruitment thread of February 2023 presents a revived guild — 'Through time we have encountered challenges and revivals' — under a management team of 'Dons' and 'Consiglieres' with mafia-styled ranks, and names no owner{{cite:thread-306694|post #1 (OP), 11 Feb 2023}}. As of September 2026 the guild stood at level 94 with 33,635 recorded wars but only seven members and no territories, its listed owner last online in November 2024{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-thenolifes|v3/guild response, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}. When Chownick left the leadership is not recorded.

## Alliances

- [[ordo-malleus|Ordo Malleus]] — listed 2017{{cite:thread-109350|post #1, Ordo Malleus guild list}}
- [[emperium-of-wynn|Emperium of Wynn]] — listed 2017{{cite:thread-188024|post #1, member-guild roster}}
- [[the-federation|The Federation]] — 5 May – 10 Nov 2018
- [[Terra]] — 30 Aug – 15 Sep 2019
- [[council-of-canyon-kingdoms|Council of Canyon Kingdoms]] — 29 Sep – 23 Nov 2019
- [[Goose]] — by 1 Feb 2021 – 11 May 2021{{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #76, 1 Feb 2021}}
- [[Valhalla]] — 11 May – 28 Nov 2021
- [[Niflheim]] — 7 Jul – 18 Dec 2021 (community alliance){{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #146, 7 Jul 2021}}
- [[Khaos]] — c. 1 Dec 2021 – Jun 2022

articles.title: Titan Times
articles.summary: Titans Valor's guild newsletter, volumes 1-21 (May 2022 - May 2026): the most important primary source for alliance history after the forum megalist's deletion, documenting Cucumber Company, smtn elf, Hestia's decline and Adonis before turning inward after 2023.

infobox.label: Writers/editors
infobox.value: bitesizedbee4 ('Bee'), GebutterteWurst ('Geb'), Snazz, Aezuh, C0rupted, Talkair, l1npengtul

articles.body:
Twenty-one volumes were published between 8 May 2022{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol1|vol. 1, 8 May 2022}} and 18 May 2026{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol21|vol. 21, 18 May 2026}} (with a gap between vol. 11 of 25 May 2023{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol11|vol. 11, 25 May 2023}} and vol. 12 of 20 February 2024{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol12|vol. 12, 20 Feb 2024}}), hosted at titansvalor.org/news, with the first thirteen volumes mirrored at titantimes.github.io.{{cite:titantimes-github-io-index|volume index}} The guild described it as "Our guild newspaper!" and used it to recruit writers to interview members and report guild affairs.{{cite:titantimes-github-io-index|Titan Times section}} After [[the-forum-megalist|the forum megalist]]'s alliance section was deleted in July 2022, Titan Times became the only regularly published, dated account of alliance affairs - the key primary source for the late [[the-realignment-era|realignment era]].

The masthead changed hands twice. The founding writer and editor was bitesizedbee4 ('Bee'), who carried vols. 1 to 10 (8 May 2022 - 23 Apr 2023){{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol1|vol. 1, 8 May 2022}}{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol10|vol. 10, 23 Apr 2023}}; GebutterteWurst ('Geb'), an ANO Councilor, joined as co-editor from vol. 7 (16 Dec 2022){{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol7|vol. 7, 16 Dec 2022}}; Snazz wrote the recent-happenings column; Aezuh handled visuals and publishing and was still being thanked for reviewing and posting the team's work in vol. 20{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol20|vol. 20, 23 Nov 2025}}; a member credited only as Andrew gave technical support in vol. 2{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol2|vol. 2, 23 May 2022}}; and karapandza appeared as a guest writer in vols. 10 and 11. C0rupted introduced himself as 'the new writer' in vol. 12 (Feb 2024){{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol12|vol. 12, 20 Feb 2024}} and remained on the team through vol. 21{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol21|vol. 21, 18 May 2026}}. From vol. 16 (Nov 2024){{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol16|vol. 16, 4 Nov 2024}} Talkair became the lead voice, credited in vol. 20 with 'not only writing but organising Titan Times for 5 whole editions'{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol20|vol. 20, 23 Nov 2025}}, with Lamplesspost writing the main-stage interviews from vol. 17{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol17|vol. 17, 15 Jan 2025}}. Vol. 21 (18 May 2026) announced another change: l1npengtul took over as Editor-in-Chief, alongside Talkair, DragonZftw and C0rupted, promising a quarterly schedule tied to the start of each guild season from vol. 22 onward{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol21|vol. 21, 18 May 2026}}.

Its most important records are concentrated in the first ten volumes: vol. 1 (8 May 2022) dates [[Cucumber Company]]'s formation to guild Season 5 ('our first season being a part of the new Cucumber Company war alliance') and the founding of [[Adonis]] as [[Hestia]] declined{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol1|vol. 1, 8 May 2022}}; vol. 3 (12 Jun 2022) records IceBlue Team's exit, Gang of Fools' arrival and [[Avicia]] joining Adonis{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol3|vol. 3, 12 Jun 2022}}; vol. 6 (12 Oct 2022) preserves the pivotal rename - 'Cucumber was archived. The new alliance name is called Smtn else' - along with Gang of Fools' betrayal and the accession of [[Paladins United]], [[The Simple Ones]] and TerraLune to what became [[smtn elf]]{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol6|vol. 6, 12 Oct 2022}}; vols. 4 and 5 (Jul–Aug 2022) carry the guild's season placings and territory claim and the Adonis shared server{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol4|vol. 4, 24 Jul 2022}}{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol5|vol. 5, 27 Aug 2022}}; vol. 9 (25 Mar 2023) records busted moments joining mid-season and Nefarious Ravens leaving 'on account of the guild disbanding'{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol9|vol. 9, 25 Mar 2023}}; vols. 12-13 (Feb-Mar 2024) record Adonis as still active{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol12|vol. 12, 20 Feb 2024}}{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol13|vol. 13, 22 Mar 2024}}.

After that the newsletter turns inward. Vols. 14-21 (2024-2026) cover guild events, the Spirit and Brilliance cabinets, dungeon and lore criticism, and ANO's internal Ocean Trials war rankings, but name no alliance at all{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol17|vol. 17, 15 Jan 2025}}{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol21|vol. 21, 18 May 2026}} - a silence that matches [[private-diplomacy-era|the private diplomacy era]]. What they do preserve is ANO's own record: the guild reaching level 105 in mid-2024 (vol. 15){{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol15|vol. 15, 5 Aug 2024}}, its season placings, and, in vol. 20 (23 Nov 2025), an interview with guild leader Calluum that is the only public account of ANO's leadership succession{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol20|vol. 20, 23 Nov 2025}}.

The newsletter's ecosystem also left machine traces: [[Titans Valor]]'s Discord bot (github.com/titantimes/valor) consumed a shared ANO/AVO alliance-claims feed between April and December 2022{{cite:github-com-titantimes-valor|repository commits, Apr-Dec 2022}}. The bot was not the work of [[motoki317]], who wrote moto-bot (github.com/motoki317/moto-bot), a separate Java Wynncraft utility bot with its own player-tracking commands, archived read-only on 27 January 2024{{cite:github-com-motoki317-moto-bot|repository page}}. Nothing links motoki317 to Titans Valor{{cite:chronicle-records|addendum 2; the motoki317 correction}}.

![Output of the '-guild' command from Titans Valor's Discord bot Valor, reproduced in Titan Times vol. 13 (22 March 2024): a guild overview giving level 103, 109 members, 31 territories and a war count of 60,937, above a table of the members online and their worlds.](/images/chronicles/media/titan-times-59a7fc93.webp){{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol13|vol. 13, 22 Mar 2024}}

Its newsletter, the Titan Times, is the principal written source for alliance history from 2022 onward.
